Each store holds the bus for 100 ns, and a module is busy for 600 ns. With 8 modules used in turn, a module is reused only after 8 [latex]\times[/latex] 100 = 800 ns [latex]\gt[/latex] 600 ns, so modules never cause waiting.

The bus is the bottleneck: one store per 100 ns.

[latex]\frac{1\,ms}{100\,ns}=\frac{10^{-3}}{10^{-7}}=10^4[/latex]

Answer: 10000

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate phrase from the options given below to complete the following sentence.

India is a post-colonial country because
options: it was a former British colony
Indian Information Technology professionals have colonized the world
India does not follow any colonial practices
India has helped other countries gain freedom
questions.solution:
"Post-colonial" describes a country after colonial rule has ended. India is post-colonial because it was earlier a British colony.

Answer: it was a former British colony

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Who ___________ was coming to see us this evening?
questions.solution:
Direct question: "Who did you say was coming to see us this evening?" "Did you say" is the question form, and "that" cannot follow when "who" is the subject of the clause.

Answer: did you say

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Match the columns.

[latex]\begin{array}{ll|ll}\hline &\textbf{Column 1} & & \textbf{Column 2 } \\\hline 1.& \text{eradicate} &P. &\text{misrepresent}\\\hline 2.&\text{distort} &Q.& \text{soak completely}\\\hline 3.&\text{saturate} &R.& \text{use}\\\hline 4.&\text{utilize} &S.& \text{destroy utterly}\\\hline \end{array}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- eradicate = destroy utterly (S)
- distort = misrepresent (P)
- saturate = soak completely (Q)
- utilize = use (R)

Answer: 1:S, 2:P, 3:Q, 4:R

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: What is the average of all multiples of 10 from 2 to 198?
questions.solution:
Multiples of 10 between 2 and 198: 10, 20, ..., 190 (an AP).

Average = [latex]\frac{10+190}{2}=100[/latex]

Answer: 100

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: The value of [latex]\sqrt{12+\sqrt{12+\sqrt{12+\dots}}}[/latex] is
questions.solution:
Let [latex]x=\sqrt{12+x}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]x^2-x-12=0[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (x [latex]-[/latex] 4)(x + 3) = 0.

x must be positive, so x = 4.

Answer: 4

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: The old city of Koenigsberg, which had a German majority population before World War 2, is now called Kaliningrad. After the events of the war, Kaliningrad is now a Russian territory and has a predominantly Russian population. It is bordered by the Baltic Sea on the north and the countries of Poland to the south and west and Lithuania to the east respectively. Which of the statements below can be inferred from this passage?
options: Kaliningrad was historically Russian in its ethnic make up
Kaliningrad is a part of Russia despite it not being contiguous with the rest of Russia
Koenigsberg was renamed Kaliningrad, as that was its original Russian name
Poland and Lithuania are on the route from Kaliningrad to the rest of Russia
questions.solution:
Kaliningrad is Russian territory, but it is bordered by the Baltic Sea, Poland and Lithuania, so it does not touch the rest of Russia.

The passage says nothing about its original name or historic ethnicity, or about the travel route.

Answer: Kaliningrad is a part of Russia despite it not being contiguous with the rest of Russia

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Number of people diagnosed with dengue fever (contracted from the bite of a mosquito) in North India is twice the number diagnosed last year. Municipal authorities have concluded that measures to control the mosquito population have failed in this region.

Which one of the following statements, if true, does not contradict this conclusion?
options: A high proportion of the affected population has returned from neighbouring countries where dengue is prevalent
More cases of dengue are now reported because of an increase in the Municipal Office's administrative efficiency
Many more cases of dengue are being diagnosed this year since the introduction of a new and effective diagnostic test
The number of people with malarial fever (also contracted from mosquito bites) has increased this year
questions.solution:
Options 1, 2, 3 give other reasons for more dengue cases (imported cases, better reporting, better diagnosis), so they weaken the conclusion.

More malaria (also mosquito-borne) supports that mosquito control failed, so it does not contradict it.

Answer: The number of people with malarial fever has increased this year

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: If [latex]x[/latex] is real and [latex]|x^2-2x+3|=11[/latex], then possible values of [latex]|-x^3+x^2-x|[/latex] include
questions.solution:
[latex]x^2-2x+3=(x-1)^2+2\gt0[/latex], so [latex]x^2-2x+3=11\Rightarrow x^2-2x-8=0\Rightarrow x=4[/latex] or [latex]x=-2[/latex].

- x = 4: [latex]|-64+16-4|=52[/latex]
- x = [latex]-[/latex]2: [latex]|8+4+2|=14[/latex]

Answer: 14, 52

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: The ratio of male to female students in a college for five years is plotted in the following line graph. If the number of female students doubled in 2009, by what percent did the number of male students increase in 2009?
questions.solution:
From the graph: ratio in 2008 = 2.5, in 2009 = 3.

Let females in 2008 = F [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] males = 2.5F. In 2009 females = 2F [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] males = 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 2F = 6F.

Increase = [latex]\frac{6F-2.5F}{2.5F}\times100=140\%[/latex]

Answer: 140

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: At what time between 6 a. m. and 7 a. m. will the minute hand and hour hand of a clock make an angle closest to [latex]60^{\circ}[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Angle at 6:m = [latex]|180-5.5m|[/latex].

Setting it to 60: 5.5m = 120 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] m = 21.8 minutes.

At 6:22 the angle is 180 [latex]-[/latex] 121 = 59[latex]^\circ[/latex], the closest among the options.

Answer: 6:22 a.m.

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
P: Good mobile phones are not cheap
Q: Cheap mobile phones are not good

L: P implies Q
M: Q implies P
N: P is equivalent to Q
Which one of the following about L, M, and N is CORRECT?
options: L, M and N are TRUE.
questions.solution:
Let G = good, C = cheap.
- P: [latex]G\rightarrow\neg C[/latex]
- Q: [latex]C\rightarrow\neg G[/latex]

Q is the contrapositive of P, so P [latex]\equiv[/latex] Q. Hence P implies Q, Q implies P, and P is equivalent to Q.

Answer: L, M and N are TRUE

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let x and Y be finite sets and f:x[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Y be a function. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: For any subsets A and B of x, |f(A[latex]\cup[/latex]B)|=|f(A)|+|f(B)|
For any subsets A and B of x, f(A[latex]\cap[/latex]B) =f(A)[latex]\cap[/latex]f(B)
For any subsets A and B of x, |f(A[latex]\cap[/latex]B)| = min{|f (A)| ,|f(B)|}
For any subsets S and T of Y, [latex]f^{-1}(S\cap T)=f^{-1}(S)\cap f^{-1}(T)[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Option 1 fails when f(A) and f(B) overlap.
- Option 2 fails for non-injective f: A = {1}, B = {2}, f(1) = f(2) = y gives [latex]f(A\cap B)=\emptyset[/latex] but [latex]f(A)\cap f(B)=\{y\}[/latex].
- Option 3 fails for the same example.
- Option 4: [latex]x\in f^{-1}(S\cap T)\iff f(x)\in S[/latex] and [latex]f(x)\in T\iff x\in f^{-1}(S)\cap f^{-1}(T)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] always true.

Answer: [latex]f^{-1}(S\cap T)=f^{-1}(S)\cap f^{-1}(T)[/latex]

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let G be a group with 15 elements. Let L be a subgroup of G. It is known that L[latex]\neq[/latex]G and that the size of L is at least 4. The size of L is _______.
questions.solution:
By Lagrange's theorem, |L| divides 15, so |L| is 1, 3, 5 or 15.

L [latex]\ne[/latex] G rules out 15, and [latex]|L|\ge4[/latex] rules out 1 and 3.

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Which one of the following statements is TRUE about every n x n matrix with only real
eigenvalues?
options: If the trace of the matrix is positive and the determinant of the matrix is negative, at least one of its eigenvalues is negative.
If the trace of the matrix is positive, all its eigenvalues are positive.
If the determinant of the matrix is positive, all its eigenvalues are positive.
If the product of the trace and determinant of the matrix is positive, all its eigenvalues are positive.
questions.solution:
Trace = sum of eigenvalues, determinant = product of eigenvalues.

- If det [latex]\lt[/latex] 0, the product is negative, so at least one eigenvalue is negative [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] option 1 true.
- Counter-examples for others: eigenvalues 3, [latex]-[/latex]1 (trace [latex]\gt[/latex] 0); [latex]-[/latex]1, [latex]-[/latex]2 (det [latex]\gt[/latex] 0); [latex]-[/latex]1, [latex]-[/latex]1, 5 (trace and det both positive).

Answer: If trace is positive and determinant is negative, at least one eigenvalue is negative

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: If V1 and V2 are 4-dimensional subspaces of a 6-dimensional vector space V, then the smallest possible dimension of  V1[latex]\cap[/latex]V2 is _______.
questions.solution:
[latex]\dim(V_1\cap V_2)=\dim V_1+\dim V_2-\dim(V_1+V_2)\ge4+4-6=2[/latex]

Answer: 2

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: If [latex]\int_{0}^{2\pi}|x sinx| dx=k \pi[/latex], then the value of k is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
On [latex][0,\pi][/latex], [latex]x\sin x\ge0[/latex]; on [latex][\pi,2\pi][/latex], [latex]x\sin x\le0[/latex]. Antiderivative of [latex]x\sin x[/latex] is [latex]\sin x-x\cos x[/latex].

- [latex]\int_0^{\pi}x\sin x\,dx=\pi[/latex]
- [latex]-\int_{\pi}^{2\pi}x\sin x\,dx=-[(0-2\pi)-(0+\pi)]=3\pi[/latex]

Total = [latex]4\pi[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] k = 4

Answer: 4

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
Consider the following minterm expression for F.
F(P,Q,R,S) = [latex]\Sigma[/latex] 0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15
The minterms 2, 7, 8 and 13 are 'do not care terms. The minimal sum of-products form for F is
questions.solution:
Minterms 0, 5, 10, 15 with don't cares 2, 7, 8, 13.

- [latex]\bar Q\bar S[/latex] = {0, 2, 8, 10} covers 0, 10
- [latex]QS[/latex] = {5, 7, 13, 15} covers 5, 15

[latex]F=\bar Q\bar S+QS[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\bar Q\bar S+QS[/latex]

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.solution:
y = a when x = 1, else y = b. This selects one of two inputs using x as the select line, i.e. a 2-to-1 multiplexer.

Answer: Multiplexor

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
Consider the following processors (ns stands for nanoseconds). Assume that the pipeline registers have zero latency.
P1: Four-stage pipeline with stage latencies 1 ns, 2 ns, 2 ns, 1 ns.
P2: Four-stage pipeline with stage latencies 1 ns, 1.5 ns, 1.5 ns, 1.5 ns.
P3: Five-stage pipeline with stage latencies 0.5 ns, 1 ns, 1 ns, 0.6 ns, 1 ns.
P4: Five-stage pipeline with stage latencies 0.5 ns, 0.5 ns, 1 ns, 1 ns, 1.1 ns.
Which processor has the highest peak clock frequency?
questions.solution:
Clock period = largest stage latency.

- P1: 2 ns [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0.5 GHz
- P2: 1.5 ns [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0.67 GHz
- P3: 1 ns [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1 GHz
- P4: 1.1 ns [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0.91 GHz

Answer: P3

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
options: Adding 100 to the upper diagonal elements and subtracting 100 from lower diagonal elements of A
questions.solution:
Each iteration simply swaps A[i][j] and A[j][i] (Temp [latex]-[/latex] C gives back the old A[i][j]).

Both loops run over all (i, j), so every off-diagonal pair is swapped twice: once at (i, j) and once at (j, i). Two swaps cancel, so A is unchanged.

Answer: The matrix A itself

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text:
The minimum number of arithmetic operations required to evaluate the polynomial
[latex]P(x)=x^{5}+4x^{3}+6x+5[/latex] for a given value of x, using only one temporary variable is _____.
questions.solution:
Write [latex]P(x)=((x^2+4)\cdot x\cdot x+6)\cdot x+5[/latex]:

- t = x * x
- t = t + 4
- t = t * x
- t = t * x ([latex]x^4+4x^2[/latex])
- t = t + 6
- t = t * x ([latex]x^5+4x^3+6x[/latex])
- t = t + 5

7 operations with one temporary.

Answer: 7

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
Consider the following rooted tree with the vertex labelled P as the root

The order in which the nodes are visited during an in-order traversal of the tree is
questions.solution:
In-order for a general tree: in-order of the first child, then the node, then in-order of the remaining children.

- P: (Q-subtree) P (R-subtree)
- Q-subtree: S Q
- R-subtree: T R (U-subtree) V, with U-subtree = W U

Order: S Q P T R W U V

Answer: SQPTRWUV

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Suppose depth first search is executed on the graph below starting at some unknown vertex. Assume that a recursive call to visit a vertex is made only after first checking that the vertex has not been visited earlier. Then the maximum possible recursion depth (including the initial call) is _________.
questions.solution:
Max recursion depth = number of vertices on the longest simple path DFS can follow.

- Left 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 grid: a snake path covers all 9 vertices, ending at its bottom-right corner.
- Bottom middle vertex: 1 (its pendant above is a dead end, so skip it).
- Right 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 grid: enter at the bottom-left corner; we must end at the middle-right vertex to reach the pendant. A grid is bipartite (5 corner-coloured, 4 other), so a corner-to-middle path can cover only 8 vertices.
- Right pendant: 1

Depth = 9 + 1 + 8 + 1 = 19

Answer: 19

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: You have an array of n elements. Suppose you implement quick sort by always choosing the central element of the array as the pivot. Then the tightest upper bound for the worst case performance is
questions.solution:
Choosing the middle element is still a fixed rule. An adversary can arrange the input so the middle element is always the smallest or largest, giving partitions of size n[latex]-[/latex]1 and 0 every time.

[latex]T(n)=T(n-1)+O(n)=O(n^2)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]O(n^2)[/latex]

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
The length of the shortest string NOT in the language (over [latex]\Sigma[/latex]={a,b}) of the following regular expression is _________.
a*b* (ba)* a*
questions.solution:
All strings of length 0, 1, 2 are generated: [latex]\epsilon[/latex], a, b, aa, ab, bb (from a*b*), ba (from (ba)*).

"bab": after the leading b's we need "ab", but "ab" cannot come from (ba)*a*. So bab is not in the language.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text: Let [latex]\Sigma[/latex] be a finite non-empty alphabet and let [latex]2^{\Sigma^{*}}[/latex] be the power set of [latex]\Sigma^{*}[/latex] . Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
[latex]\Sigma^*[/latex] can be listed in order of length (then dictionary order), so it is countably infinite.

[latex]2^{\Sigma^*}[/latex] is the power set of a countably infinite set, which is uncountable (Cantor's theorem).

Answer: [latex]2^{\Sigma^*}[/latex] is uncountable and [latex]\Sigma^*[/latex] is countable

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text: One of the purposes of using intermediate code in compilers is to
options: make parsing and semantic analysis simpler
improve error recovery and error reporting
increase the chances of reusing the machine-independent code optimizer in other compliers.
questions.solution:
Intermediate code is machine independent. The same optimizer (and front end) can be reused with different back ends for different machines.

Answer: increase the chances of reusing the machine-independent code optimizer in other compilers

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?
1) Static allocation of all data areas by a compiler makes it impossible to implement recursion.
2) Automatic garbage collection is essential to implement recursion.
3) Dynamic allocation of activation records is essential to implement recursion.
4) Both heap and stack are essential to implement recursion.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- 1: With static allocation each function has one fixed data area, so recursive calls overwrite it [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- 2: Garbage collection is not needed for recursion [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False.
- 3: Each call needs its own activation record created at run time [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- 4: A stack alone is enough; a heap is not needed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False.

Answer: 1 and 3 only

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.text: In the context of modular software design, which one of the following combinations is desirable?
questions.solution:
Good modules do one job well (high cohesion) and depend little on other modules (low coupling).

Answer: High cohesion and low coupling

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
A system uses 3 page frames for storing process pages in main memory. It uses the Least Recently Used (LRU) page replacement policy. Assume that all the page frames are initially empty. What is the total number of page faults that will occur while processing the page reference string given below?
4, 7, 6, 1, 7, 6, 1, 2, 7, 2
questions.solution:
LRU with 3 frames:

- 4, 7, 6: faults (3)
- 1: fault, evict 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {7, 6, 1} (4)
- 7, 6, 1: hits
- 2: fault, evict LRU 7 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {6, 1, 2} (5)
- 7: fault, evict 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {1, 2, 7} (6)
- 2: hit

Answer: 6

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text: What is the optimized version of the relation algebra expression  [latex]\pi _{A1}(\pi _{A2}(\sigma _{F1}(\sigma_{F2}(r))))[/latex] , where A1, A2 are sets of attributes in r with [latex]A_{1}\subset A_{2}[/latex] and F1, F2 are Boolean expressions based on the attributes in r?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Two selections combine: [latex]\sigma_{F1}(\sigma_{F2}(r))=\sigma_{F1\wedge F2}(r)[/latex]
- Since [latex]A_1\subset A_2[/latex], [latex]\pi_{A1}(\pi_{A2}(\cdot))=\pi_{A1}(\cdot)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\pi_{A1}(\sigma_{F1\wedge F2}(r))[/latex]

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text: A prime attribute of a relation scheme R is an attribute that appears
options: in all candidate keys of R.
in some candidate key of R.
in a foreign keys of R
only in the primary key of R.
questions.solution:
A prime attribute is one that belongs to at least one candidate key.

Answer: in some candidate key of R

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
In the following pairs of OSI protocol layer/sub-layer and its functionality, the
INCORRECT pair is
options: Data Link Layer and Bit synchronization
Transport layer and End-to-end process communication
Medium Access Control sub-layer and Channel sharing
questions.solution:
Bit synchronization is done by the physical layer. The data link layer handles framing, error control and flow control.

The other pairs are correct.

Answer: Data Link Layer and Bit synchronization

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: A bit-stuffing based framing protocol uses an 8-bit delimiter pattern of 01111110. If the output bit-string after stuffing is 01111100101, then the input bit-string is
questions.solution:
The sender inserts a 0 after every five consecutive 1s. Remove it:

0 11111 0 0101 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0 11111 0101 = 0111110101

Answer: 0111110101

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
Host A (on TCP/IP v4 network A) sends an IP datagram D to host B (also on TCP/IP V4 network B). Assume that no error occurred during the transmission of D. When D reaches B, which of the following IP header field(s) may be different from that of the original datagram D?
(i) TTL
(ii) Checksum
(iii) Fragment Offset
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- TTL is decremented at each router.
- Checksum is recomputed whenever the header changes.
- If a router fragments D, the fragments have new Fragment Offset values.

All three may differ.

Answer: (i), (ii) and (iii)

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
An IP router implementing Classless Inter-domain routing (CIDR) receives a packet with address 131.23.151.76. The router's routing table has the following entries:

The identifier of the output interface on which this packet will be forwarded is _____.
questions.solution:
Address 131.23.151.76, second octet 23 = 00010111.

- 131.16.0.0/12: 16 = 0001 0000 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] first 4 bits 0001 match
- 131.28.0.0/14: 28 = 000111 00 vs 000101 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] no
- 131.19.0.0/16: 19 [latex]\ne[/latex] 23 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] no
- 131.22.0.0/15: 22 = 0001011 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] first 7 bits 0001011 match

Longest prefix match is /15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] interface 1.

Answer: 1

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Every host in an IPv4 network has a 1-second resolution real-time clock with battery backup. Each host needs to generate up to 1000 unique identifiers per second. Assume that each host has a globally unique IPv4 address. Design a 50-bit globally unique ID for this purpose. After what period (in seconds) will the identifiers generated by a host wrap around?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- IPv4 address (global uniqueness): 32 bits
- Up to 1000 IDs per second: 10 bits ([latex]2^{10}=1024[/latex])
- Remaining for the clock: 50 [latex]-[/latex] 32 [latex]-[/latex] 10 = 8 bits

The clock part repeats after [latex]2^8=256[/latex] seconds.

Answer: 256

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: An IP router with a Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) of 1500 bytes has received an IP packet of size 4404 bytes with an IP header of length 20 bytes. The values of the relevant fields in the header of the third IP fragment generated by the router for this packet are
questions.solution:
Data = 4404 [latex]-[/latex] 20 = 4384 B. Max data per fragment = 1480 B (multiple of 8).

- Fragment 1: 1480 B, offset 0
- Fragment 2: 1480 B, offset 185
- Fragment 3: 4384 [latex]-[/latex] 2960 = 1424 B, offset 2960 / 8 = 370, last fragment so MF = 0

Datagram length = 1424 + 20 = 1444

Answer: MF bit: 0, Datagram Length: 1444, Offset: 370

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the transactions T1, T2, and T3 and the schedules S1 and S2 given below.
T1 : r1(x); r1(Z) ; w1(x); w1(Z)
T2 : r2(x); r2(Z); w2(Z)
T3 : r3(x); r3(x); w3(Y)

S1: r1(x); r3(Y); r3(x); r2(Y); r2(Z); w3(Y); w2(Z); r1(Z); w1(x); w1(Z)
S2: r1(x); r3(Y); r2(Y); r3(x); r1(Z); r2(Z); w3(Y); w1(x); w2(Z); w1(Z)
Which one of the following statements about the schedules is TRUE?
options: Both S1 and S2 are conflict-serializable
Neither S1 nor S2 is conflict-serializable
questions.solution:
S1: r2(Y) before w3(Y): T2[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T3; r3(x) before w1(x): T3[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T1; r2(Z), w2(Z) before r1(Z), w1(Z): T2[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T1. No cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] serializable (T2, T3, T1).

S2: r1(Z) before w2(Z): T1[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T2; r2(Z) before w1(Z): T2[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T1. Cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not serializable.

Answer: Only S1 is conflict-serializable

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the relational schema given below, where eId of the relation dependentis a foreign key referring to empId of the relation employee. Assume that every employee has at least one associated dependent in the dependent relation.

The above query evaluates to the set of empIds of employees whose age is greater than that of
questions.solution:
The join keeps employees who have some own dependent with age [latex]\ge[/latex] the employee's age (eId = empId).

Subtracting them from all employees leaves those whose age is greater than every one of their own dependents.

Answer: all of his/her dependents

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: A system contains three programs and each requires three tape units for its operation. The minimum number of tape units which the system must have such that deadlocks never arise is _________.
questions.solution:
Worst case: each program holds 2 tapes and waits for a third. That uses 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 6 tapes with deadlock.

One more tape lets one program finish and release its tapes: 6 + 1 = 7.

Answer: 7

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
An operating system uses shortest remaining time first scheduling algorithm for pre-emptive scheduling of processes. Consider the following set of processes with their arrival times and CPU burst times (in milliseconds):

The average waiting time (in milliseconds) of the processes is _________.
questions.solution:
SRTF schedule:
- 0-2 P1 (rem 10)
- 2-6 P2 (P3 arriving at 3 needs 6, more than P2's remaining)
- 6-12 P3 (P4 arriving at 8 needs 5, more than P3's remaining 4)
- 12-17 P4, 17-27 P1

Waiting = completion [latex]-[/latex] arrival [latex]-[/latex] burst:
P1 = 27 [latex]-[/latex] 0 [latex]-[/latex] 12 = 15, P2 = 0, P3 = 12 [latex]-[/latex] 3 [latex]-[/latex] 6 = 3, P4 = 17 [latex]-[/latex] 8 [latex]-[/latex] 5 = 4

Average = 22 / 4 = 5.5

Answer: 5.5

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: Consider a paging hardware with a TLB. Assume that the entire page table and all the pages are in the physical memory. It takes 10 milliseconds to search the TLB and 80 milliseconds to access the physical memory. If the TLB hit ratio is 0.6, the effective memory access time (in milliseconds) is _________.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- TLB hit: 10 + 80 = 90
- TLB miss: 10 + 80 (page table) + 80 (data) = 170

EMAT = 0.6 [latex]\times[/latex] 90 + 0.4 [latex]\times[/latex] 170 = 54 + 68 = 122

Answer: 122

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text:
Consider the basic block given below.
a= b + c
c =a + d
d =b + c
e =d - b
a =e + b
The minimum number of nodes and edges present in the DAG representation of the above basic block respectively are
questions.solution:
Simplify using values:
- d = b + c, e = d [latex]-[/latex] b = c (the new c), a = e + b = c + b = d

So e shares the node of c, and the last a shares the node of d.

- Leaves: b, c0, d0 (3 nodes)
- n1 = b + c0 (a), n2 = n1 + d0 (c, e), n3 = b + n2 (d, a) (3 nodes, 2 edges each)

Nodes = 6, edges = 6

Answer: 6 and 6

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text: Which one of the following problems is undecidable?
options: Deciding if a given context-free grammar is ambiguous
Deciding if a given string is generated by a given context-free grammar
Deciding if the language generated by a given context-free grammar is empty
Deciding if the language generated by a given context-free grammar is finite.
questions.solution:
Membership (CYK), emptiness and finiteness of CFLs are all decidable.

Ambiguity of a CFG is undecidable (reduction from Post Correspondence Problem).

Answer: Deciding if a given context-free grammar is ambiguous

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the following languages over the alphabet [latex]\sum =\{0,1,c\}: [/latex]
[latex]L_{1}=\{0^{n}|1^{n}|n\geq 0\}[/latex]
[latex]L_{2}=\{wcw^{r}|w\in \{0,1\}^{*}\}[/latex]
[latex] L_{3}=\{ww^{r}|w\in \{0,1\}^{*}\}[/latex]
Here [latex]w^{r}[/latex] is the reverse of the string w. Which of these languages are deterministic Contextfree languages?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1=\{0^n1^n\}[/latex]: push 0s, pop on 1s [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] DCFL.
- [latex]L_2=\{wcw^r\}[/latex]: c marks the middle, so the PDA knows when to start popping [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] DCFL.
- [latex]L_3=\{ww^r\}[/latex]: the middle must be guessed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL but not DCFL.

Answer: Only L1 and L2

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Suppose you want to move from 0 to 100 on the number line. In each step, you either move right by a unit distance or you take a shortcut. A shortcut is simply a pre-specified pair of integers i,j with [latex]i \lt j[/latex]. Given a shortcut i, j if you are at position i on the number line, you may directly move to j. Suppose T(k) denotes the smallest number of steps needed to move from k to 100. suppose further that there is at most 1 shortcut involving any number, and in particular from 9 there is a shortcut to 15. Let y and z be such that T(9) = 1 + min(T(y), T(z)). Then the value of the product yz is_______.
questions.solution:
From 9 you can either step right to 10 or take the shortcut to 15.

[latex]T(9)=1+\min(T(10),T(15))[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] y, z = 10, 15

yz = 150

Answer: 150

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Consider the decision problem 2CNFSAT defined as follows:
{ [latex]\phi[/latex] | [latex]\phi[/latex] is a satisfiable propositional formula in CNF with at most two literal per clause}
For example, [latex]\phi =(x_{1} \vee x_{2}) \wedge (x_{1} \vee \bar{x_{3}}) \wedge (x_{2} \vee x_{4})[/latex] is a Boolean formula and it is in 2CNFSAT.
The decision problem 2CNFSAT is
options: solvable in polynomial time by reduction to directed graph reachability.
solvable in constant time since any input instance is satisfiable
questions.solution:
Each clause [latex](a\vee b)[/latex] gives implications [latex] eg a ightarrow b[/latex] and [latex] eg b ightarrow a[/latex]. The formula is unsatisfiable iff some x reaches [latex] eg x[/latex] and [latex] eg x[/latex] reaches x in this implication graph.

So 2-SAT is solved in polynomial (linear) time by graph reachability.

Answer: solvable in polynomial time by reduction to directed graph reachability

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: Suppose we have a balanced binary search tree T holding n numbers. We are given two numbers L and H and wish to sum up all the numbers in T that lie between L and H. Suppose there are m such numbers in T. If the tightest upper bound on the time to compute the sum is [latex]O(n^{a}log^{b}n+m^{c}log^{d}n)[/latex], the value of a + 10b + 100c + 1000d is _______.
questions.solution:
Find L in the balanced BST in [latex]O(\log n)[/latex], then walk in-order through the m values up to H in O(m).

Time = [latex]O(\log n+m)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a = 0, b = 1, c = 1, d = 0

a + 10b + 100c + 1000d = 0 + 10 + 100 + 0 = 110

Answer: 110

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Consider a hash table with 100 slots. Collisions are resolved using chaining. Assuming
simple uniform hashing, what is the probability that the first 3 slots are unfilled after the first 3 insertions?
questions.solution:
With chaining, each key independently goes to any of the 100 slots. The chance it avoids the first 3 slots is 97/100.

For 3 insertions: [latex]\frac{97\times97\times97}{100^3}[/latex]

Answer: (97 [latex]\times[/latex] 97 [latex]\times[/latex] 97) / [latex]100^3[/latex]

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
options: number of internal nodes in the tree
number of nodes without a right sibling in the tree.
number of leaf nodes in the tree.
questions.solution:
For each node, a node with no child contributes 1; otherwise its count comes from its children. Then the count for the right siblings is added.

So only nodes without children (leaves) are counted.

Answer: number of leaf nodes in the tree

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
options: It will run into an infinite loop when x is not in listA
It is an implementation of binary search
It will always find the maximum element in listA.
It will return ? 1 even when x is present in listA.
questions.solution:
k is the middle of [i, j]. If x [latex]\lt[/latex] A[k] search the left half; if x [latex]\gt[/latex] A[k] search the right half; if equal both updates make i [latex]\gt[/latex] j and the loop stops with A[k] = x.

This is binary search: it returns k when found and [latex]-[/latex]1 otherwise, and always terminates.

Answer: It is an implementation of binary search

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: An instruction pipeline has five stages, namely, instruction fetch (IF), instruction decode and register fetch (ID/RF), instruction execution (Ex), memory access (MEM), and register write back (WB) with stage latencies 1 ns, 2.2 ns, 2 ns, 1 ns, and 0.75 ns, respectively (ns stands for nanoseconds). To gain in terms of frequency, the designers have decided to split the ID/RF stage into three stages (ID, RF1, RF2) each of latency 2.2/3 ns. Also, the Ex stage is split into two stages (Ex1, Ex2) each of latency 1 ns. The new design has a total of eight pipeline stages. A program has 20% branch instructions which execute in the Ex stage and produce the next instruction pointer at the end of the Ex stage in the old design and at the end of the Ex2 stage in the new design. The IF stage stalls after fetching a branch instruction until the next instruction pointer is computed. All instructions other than the branch instruction have an average CPI of one in both the designs. The execution times of this program on the old and the new design are P and Q nanoseconds, respectively. The value of P/Q is __________
questions.solution:
Old design: clock = 2.2 ns. Branch resolved at end of stage 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 stall cycles.
CPI = 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 + 0.2 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 = 1.4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P = 1.4 [latex]\times[/latex] 2.2 = 3.08 ns per instruction

New design: clock = 1 ns. Branch resolved at end of Ex2 = stage 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 stall cycles.
CPI = 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 + 0.2 [latex]\times[/latex] 6 = 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q = 2 ns per instruction

P/Q = 3.08 / 2 = 1.54

Answer: 1.54

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
The memory access time is 1 nanosecond for a read operation with a hit in cache, 5
nanoseconds for a read operation with a miss in cache, 2 nanoseconds for a write operation
with a hit in cache and 10 nanoseconds for a write operation with a miss in cache. Execution
of a sequence of instructions involves 100 instruction fetch operations, 60 memory operand
read operations and 40 memory operand write operations. The cache hit-ratio is 0.9. The
average memory access time (in nanoseconds) in executing the sequence of instructions is
__________.
questions.solution:
Reads = 100 fetches + 60 operands = 160, writes = 40.

- Avg read = 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 + 0.1 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 1.4 ns
- Avg write = 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 + 0.1 [latex]\times[/latex] 10 = 2.8 ns

Average = [latex]\frac{160\times1.4+40\times2.8}{200}=\frac{224+112}{200}=1.68[/latex]

Answer: 1.68

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: The above synchronous sequential circuit built using JK flip-flops is initialized with [latex]Q_{2}Q_{1}Q_{0}[/latex] = 000. The state sequence for this circuit for the next 3 clock cycles is
questions.solution:
From the circuit: [latex]J_2=\bar Q_1, K_2=Q_0[/latex]; [latex]J_1=Q_2, K_1=\bar Q_2[/latex]; [latex]J_0=Q_1, K_0=\bar Q_0[/latex].

- 000: J2K2 = 10 (set), J1K1 = 01 (reset), J0K0 = 01 (reset) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 100
- 100: J2K2 = 10, J1K1 = 10 (set), J0K0 = 01 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 110
- 110: J2K2 = 00 (hold 1), J1K1 = 10, J0K0 = 11 (toggle) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 111

Answer: 100, 110, 111

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
With respect to the numerical evaluation of the definite integral,[latex]K=\int_{a}^{b}x^{2}dx[/latex] , where a and b are given, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
(I) The value of K obtained using the trapezoidal rule is always greater than or equal to the exact value of the definite integral.
(II) The value of K obtained using the Simpson's rule is always equal to the exact value of the definite integral.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: [latex]x^2[/latex] is convex, so the chord (trapezoid) lies above the curve [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] trapezoidal value [latex]\ge[/latex] exact [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- II: Simpson's rule is exact for polynomials up to degree 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
The value of the integral given below is
[latex]\int_{0}^{\pi }x^{2}cosxdx[/latex]
questions.solution:
Integrate by parts: [latex]\int x^2\cos x\,dx=x^2\sin x+2x\cos x-2\sin x[/latex]

From 0 to [latex]\pi[/latex]: [latex](0+2\pi(-1)-0)-0=-2\pi[/latex]

Answer: [latex]-2\pi[/latex]

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let S be a sample space and two mutually exclusive events A and B be such that A[latex]\cup[/latex]B = S. If P(.) denotes the probability of the event, the maximum value of P(A)P(B) is ______
questions.solution:
Mutually exclusive and union = S, so P(A) + P(B) = 1.

P(A)(1 [latex]-[/latex] P(A)) is maximum at P(A) = 0.5, giving 0.5 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.5 = 0.25.

Answer: 0.25

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider the set of all functions f:{0,1,...,2014}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{0,1...,2014} such that f(f(i))=i, for 0[latex]\leq[/latex]i[latex]\leq[/latex]2014 . Consider the following statements.
P. For each such function it must be the case that for every i, f(i) = i,
Q. For each such function it must be the case that for some i,f(i) = i,
R. Each such function must be onto.
Which one of the following is CORRECT?
options: P, Q and R are true
Only Q and R are true
Only P and Q are true
questions.solution:
f(f(i)) = i means f is its own inverse, so f is a bijection [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R true.

- P false: f can swap pairs, e.g. f(0) = 1, f(1) = 0.
- Q true: f splits the 2015 elements into fixed points and swapped pairs. 2015 is odd, so at least one fixed point exists.

Answer: Only Q and R are true

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
There are two elements x,y in a group (G,*) such that every element in the group can be written as a product of some number of x's and y's in some order. It is known that
x * x = y * y = x * y *x * y = y* x * y *x = e
where e is the identity element. The maximum number of elements in such a group is _______.
questions.solution:
[latex]x^2=y^2=e[/latex] and [latex](xy)^2=e[/latex] give [latex]xy=(xy)^{-1}=y^{-1}x^{-1}=yx[/latex], so x and y commute.

Every product then reduces to one of e, x, y, xy (the Klein four-group).

Answer: 4

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: If G is a forest with n vertices and k connected components, how many edges does G have?
questions.solution:
Each tree with [latex]n_i[/latex] vertices has [latex]n_i-1[/latex] edges. Summing over k trees: [latex]\sum(n_i-1)=n-k[/latex].

Answer: n [latex]-[/latex] k

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let [latex]\delta[/latex] denote the minimum degree of a vertex in a graph. For all planar graphs on n vertices with [latex]\delta \geq 3[/latex], which one of the following is TRUE?
options: In any planar embedding, the number of faces is at least [latex]\frac{n}{2}+2[/latex]
In any planar embedding, the number of faces is less than [latex]\frac{n}{2}+2[/latex]
There is a planar embedding in which the number of faces is less than [latex]\frac{n}{2}+2[/latex]
There is a planar embedding in which the number of faces is at most [latex]\frac{n}{\delta +1}[/latex]
questions.solution:
[latex]\delta\ge3\Rightarrow 2e=\sum\deg\ge3n\Rightarrow e\ge\frac{3n}{2}[/latex]

Euler: [latex]f=e-n+2\ge\frac{3n}{2}-n+2=\frac n2+2[/latex], for every planar embedding.

Answer: In any planar embedding, the number of faces is at least [latex]\frac n2+2[/latex]

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: The CORECT formula for the sentence, "not all rainy days are cold" is
questions.solution:
"Not all rainy days are cold" = there is a rainy day that is not cold.

[latex]\neg\forall d(Rainy(d)\rightarrow Cold(d))\equiv\exists d(Rainy(d)\wedge\sim Cold(d))[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\exists d(Rainy(d)\wedge\sim Cold(d))[/latex]

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the following relational schema:
Employee (empId, empName, empDept )
Customer (custId,custName, salesRepId, rating)
SalesRepId is a foreign key referring to empId of the employee relation. Assume that each employee makes a sale to at least one customer. What does the following query return?
SELECT empName 
FROM employee E 
 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT custId
FROM customer C
WHERE C. salesRepId = E. empId
AND C. rating < > 'GOOD')
options: Names of all the employees with at least one of their customers having a 'GOOD' rating
Names of all the employees with at most one of their customers having a 'GOOD' rating.
Names of all the employees with none of their customers having a 'GOOD' rating.
Names of all the employees with all their customers having a 'GOOD' rating.
questions.solution:
The subquery finds this employee's customers whose rating is not 'GOOD'. NOT EXISTS keeps the employee only if there are none.

Since every employee has at least one customer, this means all of the employee's customers are rated 'GOOD'.

Answer: Names of all the employees with all their customers having a 'GOOD' rating

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
Let [latex]\oplus[/latex] denote the Exclusive OR (XOR) operation. Let '1' and '0' denote the binary constants. Consider the following Boolean Algebra for F over two variables P and Q.
[latex]F(P,Q)=((1\oplus P)\oplus (P\oplus Q)) \oplus ((P\oplus Q) \oplus (Q\oplus 0))[/latex]
The equivalent expression for F is
questions.solution:
XOR is associative and [latex]a\oplus a=0[/latex]:

[latex]F=1\oplus P\oplus P\oplus Q\oplus P\oplus Q\oplus Q\oplus0=1\oplus P\oplus Q=\overline{P\oplus Q}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\overline{P\oplus Q}[/latex]

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
[latex]\underset{\text{I}}{\underline{\text{While trying to collect}}}[/latex] an envelope [latex]\underset{\text{II}}{\underline{\text{from under the table}}}[/latex],
[latex]\underset{\text{III}}{\underline{\text{Mr. X fell down}}}[/latex] and [latex]\underset{\text{IV}}{\underline{\text{was losing consciousness}}}[/latex].

Which one of the above underlined parts of the sentence is NOT appropriate?
questions.solution:
Falling down is a completed event, so it should be "lost consciousness". "Was losing consciousness" (continuous) does not fit.

Answer: IV

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: If she _______ how to calibrate the instrument, she ________ done the experiment.
questions.solution:
Third conditional (an unreal past situation): "If + had + past participle, ... could/would have + past participle".

"If she had known how to calibrate the instrument, she could have done the experiment."

Answer: had known, could have

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the word "coherent".
questions.solution:
Coherent = logical and well connected. Rambling = wandering, disconnected (opposite).

Answer: rambling

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Which number does not belong in the series below?

2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50, 64
questions.solution:
The terms are [latex]n^2+1[/latex]: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50, 65.

The last term should be 65, not 64.

Answer: 64

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
The table below has question-wise data on the performance of students in an examination. The marks for each question are also listed. There is no negative or partial marking in the examination.

[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \textbf{Q No.} & \textbf{Marks} &\textbf{Answered}&\textbf{Answered}&\textbf{Not}\\&&\textbf{ Correctly} &\textbf{Wrongly} & \textbf{Attempted} \\\hline \text{1} & \text{2} &\text{21} &\text{17} &\text{6}\\\hline \text{2} & \text{3} &\text{15} & \text{27}& \text{2}\\\hline \text{3} & \text{2} &\text{23} & \text{18} & \text{3}\\\hline \end{array}[/latex]

What is the average of the marks obtained by the class in the examination?
questions.solution:
Marks: Q1 = 21 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 42, Q2 = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 = 45, Q3 = 23 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 46 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] total 133.

Students = 21 + 17 + 6 = 44.

Average = 133 / 44 = 3.02

Answer: 3.02

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: A dance programme is scheduled for 10.00 a.m. Some students are participating in the programme and they need to come an hour earlier than the start of the event. These students should be accompanied by a parent. Other students and parents should come in time for the programme. The instruction you think that is appropriate for this is
options: Students should come at 9.00 a.m. and parents should come at 10.00 a.m.
Participating students should come at 9.00 a.m. accompanied by a parent, and other parents and students should come by 10.00 a.m.
Students who are not participating should come by 10.00 a.m. and they should not bring their parents. Participating students should come at 9.00 a.m.
Participating students should come before 9.00 a.m. Parents who accompany them should come at 9.00 a.m. All others should come at 10.00 a.m.
questions.solution:
Only participating students come at 9 a.m. with a parent; everyone else comes by 10 a.m. Option 2 says exactly this.

Option 1 sends all students at 9; option 3 forbids parents; option 4 has the students before 9.

Answer: Option 2

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
By the beginning of the 20th century, several hypotheses were being proposed, suggesting a paradigm shift in our understanding of the universe. However, the clinching evidence was provided by experimental measurements of the position of a star which was directly behind our sun.

Which of the following inference(s) may be drawn from the above passage?

i. Our understanding of the universe changes based on the positions of stars
ii. Paradigm shifts usually occur at the beginning of centuries
iii. Stars are important objects in the universe
iv. Experimental evidence was important in confirming this paradigm shift
questions.solution:
The passage only says experimental measurement provided the clinching evidence for the paradigm shift.

It does not claim that star positions change our understanding in general, that shifts happen at the start of centuries, or that stars are important objects.

Answer: iv only

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in Rupees grew at 7% during 2012-2013. For international comparison, the GDP is compared in US Dollars (USD) after conversion based on the market exchange rate. During the period 2012-2013 the exchange rate for the USD increased from Rs. 50/USD to Rs.60/ USD. India's GDP in USD during the period 2012-2013
questions.solution:
Let GDP = G rupees. In USD: before = G/50, after = 1.07G/60.

Ratio = [latex]\frac{1.07\times50}{60}=0.892[/latex], a fall of about 11%.

Answer: decreased by 11%

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: The ratio of male to female students in a college for five years is plotted in the following line graph. If the number of female students in 2011 and 2012 is equal, what is the ratio of male students in 2012 to male students in 2011?
questions.solution:
From the graph: male/female in 2011 = 1, in 2012 = 1.5.

With equal females F: males in 2012 : 2011 = 1.5F : F = 1.5 : 1

Answer: 1.5:1

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Consider the equation: [latex](7526)_8 - (Y)_8=(4364)_8[/latex], where [latex](X)_N[/latex] stands for [latex]X[/latex] to the base [latex]N[/latex]. Find [latex]Y[/latex].
questions.solution:
[latex]Y=(7526)_8-(4364)_8[/latex] (subtract in base 8, borrowing 8):

- 6 [latex]-[/latex] 4 = 2
- 2 [latex]-[/latex] 6: borrow, 8 + 2 [latex]-[/latex] 6 = 4
- 4 [latex]-[/latex] 3 = 1
- 7 [latex]-[/latex] 4 = 3

Y = 3142. Check: 4364 + 3142 = 7526 in octal.

Answer: 3142

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: If [latex]g(x)=1-x[/latex] and [latex]h(x)=\frac{x}{x-1}[/latex], then [latex]\frac{g(h(x))}{h(g(x))}[/latex] is:
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]g(h(x))=1-\frac{x}{x-1}=\frac{-1}{x-1}[/latex]
- [latex]h(g(x))=\frac{1-x}{(1-x)-1}=\frac{x-1}{x}[/latex]

[latex]\frac{g(h(x))}{h(g(x))}=\frac{-x}{(x-1)^2}[/latex]

Also [latex]\frac{h(x)}{g(x)}=\frac{x}{(x-1)(1-x)}=\frac{-x}{(x-1)^2}[/latex], the same.

Answer: [latex]\frac{h(x)}{g(x)}[/latex]

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: [latex]\lim_{x\rightarrow \infty }x^{1/x}[/latex] is
questions.solution:
[latex]x^{1/x}=e^{\frac{\ln x}{x}}[/latex], and [latex]\frac{\ln x}{x}\rightarrow0[/latex] as [latex]x\rightarrow\infty[/latex].

So the limit is [latex]e^0=1[/latex].

Answer: 1

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Match the following:
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Prim's MST: greedy (ii)
- Floyd-Warshall: dynamic programming (iii)
- Mergesort: divide and conquer (iv)
- Hamiltonian circuit: backtracking (i)

Answer: P-ii, Q-iii, R-iv, S-i

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Which one of the following is the recurrence equation for the worst case time complexity of the Quicksort algorithm for sorting n ( [latex]\geq[/latex]2) numbers? In the recurrence equations given in the options below, c is a constant.
questions.solution:
Worst case: the pivot is the smallest/largest each time, so the partition sizes are n[latex]-[/latex]1 and 1, plus linear partitioning work.

T(n) = T(n [latex]-[/latex] 1) + T(1) + cn

Answer: T(n) = T(n-1) + T(1) + cn

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: The height of a tree is the length of the longest root-to-leaf path in it. The maximum and minimum number of nodes in a binary tree of height 5 are
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Maximum: complete tree with levels 0 to 5 = [latex]2^6-1=63[/latex] nodes
- Minimum: a single path of 5 edges = 6 nodes

Answer: 63 and 6

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.text: Match the following:
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Condition coverage looks at the code: white-box (iii)
- Equivalence class partitioning uses only the specification: black-box (i)
- Volume testing checks behaviour under large data: performance (iv)
- Alpha testing is done on the whole system: system testing (ii)

Answer: P-iii, Q-i, R-iv, S-ii

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
Which of the following is/are correct inorder traversal sequence(s) of binary search tree(s)?
I. 3, 5, 7, 8, 15, 19, 25
II. 5, 8, 9, 12, 10, 15, 25
III. 2, 7, 10, 8, 14, 16, 20
IV. 4, 6, 7, 9 18, 20, 25
questions.solution:
In-order traversal of a BST is always sorted.

- I: sorted [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] valid
- II: 12 before 10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] invalid
- III: 10 before 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] invalid
- IV: sorted [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] valid

Answer: I and IV only

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text: Which one of the following is TRUE at any valid state in shift-reduce parsing?
options: Viable prefixes appear only at the bottom of the stack and not inside
Viable prefixes appear only at the top of the stack and not inside
The stack contains only a set of viable prefixes
The stack never contains viable prefixes
questions.solution:
In a valid shift-reduce parse, the stack content is always a viable prefix, i.e. a prefix of some right sentential form that does not go past the handle.

Answer: The stack contains only a set of viable prefixes

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT equivalent to [latex]p\leftrightarrow q[/latex]?
questions.solution:
[latex]p\leftrightarrow q[/latex] is true when p and q are equal.

- Options 1, 2: [latex](p\rightarrow q)\wedge(q\rightarrow p)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] equivalent
- Option 4: both false or both true [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] equivalent
- Option 3: exactly one is true, which is XOR, the negation of [latex]p\leftrightarrow q[/latex]

Answer: [latex](\neg p\wedge q)\vee(p\wedge\neg q)[/latex]

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
For a set A, the power set of A is denoted by [latex]2^{A}[/latex]. If A={5,{6},{7}}, which of the following options are TRUE?
I. [latex]\phi \in 2^{A}[/latex]
II. [latex]\phi \subseteq 2^{A}[/latex]
III. {5,{6}} [latex]\in 2^{A}[/latex]
IV. {5,{6}}[latex]\subseteq 2^{A}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: [latex]\phi\subseteq A[/latex], so [latex]\phi\in2^A[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II: the empty set is a subset of every set [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- III: {5, {6}} [latex]\subseteq[/latex] A, so it is an element of [latex]2^A[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- IV: would need 5 [latex]\in2^A[/latex], but 5 is not a subset of A [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: I, II and III only

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: Consider a 4-bit Johnson counter with an initial value of 0000. The counting sequence of this counter is
questions.solution:
A Johnson counter shifts right and feeds the complement of the last bit back to the first:

0000 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1000 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1100 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1110 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1111 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0111 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0011 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0001 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0000

In decimal: 0, 8, 12, 14, 15, 7, 3, 1, 0

Answer: 0, 8, 12, 14, 15, 7, 3, 1, 0

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
For computers based on three-address instruction formats, each address field can be used to specify which of the following:
(S1) A memory operand
(S2) A processor register
(S3) An implied accumulator register
options: All of S1, S2 and S3
questions.solution:
In a three-address instruction, each address field explicitly names a memory location or a register. An implied accumulator is used only in one-address formats.

Answer: Either S1 or S2

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
Suppose two hosts use a TCP connection to transfer a large file. Which of the following statements is/are FALSE with respect to the TCP connection?
I. If the sequence number of a segment is m, then the sequence number of the subsequent segment is always m+1.
II. If the estimated round trip time at any given point of time is t sec, the value of the retransmission timeout is always set to greater than or equal to t sec.
III. The size of the advertised window never changes during the course of the TCP connection.
IV. The number of unacknowledged bytes at the sender is always less than or equal to the advertised window.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: TCP numbers bytes, so the next sequence number is m + (segment length) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- II: RTO is set to at least the estimated RTT [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- III: the advertised window changes as the receive buffer fills and empties [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- IV: the sender keeps unacknowledged bytes within the window [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True

Answer: I and III only

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Suppose that everyone in a group of N people wants to communicate secretly with the N-1 others using symmetric key cryptographic system. The communication between any two persons should not be decodable by the others in the group. The number of keys required in the system as a whole to satisfy the confidentiality requirement is
questions.solution:
Each pair of people needs its own shared secret key.

Number of pairs = [latex]\binom N2=\frac{N(N-1)}{2}[/latex]

Answer: N(N-1)/2

questions.subject: Web Technology
questions.text:
Which of the following statements is/are FALSE?
I. XML overcomes the limitations in HTML to support a structured way of organizing content.
II. XML specification is not case sensitive while HTML specification is case sensitive.
III. XML supports user defined tags while HTML uses pre-defined tags.
IV. XML tags need not be closed while HTML tags must be closed.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: True
- II: reversed: XML is case sensitive, HTML is not [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- III: True
- IV: reversed: XML tags must be closed, HTML is lenient [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: II and IV only

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Which one of the following fields of an IP header is NOT modified by a typical IP router?
questions.solution:
Routers decrease TTL, recompute the checksum, and change the length when they fragment. The source address stays the same (unless NAT is used, which is not typical routing).

Answer: Source address

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: In one of the pairs of protocols given below, both the protocols can use multiple TCP connections between the same client and the server. Which one is that?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- HTTP: a browser can open several parallel TCP connections to the same server.
- FTP: uses a control connection plus separate data connections.

TELNET and SMTP use a single connection.

Answer: HTTP, FTP

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
For any two languages L1 and L2 such that L1 is context-free and L2 is recursively enumerable but not recursive, which of the following is/are necessarily true?
I. [latex]\bar{L_{1}}[/latex] (complement of L1) is recursive
II. [latex] \bar{L_{2}}[/latex] (complement of L2) is recursive
III. [latex]\bar{L_{1}}[/latex] is context-free
IV. [latex]\bar{L_{1}} \cup L_{2}[/latex] is recursively enumerable
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: CFLs are decidable, and recursive languages are closed under complement [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II: if [latex]\bar L_2[/latex] were recursive, L2 would be recursive [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- III: CFLs are not closed under complement [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not necessarily
- IV: [latex]\bar L_1[/latex] is recursive (so RE), and RE is closed under union [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True

Answer: I and IV only

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: Consider a system with byte-addressable memory, 32-bit logical addresses, 4 kilobyte page size and page table entries of 4 bytes each. The size of the page table in the system in megabytes is ________ .
questions.solution:
Number of pages = [latex]\frac{2^{32}}{2^{12}}=2^{20}[/latex]

Page table size = [latex]2^{20}\times4[/latex] B = 4 MB

Answer: 4

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
The following two functions P1 and P2 that share a variable B with an initial value of 2 execute concurrently.

The number of distinct values that B can possibly take after the execution is______________.
questions.solution:
B = 2 initially. Possible results:

- P1 then P2: C = 1, B = 2; D = 4, B = 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3
- P2 then P1: D = 4, B = 3; C = 2, B = 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4
- Both read B = 2 first (C = 1, D = 4), and P1 writes last: B = 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2

Distinct values {2, 3, 4} = 3

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text: SELECT operation in SQL is equivalent to
options: the selection operation in relational algebra
the selection operation in relational algebra, except that SELECT in SQL retains duplicates
the projection operation in relational algebra
the projection operation in relational algebra, except that SELECT in SQL retains duplicates
questions.solution:
The SELECT list chooses columns, which is projection. Unlike relational algebra, SQL keeps duplicate rows unless DISTINCT is used.

Answer: the projection operation, except that SELECT in SQL retains duplicates

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text: A file is organized so that the ordering of data records is the same as or close to the ordering of data entries in some index. Then that index is called
questions.solution:
When the data file is stored in (nearly) the same order as the index entries, the index is called clustered.

Answer: Clustered

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: In the LU decomposition of the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 2\\ 4&9 \end{bmatrix}[/latex], if the diagonal elements of U are both 1, then the lower diagonal entry [latex]l_{22}[/latex] of L is________.
questions.solution:
Crout form: [latex]\begin{bmatrix}2&2\\4&9\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}l_{11}&0\\l_{21}&l_{22}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&u_{12}\\0&1\end{bmatrix}[/latex]

- [latex]l_{11}=2,\; l_{11}u_{12}=2\Rightarrow u_{12}=1[/latex]
- [latex]l_{21}=4,\; l_{21}u_{12}+l_{22}=9\Rightarrow l_{22}=5[/latex]

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- f1 swaps copies only (call by value), so a = 4, b = 5 stay.
- f2 swaps through pointers: b = 6, c = 5.

c [latex]-[/latex] a [latex]-[/latex] b = 5 [latex]-[/latex] 4 [latex]-[/latex] 6 = [latex]-[/latex]5

Answer: -5

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: What are the worst-case complexities of insertion and deletion of a key in a binary search tree?
questions.solution:
A BST can be skewed (a chain) with height n [latex]-[/latex] 1. Insertion and deletion may then walk the whole chain.

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] for both insertion and deletion

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Suppose that the stop-and-wait protocol is used on a link with a bit rate of 64 kilobits per second and 20 milliseconds propagation delay. Assume that the transmission time for the acknowledgement and the processing time at nodes are negligible. Then the minimum frame size in bytes to achieve a link utilization of at least 50% is______________.
questions.solution:
Stop-and-wait utilization = [latex]\frac{T_t}{T_t+2T_p}\ge\frac12\Rightarrow T_t\ge2T_p=40[/latex] ms.

Frame size = [latex]64\times10^3\times40\times10^{-3}=2560[/latex] bits = 320 bytes.

Answer: 320

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
Consider a max heap, represented by the array: 40, 30, 20, 10, 15, 16, 17, 8, 4.

Now consider that a value 35 is inserted into this heap. After insertion, the new heap is
questions.solution:
35 goes to the next free position (index 10), as child of 15.

- 35 [latex]\gt[/latex] 15: swap [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 35 under 30
- 35 [latex]\gt[/latex] 30: swap [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 35 under 40
- 35 [latex]\lt[/latex] 40: stop

Heap: 40, 35, 20, 10, 30, 16, 17, 8, 4, 15

Answer: 40, 35, 20, 10, 30, 16, 17, 8, 4, 15

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.solution:
Decision points: while, if, else if, and the final if = 4.

Cyclomatic complexity = 4 + 1 = 5

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Consider a LAN with four nodes [latex]S_{1},S_{2},S_{3} \; and \; S_{4}[/latex] . Time is divided into fixed-size slots, and a node can begin its transmission only at the beginning of a slot. A collision is said to have occurred if more than one node transmit in the same slot. The probabilities of generation of a frame in a time slot by [latex]S_{1},S_{2},S_{3} \; and \;  S_{4}[/latex] are 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4, respectively. The probability of sending a frame in the first slot without any collision by any of these four stations is _____________.
questions.solution:
Success = exactly one station transmits.

- Only S1: 0.1 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.7 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.6 = 0.0336
- Only S2: 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.2 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.7 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.6 = 0.0756
- Only S3: 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.3 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.6 = 0.1296
- Only S4: 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.7 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.4 = 0.2016

Total = 0.4404

Answer: 0.44

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
The binary operator [latex]\neq[/latex] is defined by the following truth table.

Which one of the following is true about the binary operator [latex]\neq[/latex]?
questions.solution:
The table is exactly XOR ([latex]p\oplus q[/latex]).

XOR is commutative ([latex]p\oplus q=q\oplus p[/latex]) and associative ([latex](p\oplus q)\oplus r=p\oplus(q\oplus r)[/latex]).

Answer: Both commutative and associative

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.solution:
[latex]\frac{1}{x(x+1)}=\frac1x-\frac1{x+1}[/latex], so the sum telescopes:

[latex]1-\frac1{100}=0.99[/latex]

Answer: 0.99

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Suppose L={p,q,r,s,t} is a lattice represented by the following Hasse diagram:

For any [latex]x,y\in L[/latex] not necessarily distinct, [latex]x\vee y[/latex] and [latex]x\wedge y[/latex] are join and meet of x,y respectively. Let [latex]L^{3}=\{(x,y,z):x,y,z\in L\}[/latex] be the set of all ordered triplets of the elements of L. Let [latex]P_{r} [/latex] be the probability that an element [latex](x,y,z)\in L^{3}[/latex] chosen equiprobably satisfies [latex]x\vee (y \wedge z)=(x\vee y)\wedge (x\vee z)[/latex] . Then
questions.solution:
The lattice has bottom p, top t, and q, r, s incomparable in the middle (the diamond [latex]M_3[/latex]). It is not distributive.

- Fails for x, y, z = three different middle elements, e.g. [latex]q\vee(r\wedge s)=q\vee p=q[/latex] but [latex](q\vee r)\wedge(q\vee s)=t\wedge t=t[/latex]. There are 3! = 6 such triples.
- It holds for all other triples.

[latex]P_r=\frac{125-6}{125}=\frac{119}{125}[/latex], which lies between 1/5 and 1.

Answer: [latex]\frac15\lt P_r\lt1[/latex]

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
Consider the operations
[latex]f(X,Y,Z)=X'YZ+XY'+Y'Z'[/latex] and [latex] g(X,Y,Z)=X'YZ+X'YZ'+XY[/latex].
Which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
Post's theorem: a function alone is complete if it is not 0-preserving, not 1-preserving, not self-dual, not monotone and not linear.

f: f(0,0,0) = 1, f(1,1,1) = 0 (so also not monotone). f(0,0,1) = f(1,1,0) = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not self-dual. Not linear (fitting [latex]1\oplus Y\oplus Z[/latex] from the first rows gives f(1,1,1) = 1, but it is 0). So {f} is complete.

g: g(0,0,0) = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0-preserving, so {g} cannot produce 1 from 0s [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not complete.

Answer: Only {f} is functionally complete

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let G be a connected planar graph with 10 vertices. If the number of edges on each face is three, then the number of edges in G is ___________.
questions.solution:
Each face has 3 edges and each edge lies on 2 faces: 3f = 2e.

Euler: [latex]v-e+f=2\Rightarrow10-e+\frac{2e}{3}=2\Rightarrow e=24[/latex]

Answer: 24

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let [latex]a_{n}[/latex] represent the number of bit strings of length n containing two consecutive 1s. What is the recurrence relation for [latex]a_{n}[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Split by how the string starts:

- Starts with 0: the remaining n[latex]-[/latex]1 bits need 11 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]a_{n-1}[/latex]
- Starts with 10: the remaining n[latex]-[/latex]2 bits need 11 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]a_{n-2}[/latex]
- Starts with 11: already done, rest free [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]2^{n-2}[/latex]

[latex]a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}+2^{n-2}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]a_{n-2}+a_{n-1}+2^{n-2}[/latex]

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text:
A variable x is said to be live at a statement [latex]S_{i}[/latex] in a program if the following three conditions hold simultaneously:
i. There exists a statement [latex]S_{j}[/latex] that uses x
ii. There is a path from [latex]S_{i}[/latex] to [latex]S_{j}[/latex] in the flow graph corresponding to the program
iii. The path has no intervening assignment to x including at [latex]S_{i}[/latex] and [latex]S_{j}[/latex]

The variables which are live both at the statement in basic block 2 and at the statement in basic block 3 of the above control flow graph are
questions.solution:
Live-in = use [latex]\cup[/latex] (live-out [latex]-[/latex] def).

- Block 1 uses q, r, v before defining them [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] in(1) = {q, r, v}
- in(4) = {v, r} [latex]\cup[/latex] (in(1) [latex]-[/latex] {q}) = {r, v}
- in(2) = {r, u} [latex]\cup[/latex] (in(4) [latex]-[/latex] {v}) = {r, u}
- in(3) = {s, u} [latex]\cup[/latex] (in(4) [latex]-[/latex] {q}) = {r, s, u, v}

Common: r, u

Answer: r, u

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text: The least number of temporary variables required to create a three-address code in static single assignment form for the expression q + r / 3 + s - t * 5 + u * v /w is _______________.
questions.solution:
In SSA every result gets a new variable. Count the operations:

t1 = r / 3, t2 = q + t1, t3 = t2 + s, t4 = t * 5, t5 = t3 [latex]-[/latex] t4, t6 = u * v, t7 = t6 / w, t8 = t5 + t7

8 operations [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 temporaries

Answer: 8

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider an Entity-Relationship (ER) model in which entity sets E1 and E2 are connected by an m : n relationship R12. E1 and E3 are connected by a 1 : n (1 on the side of E1 and n on the side of E3) relationship R13.

E1 has two single-valued attributes a11 and a12 of which a11 is the key attribute. E2 has two single-valued attributes a21 and a22 of which a21 is the key attribute. E3 has two single-valued attributes a31 and a32 of which a31 is the key attribute. The relationships do not have any attributes.

If a relational model is derived from the above ER model, then the minimum number of relations that would be generated if all the relations are in 3NF is _______.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- E1(a11, a12), E2(a21, a22): one relation each
- R12 is m:n: needs its own relation (a11, a21)
- R13 is 1:n: add a11 as a foreign key in E3(a31, a32, a11), no separate table

Total = 4

Answer: 4

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text: Consider the DFAs M and N given above. The number of states in a minimal DFA that accepts the language L(M)[latex]\cap[/latex] L(N) is___________
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- M accepts strings ending with a.
- N accepts strings ending with b.

No string can end with both, so [latex]L(M)\cap L(N)=\emptyset[/latex]. The minimal DFA has a single non-accepting state.

Answer: 1

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the NPDA [latex]\langle Q=\{q_{0},q_{1},q_{2}\},[/latex] [latex]\Sigma =\{0,1\},[/latex] [latex]\Gamma =\{0,1,\perp \},\delta ,q_{0},\perp ,[/latex] [latex]F=\{q_{2}\} \rangle[/latex], where (as per usual convention) Q is the set of states, [latex]\Sigma[/latex] is the input alphabet, [latex]\Gamma[/latex] is the stack alphabet, [latex]\delta[/latex] is the state transition function, [latex]q_{0}[/latex] is the initial state, [latex]\perp[/latex] is the initial stack symbol, and [latex]F[/latex] is the set of accepting states. The state transition is as follows:

Which one of the following sequences must follow the string 101100 so that the overall string is accepted by the automaton?
questions.solution:
q0 pushes the input. It moves to q1 on one symbol or [latex]\epsilon[/latex] (an optional middle symbol). In q1, a 0 pops a 1 and a 1 pops a 0, so the second half must be the complement of the first half reversed.

Total length 6 + 5 = 11, so w = 10110 and the middle symbol is 0.
Reverse of w = 01101, complement = 10010.

Answer: 10010

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Let G = (V, E) be a simple undirected graph, and s be a particular vertex in it called the source. For [latex]x \in V[/latex], let d(x) denote the shortest distance in G from s to x. A breadth first search (BFS) is performed starting at s. Let T be the resultant BFS tree. If (u,v) is an edge of G that is not in T, then which one of the following CANNOT be the value of d(u)-d(v)?
questions.solution:
In BFS of an undirected graph, every edge joins vertices whose levels differ by at most 1. If d(u) [latex]-[/latex] d(v) were 2, v would have discovered u earlier, giving d(u) = d(v) + 1.

So d(u) [latex]-[/latex] d(v) can only be [latex]-[/latex]1, 0 or 1.

Answer: 2

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: Consider a uniprocessor system executing three tasks T1, T2 and T3, each of which is composed of an infinite sequence of jobs (or instances) which arrive periodically at intervals of 3, 7 and 20 milliseconds, respectively. The priority of each task is the inverse of its period, and the available tasks are scheduled in order of priority, with the highest priority task scheduled first. Each instance of T1, T2 and T3 requires an execution time of 1, 2 and 4 milliseconds, respectively. Given that all tasks initially arrive at the beginning of the 1st millisecond and task preemptions are allowed, the first instance of T3 completes its execution at the end of _____________ milliseconds.
questions.solution:
Priorities: T1 (period 3) [latex]\gt[/latex] T2 (7) [latex]\gt[/latex] T3 (20).

- 0-1 T1, 1-3 T2, 3-4 T1 (new instance)
- 4-6 T3 (2 of 4 ms)
- 6-7 T1, 7-9 T2, 9-10 T1
- 10-12 T3 (remaining 2 ms) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] done

Answer: 12

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: A positive edge-triggered D flip-flop is connected to a positive edge-triggered JK flip-flop as follows. The Q output of the D flip-flop is connected to both the J and K inputs of the JK flip-flop, while the Q output of the JK flip-flop is connected to the input of the D flip-flop. Initially, the output of the D flip-flop is set to logic one and the output of the JK flip-flop is cleared. Which one of the following is the bit sequence (including the initial state) generated at the Q output of the JK flip-flop when the flip-flops are connected to a free-running common clock? Assume that J=K=1 is the toggle mode and J=K=0 is the state-holding mode of the JK flip-flop. Both the flip-flops have non-zero propagation delays.
questions.solution:
Each clock: J = K = old D output, and D takes the old JK output. Start D = 1, Q(JK) = 0.

- Clock 1: J=K=1, toggle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q = 1; D = 0
- Clock 2: J=K=0, hold [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q = 1; D = 1
- Clock 3: J=K=1, toggle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q = 0; D = 1
- Clock 4: toggle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q = 1; D = 0, and the pattern repeats

Sequence: 0 1 1 0 1 1 0...

Answer: 0110110...

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: Consider a disk pack with a seek time of 4 milliseconds and rotational speed of 10000 rotations per minute (RPM). It has 600 sectors per track and each sector can store 512 bytes of data. Consider a file stored in the disk. The file contains 2000 sectors. Assume that every sector access necessitates a seek, and the average rotational latency for accessing each sector is half of the time for one complete rotation. The total time (in milliseconds) needed to read the entire file is ____________.
questions.solution:
One rotation = 60 / 10000 s = 6 ms.

Per sector: seek 4 + latency 3 + transfer 6/600 = 0.01 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 7.01 ms

Total = 2000 [latex]\times[/latex] 7.01 = 14020 ms

Answer: 14020

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: Consider a non-pipelined processor with a clock rate of 2.5 gigahertz and average cycles per instruction of four. The same processor is upgraded to a pipelined processor with five stages; but due to the internal pipeline delay, the clock speed is reduced to 2 gigahertz. Assume that there are no stalls in the pipeline. The speed up achieved in this pipelined processor is_________.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Non-pipelined: 4 cycles / 2.5 GHz = 1.6 ns per instruction
- Pipelined (CPI 1): 1 / 2 GHz = 0.5 ns per instruction

Speed-up = 1.6 / 0.5 = 3.2

Answer: 3.2

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: Suppose the following disk request sequence (track numbers) for a disk with 100 tracks is given: 45, 20, 90, 10, 50, 60, 80, 25, 70. Assume that the initial position of the R/W head is on track 50. The additional distance that will be traversed by the R/W head when the Shortest Seek Time First (SSTF) algorithm is used compared to the SCAN (Elevator) algorithm (assuming that SCAN algorithm moves towards 100 when it starts execution) is____________ tracks.
questions.solution:
SSTF from 50: 50 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 45 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 60 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 70 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 80 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 90 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 25 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 20 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10
= 5 + 15 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 65 + 5 + 10 = 130

SCAN (elevator), going up and reversing after the last request: 50 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 90 = 40, then 90 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10 = 80 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 120

Extra distance = 130 [latex]-[/latex] 120 = 10

Answer: 10

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: Consider a main memory with five page frames and the following sequence of page references: 3, 8, 2, 3, 9, 1, 6, 3, 8, 9, 3, 6, 2, 1, 3. Which one of the following is true with respect to page replacement policies First In First Out (FIFO) and Least Recently Used (LRU)?
options: Both incur the same number of page faults
FIFO incurs 2 more page faults than LRU
LRU incurs 2 more page faults than FIFO
FIFO incurs 1 more page faults than LRU
questions.solution:
FIFO: 3, 8, 2, 9, 1 (5); 6 replaces 3; 3 replaces 8; 8 replaces 2; 2 replaces 9 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 9 faults

LRU: 3, 8, 2, 9, 1 (5); 6 replaces 8; 8 replaces 2; 2 replaces 1; 1 replaces 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 9 faults

Answer: Both incur the same number of page faults

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: [latex]\int_{1/ \pi }^{2/ \pi}\frac{cos(1/x)}{x^{2}}dx=[/latex]_________.
questions.solution:
Let u = 1/x, so [latex]du=-\frac{dx}{x^2}[/latex]. Limits: x = 1/[latex]\pi[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] u = [latex]\pi[/latex], x = 2/[latex]\pi[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] u = [latex]\pi/2[/latex].

[latex]\int_{\pi}^{\pi/2}-\cos u\,du=\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}\cos u\,du=\sin\pi-\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=-1[/latex]

Answer: -1

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider the following 2x2 matrix A where two elements are unknown and are marked by a and b. The eigenvalues of this matrix are -1 and 7. What are the values of a and b?
[latex]A=\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 4\\ b&a \end{pmatrix}[/latex].
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Trace: 1 + a = [latex]-[/latex]1 + 7 = 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a = 5
- Determinant: a [latex]-[/latex] 4b = ([latex]-[/latex]1)(7) = [latex]-[/latex]7 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 [latex]-[/latex] 4b = [latex]-[/latex]7 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] b = 3

Answer: a = 5, b = 3

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: An algorithm performs [latex](log N)^{1/2}[/latex] find operations, [latex]N[/latex]  insert operations, [latex](log N)^{1/2}[/latex] delete operations, and [latex](log N)^{1/2}[/latex] decrease-key operations on a set of data items with keys drawn from a linearly ordered set.
