For a delete operation, a pointer is provided to the record that must be deleted. For the decrease-key operation, a pointer is provided to the record that has its key decreased. Which one of the following data structures is the most suited for the algorithm to use, if the goal is to achieve the best total asymptotic complexity considering all the operations?
questions.solution:
N inserts dominate. Compare total cost:

- Unsorted array: insert O(1), find O(N), delete/decrease-key with pointer O(1) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N\sqrt{\log N})[/latex]
- Min-heap: N inserts cost [latex]O(N\log N)[/latex]
- Sorted array / sorted list: each insert O(N) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N^2)[/latex]

Answer: Unsorted array

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the following relations:

Consider the following SQL query.

The number of rows that will be returned by the SQL query is _____________.
questions.solution:
The query groups by Student_Name. The names are Raj (roll 1 and roll 3) and Rohit, so there are 2 groups.

Rows: Raj, 310 and Rohit, 140

Answer: 2

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
One row = 3 ints = 12 bytes.

- x + 3 = address of row 3 = 2000 + 3 [latex]\times[/latex] 12 = 2036
- *(x + 3) = address of x[3][0] = 2036
- *(x + 2) + 3 = address of x[2][0] + 3 ints = 2024 + 12 = 2036

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: The graph shown below has 8 edges with distinct integer edge weights. The minimum spanning tree (MST) is of weight 36 and contains the edges: {(A, C), (B, C), (B, E), (E, F), (D, F)}. The edge weights of only those edges which are in the MST are given in the figure shown below. The minimum possible sum of weights of all 8 edges of this graph is ___________.
questions.solution:
MST weights: AC = 9, BC = 2, BE = 15, EF = 4, DF = 6 (total 36). A non-MST edge must be heavier than every MST edge on its cycle (weights are distinct).

- AB: cycle A-C-B, max 9 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] AB [latex]\ge[/latex] 10
- CD: path C-B-E-F-D, max 15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CD [latex]\ge[/latex] 16
- DE: path D-F-E, max 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] DE [latex]\ge[/latex] 7

Minimum total = 36 + 10 + 16 + 7 = 69

Answer: 69

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.solution:
For each of the n iterations:
- the j loop makes [latex]p\approx\log n[/latex]
- the k loop doubles k up to p, adding [latex]\log p\approx\log\log n[/latex] to q

q [latex]\approx n\log\log n[/latex]

Answer: [latex]n\log(\log n)[/latex]

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
Consider the following pseudo code, where x and y are positive integers. 
 begin
   q := 0
    r := x 
    while r >= y  do
         begin
               r := r - y
              q := q + 1
        end
end
The post condition that needs to be satisfied after the program terminates is
questions.solution:
The loop subtracts y from r and counts it in q, which is division of x by y. Invariant: x = qy + r. The loop stops when r [latex]\lt[/latex] y.

Answer: {x = qy + r [latex]\wedge[/latex] r [latex]\lt[/latex] y}

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Didn't you buy ____ when you went shopping?
questions.solution:
"Any" is used in questions and negatives. "Paper" here is uncountable, so "a few" is wrong, and "no" makes a double negative.

Answer: any paper

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Which of the following options is the closest in meaning of the sentence below?

She enjoyed herself immensely at the party.
options: She had a terrible time at the party
She had a horrible time at the party
She had a terrific time at the party
She had a terrifying time at the party
questions.solution:
"Enjoyed herself immensely" = had a very good time. "Terrific" means excellent here; terrible, horrible and terrifying are negative.

Answer: She had a terrific time at the party

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Given Set A=2,3,4,5 and Set B=11,12,13,14,15, two numbers are randomly selected, one from each set. What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers equals 16?
questions.solution:
Total pairs = 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 20.

Sum 16: (2, 14), (3, 13), (4, 12), (5, 11) = 4 pairs

Probability = 4 / 20 = 0.2

Answer: 0.2

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Based on the given statements, select the most appropriate option to solve the given question.

If two floors in a certain building are 9 feet apart, how many steps are there in a set of stairs that extends from the first floor to the second floor of the building?

Statements:

I. Each step is 3/4 foot high.
II. Each step is 1 foot wide.
options: Statements I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not sufficient.
Statements II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Statements I and II together are not sufficient.?
questions.solution:
Number of steps = height / step height = 9 / (3/4) = 12, so statement I alone answers it.

The width of a step does not tell how many steps there are.

Answer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Which one of the following combinations is incorrect?
questions.solution:
Wheedle means to coax or flatter someone into doing something. It does not mean roundabout.

The other pairs are correct.

Answer: Wheedle - Roundabout

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
The number of students in a class who have answered correctly, wrongly, or not attempted each question in an exam, are listed in the table below. The marks for each question are also listed. There is no negative or partial marking.

[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \textbf{Q No.} & \textbf{Marks} &\textbf{Answered}&\textbf{Answered}&\textbf{Not}\\&&\textbf{ Correctly} &\textbf{Wrongly} & \textbf{Attempted} \\\hline \text{1} & \text{2} &\text{21} &\text{17} &\text{6}\\\hline \text{2} & \text{3} &\text{15} & \text{27}& \text{2}\\\hline \text{3} & \text{1} &\text{11} & \text{29} & \text{4}\\\hline \text{4} & \text{2} &\text{23} & \text{18} & \text{3}\\\hline \text{5} & \text{5} &\text{31} & \text{12} & \text{1} \\\hline \end{array}[/latex]

What is the average of the marks obtained by the class in the examination?
questions.solution:
Marks: 21 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 + 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 + 11 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 + 23 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 + 31 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 42 + 45 + 11 + 46 + 155 = 299

Students = 21 + 17 + 6 = 44

Average = 299 / 44 = 6.795

Answer: 6.795

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Select the alternative meaning of the underlined part of the sentence.
The chain snatchers [latex]\underline{\text{took to their heels}}[/latex] when the police party arrived.
options: Took shelter in a thick jungle
questions.solution:
"Take to one's heels" means to run away, i.e. to take flight.

Answer: Took to flight

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
The given statement is followed by some courses of action. Assuming the statement to be true, decide the correct option.

Statement:
There has been a significant drop in the water level in the lakes supplying water to the city.

Course of action:
I. The water supply authority should impose a partial cut in supply to tackle the situation.
II. The government should appeal to all the residents through mass media for minimal use of water.
III. The government should ban the water supply in lower areas.
questions.solution:
A partial supply cut (I) and an appeal to save water (II) are sensible ways to manage a shortage.

Banning supply only in lower areas (III) is unfair and extreme.

Answer: Statements I and II follow

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: The pie chart below has the breakup of the number of students from different departments in an engineering college for the year 2012. The proportion of male to female students in each department is 5:4. There are 40 males in Electrical Engineering. What is the difference between the numbers of female students in the civil department and the female students in the Mechanical department?
questions.solution:
Electrical = 20% with 40 males. Males : females = 5 : 4, so Electrical total = 40 [latex]\times[/latex] 9/5 = 72 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] college total = 360.

- Civil (30%) = 108 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] females = 108 [latex]\times[/latex] 4/9 = 48
- Mechanical (10%) = 36 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] females = 16

Difference = 48 [latex]-[/latex] 16 = 32

Answer: 32

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
The probabilities that a student passes in mathematics, physics and chemistry are m,p and c respectively. Of these subjects, the student has 75% chance of passing in at least one, a 50% chance of passing in at least two and a 40% chance of passing in exactly two. Following relations are drawn in m,p,c:

I. p+m+c=27/20
II. p+m+c=13/20
III. (p)x(m)x(c)=1/10
options: Relations II and III are true.
Relations I and III are true.
questions.solution:
P(exactly 3) = P(at least 2) [latex]-[/latex] P(exactly 2) = 0.5 [latex]-[/latex] 0.4 = 0.1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] pmc = 1/10 (III true).
P(exactly 1) = 0.75 [latex]-[/latex] 0.5 = 0.25

p + m + c = expected number of subjects passed = 1(0.25) + 2(0.4) + 3(0.1) = 1.35 = 27/20 (I true).

Answer: Relations I and III are true

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider the following two statements.

S1: If a candidate is known to be corrupt, then he will not be elected
S2: If a candidate is kind, he will be elected

Which one of the following statements follows from S1 and S2 as per sound inference rules of logic?
options: If a person is known to be corrupt, he is kind
If a person is not known to be corrupt, he is not kind
If a person is kind, he is not known to be corrupt
If a person is not kind, he is not known to be corrupt
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: corrupt [latex]\rightarrow\neg[/latex] elected, whose contrapositive is elected [latex]\rightarrow\neg[/latex] corrupt
- S2: kind [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] elected

Chaining: kind [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] elected [latex]\rightarrow\neg[/latex] corrupt.

Answer: If a person is kind, he is not known to be corrupt

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: The cardinality of the power set of { 0, 1, 2,..., 10 } is _________.
questions.solution:
The set {0, 1, ..., 10} has 11 elements.

[latex]|P(S)|=2^{11}=2048[/latex]

Answer: 2048

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let R be the relation on the set of positive integers such that aRb if and only if a and b are distinct and have a common divisor other than 1. Which one of the following statements about R is true?
options: R is symmetric and reflexive but not transitive
R is reflexive but not symmetric and not transitive
R is transitive but not reflexive and not symmetric
R is symmetric but not reflexive and not transitive
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Not reflexive: a and b must be distinct.
- Symmetric: a common divisor of a, b is also a common divisor of b, a.
- Not transitive: 2 R 6 and 6 R 3, but 2 and 3 have no common divisor other than 1.

Answer: R is symmetric but not reflexive and not transitive

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: The number of divisors of 2100 is _____ .
questions.solution:
[latex]2100=2^2\times3\times5^2\times7[/latex]

Number of divisors = (2 + 1)(1 + 1)(2 + 1)(1 + 1) = 36

Answer: 36

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: The larger of the two eigenvalues of the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 5\\ 2&1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] is _______.
questions.solution:
[latex]\lambda^2-(4+1)\lambda+(4-10)=\lambda^2-5\lambda-6=(\lambda-6)(\lambda+1)=0[/latex]

Eigenvalues 6 and [latex]-[/latex]1; the larger is 6.

Answer: 6

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: An unordered list contains n distinct elements. The number of comparisons to find an element in this list that is neither maximum nor minimum is
questions.solution:
Take any 3 elements and compare them (3 comparisons). The middle one of the three is neither the overall maximum nor the overall minimum.

This is a constant number of comparisons.

Answer: [latex]\Theta(1)[/latex]

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: The minimum number of JK flip-flops required to construct a synchronous counter with the count sequence (0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,0,0,...) is __________ .
questions.solution:
The sequence 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3 has 8 steps before repeating. Equal outputs at different steps must still be different internal states, so 8 states are needed.

[latex]2^3=8[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 flip-flops

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: Assume that for a certain processor, a read request takes 50 nanoseconds on a cache miss and 5 nanoseconds on a cache hit. Suppose while running a program, it was observed that 80% of the processor's read requests result in a cache hit. The average read access time in nanoseconds is __________.
questions.solution:
Average = 0.8 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 + 0.2 [latex]\times[/latex] 50 = 4 + 10 = 14 ns

Answer: 14

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: A computer system implements a 40-bit virtual address, page size of 8 kilobytes, and a 128-entry translation look-aside buffer (TLB) organized into 32 sets each having four ways. Assume that the TLB tag does not store any process id. The minimum length of the TLB tag in bits is _________.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Page offset: 8 KB = [latex]2^{13}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 13 bits, so page number = 40 [latex]-[/latex] 13 = 27 bits
- 32 sets [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 index bits

Tag = 27 [latex]-[/latex] 5 = 22 bits

Answer: 22

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
I. The complement of every Turing decidable language is Turing decidable
II. There exists some language which is in NP but is not Turing decidable
III. If L is a language in NP, L is Turing decidable

Which of the above statements is/are true?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: decidable languages are closed under complement [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II: every NP language is decided by a (time-bounded) Turing machine [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- III: same reason [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True

Answer: Only I and III

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
foo first recurses to the next character and prints the current one on the way back, so it prints in reverse. It stops at the end of string or at a space.

Only "ABCD" is processed, printed reversed: DCBA

Answer: DCBA

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: Consider a complete binary tree where the left and the right subtrees of the root are max-heaps. The lower bound for the number of operations to convert the tree to a heap is
questions.solution:
Both subtrees are already heaps, so only the root may be out of place. One heapify (sift-down) from the root fixes it, moving down at most the height of the tree.

Bound = [latex]\Omega(\log n)[/latex] (and this is enough).

Answer: [latex]\Omega(\log n)[/latex]

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: A binary tree T has 20 leaves. The number of nodes in T having two children is _______.
questions.solution:
In any binary tree, (nodes with 2 children) = (leaves) [latex]-[/latex] 1.

20 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 19

Answer: 19

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
Software Engineering
questions.text: A software requirements specification (SRS) document should avoid discussing which one of the following?
questions.solution:
An SRS says what the system must do (functional and non-functional needs, interfaces, UI requirements). How it is built (the design) belongs in the design document.

Answer: Design specification

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Consider two decision problems Q1,Q2 such that Q1 reduces in polynomial time to 3-SAT and 3-SAT reduces in polynomial time to Q2. Then which one of the following is consistent with the above statement?
options: Q1 is in NP, Q2 is NP hard.
Q2 is in NP, Q1 is NP hard
Both Q1 and Q2 are in NP .
Both Q1 and Q2 are NP hard
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Q1 [latex]\le_p[/latex] 3-SAT, and 3-SAT is in NP [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q1 is in NP.
- 3-SAT [latex]\le_p[/latex] Q2, and 3-SAT is NP-hard [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q2 is NP-hard.

Answer: Q1 is in NP, Q2 is NP hard

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text: Match the following:
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Lexical analysis: DFA minimization (2)
- Parsing: production (parse) tree (4)
- Register allocation: graph coloring (1)
- Expression evaluation: post-order traversal (3)

Answer: P-2, Q-4, R-1, S-3

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text: In the context of abstract-syntax-tree (AST) and control-flow-graph (CFG), which one of the following is TRUE?
options: In both AST and CFG, let node N2 be the successor of node N1. In the input program, the code corresponding to N2 is present after the code corresponding to N1
For any input program, neither AST nor CFG will contain a cycle
The maximum number of successors of a node in an AST and a CFG depends on the input program
Each node in AST and CFG corresponds to at most one statement in the input program
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Option 1: in a CFG a loop edge goes back to earlier code [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] false.
- Option 2: CFGs have cycles for loops [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] false.
- Option 3: an AST node can have as many children as the construct needs, and a CFG node (e.g. switch) as many successors as the code has [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- Option 4: a CFG basic block can contain many statements [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] false.

Answer: The maximum number of successors depends on the input program

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.text: Consider the basic COCOMO model where E is the effort applied in person-months, D is the development time in chronological months, KLOC is the estimated number of delivered lines of code (in thousands) and [latex]a_{b},b_{b},c_{b},d_{b}[/latex] have their usual meanings. The basic COCOMO equations are of the form
questions.solution:
Basic COCOMO: effort from size, then time from effort.

[latex]E=a_b(KLOC)^{b_b},\quad D=c_b(E)^{d_b}[/latex]

Answer: E = [latex]a_b[/latex](KLOC)exp([latex]b_b[/latex]), D = [latex]c_b[/latex](E)exp([latex]d_b[/latex])

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: A system has 6 identical resources and N processes competing for them. Each process can request atmost 2 resources. Which one of the following values of N could lead to a deadlock?
questions.solution:
Deadlock is possible when every process holds one less than its maximum and nothing is left: N [latex]\times[/latex] (2 [latex]-[/latex] 1) [latex]\ge[/latex] 6, i.e. [latex]N\ge6[/latex].

Strictly, none of 1, 2, 3, 4 can deadlock (with N = 4, after each holds 1 there are still 2 free). The question is flawed; the official key marks N = 4, the largest choice.

Answer: 4 (as per key)

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the following transaction involving two bank accounts x and y.

read(x); x:=x-50; write(x); read(y); y:=y+50; write(y)

The constraint that the sum of the accounts x and y should remain constant is that of
questions.solution:
Keeping x + y constant is an integrity rule of the database, which the transaction must preserve. That is the consistency property.

Answer: Consistency

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
With reference to the B+ tree index of order 1 shown below, the minimum number of nodes (including the Root node) that must be fetched in order to satisfy the following query:
"Get all records with a search key greater than or equal to 7 and less than 15"
is ____________.
questions.solution:
Search for 7: root (9) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] left internal node (5) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] leaf [5, 7].

Then follow leaf links: [9, 11] and [13, 15], where 15 shows we can stop.

Nodes = root + 1 internal + 3 leaves = 5

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: Identify the correct order in which a server process must invoke the function calls accept, bind, listen, and recv according to UNIx socket API.
questions.solution:
Server side: socket, then bind (attach address), listen (become passive), accept (take a connection), recv (read data).

Answer: bind, listen, accept, recv

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: A link has a transmission speed of [latex]10^{6}[/latex] bits/sec. It uses data packets of size 1000 bytes each. Assume that the acknowledgment has negligible transmission delay, and that its propagation delay is the same as the data propagation delay. Also assume that the processing delays at nodes are negligible. The efficiency of the stop-and-wait protocol in this setup is exactly 25%. The value of the one-way propagation delay (in milliseconds) is ________.
questions.solution:
[latex]T_t=\frac{8000}{10^6}=8[/latex] ms.

[latex]\eta=\frac{T_t}{T_t+2T_p}=0.25\Rightarrow 8+2T_p=32\Rightarrow T_p=12[/latex] ms

Answer: 12

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about HTTP cookies?
options: A cookie is a piece of code that has the potential to compromise the security of an Internet user
A cookie gains entry to the user's work area through an HTTP header
A cookie has an expiry date and time
Cookies can be used to track the browsing pattern of a user at a particular site
questions.solution:
A cookie is a small piece of data (name-value text) stored by the browser, not executable code.

It does come in the Set-Cookie HTTP header, has an expiry time and can track browsing on a site.

Answer: A cookie is a piece of code that has the potential to compromise security

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
Consider the following routing table at an IP router:

For each IP address in Group I identify the correct choice of the next hop from Group II using the entries from the routing table above.
questions.solution:
AND the address with each mask and look for the longest match:

- i) 171 AND 254 = 170 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Interface 0 (a)
- ii) 167 AND 254 = 166 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R2 (c)
- iii) 163: /23 gives 162, /22 gives 160, no match [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] default R4 (e)
- iv) 165: /23 gives 164 (no /23 entry), /22 gives 164 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R3 (d)

Answer: i-a, ii-c, iii-e, iv-d

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Host A sends a UDP datagram containing 8880 bytes of user data to host B over an Ethernet LAN. Ethernet frames may carry data up to 1500 bytes (i.e. MTU=1500 bytes). Size of UDP header is 8 bytes and size of IP header is 20 bytes. There is no option field in IP header. How many total number of IP fragments will be transmitted and what will be the contents of offset field in the last fragment?
questions.solution:
IP payload = 8880 + 8 (UDP header) = 8888 bytes. Max data per fragment = 1500 [latex]-[/latex] 20 = 1480.

6 fragments carry 6 [latex]\times[/latex] 1480 = 8880 bytes, and 8 bytes remain [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 7 fragments.

Offset of the last = 8880 / 8 = 1110

Answer: 7 and 1110

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Assume that the bandwidth for a TCP connection is 1048560 bits/sec. Let [latex]\alpha[/latex] be the value of RTT in milliseconds (rounded off to the nearest integer) after which the TCP window scale option is needed. Let [latex]\beta[/latex] be the maximum possible window size with window scale option. Then the values of [latex]\alpha[/latex] and [latex]\beta[/latex] are
questions.solution:
Without scaling, max window = 65535 bytes. Bandwidth = 1048560 / 8 = 131070 bytes/s.

Scaling is needed once bandwidth [latex]\times[/latex] RTT exceeds 65535: RTT = 65535 / 131070 = 0.5 s = 500 ms.

The max scale shift is 14, so [latex]\beta=65535\times2^{14}[/latex].

Answer: 500 milliseconds, 65535 [latex]\times[/latex] [latex]2^{14}[/latex]

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider a simple checkpointing protocol and the following set of operations in the log.
(start, T4); (write, T4, y, 2, 3); (start, T1); (commit, T4); (write, T1, z, 5, 7);
(checkpoint);
(start, T2); (write, T2, x, 1, 9); (commit, T2); (start, T3), (write, T3, z, 7, 2);
If a crash happens now and the system tries to recover using both undo and redo operations, what are the contents of the undo list and the redo list?
options: Undo: T3, T1; Redo: T2, T4
Undo: none; Redo: T2, T4, T3, T1
Undo: T3, T1, T4; Redo: T2
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- T4 committed before the checkpoint [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] already safe, nothing to do.
- T1 started before the checkpoint and never committed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undo.
- T2 committed after the checkpoint [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] redo.
- T3 never committed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undo.

Answer: Undo: T3, T1; Redo: T2

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text: Consider two relations R1(A,B) with the tuples (1,5), (3,7) and R2(A,C) = (1,7), (4,9). Assume that R(A,B,C) is the full natural outer join of R1 and R2. Consider the following tuples of the form (A,B,C): a = (1,5,null), b = (1,null,7), c = (3, null, 9), d = (4,7,null), e = (1,5,7), f = (3,7,null), g = (4,null,9). Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: R contains a, b, e, f, g but not c, d.
R contains all of a, b, c, d, e, f, g.
R contains e, f, g but not a, b.
R contains e but not f, g.
questions.solution:
Natural join on A:
- A = 1 matches: (1, 5, 7) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] e
- R1 (3, 7) has no match: (3, 7, null) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f
- R2 (4, 9) has no match: (4, null, 9) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] g

Since A = 1 matched, (1, 5, null) and (1, null, 7) do not appear.

Answer: R contains e, f, g but not a, b

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: Consider six memory partitions of sizes 200 KB, 400 KB, 600 KB, 500 KB, 300 KB and 250 KB, where KB refers to kilobyte. These partitions need to be allotted to four processes of sizes 357 KB, 210 KB, 468 KB and 491 KB in that order. If the best fit algorithm is used, which partitions are NOT allotted to any process?
questions.solution:
Best fit picks the smallest partition that fits:

- 357 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 400
- 210 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 250
- 468 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 500
- 491 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 600

Unused: 200 KB and 300 KB

Answer: 200 KB and 300 KB

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: Consider a typical disk that rotates at 15000 rotations per minute (RPM) and has a transfer rate of 50x[latex]10^{6}[/latex]  bytes/sec. If the average seek time of the disk is twice the average rotational delay and the controller's transfer time is 10 times the disk transfer time, the average time (in milliseconds) to read or write a 512-byte sector of the disk is ______.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- One rotation = 60 / 15000 s = 4 ms [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] average rotational delay = 2 ms
- Seek = 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 4 ms
- Disk transfer = 512 / (50 [latex]\times[/latex] [latex]10^6[/latex]) = 0.01024 ms
- Controller = 10 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.01024 = 0.1024 ms

Total = 4 + 2 + 0.01024 + 0.1024 [latex]\approx[/latex] 6.11 ms

Answer: 6.11 (6.1 to 6.2)

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: A computer system implements 8 kilobyte pages and a 32-bit physical address space. Each page table entry contains a valid bit, a dirty bit, three permission bits, and the translation. If the maximum size of the page table of a process is 24 megabytes, the length of the virtual address supported by the system is _____ bits.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Frames = [latex]2^{32}/2^{13}=2^{19}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 19 bits for translation
- PTE = 19 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 24 bits = 3 bytes
- Entries = 24 MB / 3 B = 8M = [latex]2^{23}[/latex] pages

Virtual address = 23 + 13 = 36 bits

Answer: 36

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text:
Consider the intermediate code given below.
(1) i = 1
(2) j = 1
(3) t1 = 5 * i
(4) t2 = t1 + j
(5) t3 = 4 * t2
(6) t4 = t3
(7) a[t4] = -1
(8) j = j + 1
(9) if j[latex]\leq [/latex]5 goto (3)
(10) i=i+1
(11) if i[latex]\lt [/latex]5 goto (2)
The number of nodes and edges in the control-flow-graph constructed for the above code, respectively, are
questions.solution:
Leaders: (1), (2) (target of 11), (3) (target of 9), (10) (after a jump).
Blocks: B1 = {1}, B2 = {2}, B3 = {3-9}, B4 = {10, 11}, plus Entry and Exit [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 nodes.

Edges: Entry[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B1, B1[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B2, B2[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B3, B3[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B3, B3[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B4, B4[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B2, B4[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Exit [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 7 edges.

Answer: 6 and 7

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text: The number of states in the minimal deterministic finite automaton corresponding to the regular expression (0+1)*(10) is __________.
questions.solution:
Language: strings ending in "10". States needed: no progress, last symbol 1, last two symbols 10 (accepting).

These are all distinguishable, so the minimal DFA has 3 states.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Which of the following languages is/are regular?
[latex]L_{1}:\{wxw^{R}|w,x \in \{a,b\}^{*} \; and \; |w|,|x| \gt 0 \}, w^{R}[/latex] is the reverse of string w
[latex]L_{2}:\{a^{n}b^{m}|m\neq n \; and \; m,n\geq 0\}[/latex]
[latex]L_{3}:\{a^{p}b^{q}c^{r}|p,q,r\geq 0\}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- L1: since x can be anything, it is enough that the first and last symbols match (w of length 1). L1 = a(a+b)+a + b(a+b)+b [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] regular.
- L2: [latex]a^nb^m[/latex] with [latex]m\ne n[/latex] needs counting [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not regular.
- L3 = a*b*c* [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] regular.

Answer: L1 and L3 only

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Given below are some algorithms, and some algorithm design paradigms.

Match the above algorithms on the left to the corresponding design paradigm they follow.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Dijkstra: greedy (iii)
- Floyd-Warshall: dynamic programming (ii)
- Binary search: divide and conquer (i)
- Backtracking: depth-first search (iv)

Answer: 1-iii, 2-ii, 3-i, 4-iv

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
A Young tableau is a 2D array of integers increasing from left to right and from top to bottom. Any unfilled entries are marked with [latex]\infty[/latex], and hence there cannot be any entry to the right of, or below a [latex]\infty[/latex]. The following Young tableau consists of unique entries.

When an element is removed from a Young tableau, other elements should be moved into its place so that the resulting table is still a Young tableau (unfilled entries may be filled in with a [latex]\infty[/latex]). The minimum number of entries (other than 1) to be shifted, to remove 1 from the given Young tableau is _______.
questions.solution:
Removing 1 leaves a hole. Repeatedly fill it with the smaller of its right and lower neighbour:

- hole (1,1): min(2, 3) = 2 moves left
- hole (1,2): min(5, 4) = 4 moves up
- hole (2,2): min(6, 12) = 6 moves left
- hole (2,3): min(23, 18) = 18 moves up
- hole (3,3): min(25, [latex]\infty[/latex]) = 25 moves left
- hole (3,4) gets [latex]\infty[/latex]

Shifted: 2, 4, 6, 18, 25 = 5 entries

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.solution:
The pivot is at index left_end and is the (left_end + 1)-th smallest.

- If left_end + 1 [latex]\gt[/latex] k: search the left part a[0 .. left_end[latex]-[/latex]1] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (a, left_end, k)
- Else: search the right part starting at a + left_end + 1, with n [latex]-[/latex] left_end [latex]-[/latex] 1 elements, for the (k [latex]-[/latex] left_end [latex]-[/latex] 1)-th smallest

Answer: (a, left_end, k) and (a+left_end+1, n-left_end-1, k-left_end-1)

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Which one of the following hash functions on integers will distribute keys most uniformly over 10 buckets numbered 0 to 9 for i ranging from 0 to 2020?
questions.solution:
Last digit of [latex]i^3[/latex] for last digits 0..9: 0, 1, 8, 7, 4, 5, 6, 3, 2, 9. Every bucket gets used equally.

Squares end only in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 9, so options 1, 3, 4 leave some buckets empty.

Answer: h(i) = [latex]i^3[/latex] mod 10

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: The secant method is used to find the root of an equation f(x)=0. It is started from two distinct estimates [latex]x_{a}[/latex] and [latex]x_{b}[/latex] for the root. It is an iterative procedure involving linear interpolation to a root. The iteration stops if [latex]f(x_{b})[/latex] is very small and then [latex]x_{b}[/latex] is the solution. The procedure is given below. Observe that there is an expression which is missing and is marked by ?. Which is the suitable expression that is to be put in place of ? so that it follows all steps of the secant method?
questions.solution:
The secant line through [latex](x_a,f(x_a))[/latex] and [latex](x_b,f_b)[/latex] crosses the x-axis at:

[latex]x_t=x_b-\frac{(x_b-x_a)f_b}{f_b-f(x_a)}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]x_b-(x_b-x_a)f_b/(f_b-f(x_a))[/latex]

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
Inside stkFunc, the static local stkTop (starting at 0) hides the global one.

- stkFunc([latex]-[/latex]1, 10): size = 10
- push 5, push 10
- the two pops return 10 and 5

10 + 5 = 15

Answer: 15

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
Consider the sequence of machine instructions given below:
MUL R5, R0, R1
DIV R6, R2, R3
ADD R7, R5, R6
SUB R8, R7, R4
In the above sequence, R0 to R8 are general purpose registers. In the instructions shown, the first register stores the result of the operation performed on the second and the third registers. This sequence of instructions is to be executed in a pipelined instruction processor with the following 4 stages: (1) Instruction Fetch and Decode (IF), (2) Operand Fetch (OF), (3) Perform Operation (PO) and (4) Write back the result (WB). The IF, OF and WB stages take 1 clock cycle each for any instruction. The PO stage takes 1 clock cycle for ADD or SUB instruction, 3 clock cycles for MUL instruction and 5 clock cycles for DIV instruction. The pipelined processor uses operand forwarding from the PO stage to the OF stage.

The number of clock cycles taken for the execution of the above sequence of instructions is ___________.
questions.solution:
Cycle-by-cycle (PO stage can hold one instruction at a time; results forwarded from PO):

- MUL: IF 1, OF 2, PO 3-5, WB 6
- DIV: IF 2, OF 3, PO 6-10, WB 11
- ADD: IF 3, OF 4, waits for R6, PO 11, WB 12
- SUB: IF 4, OF 5, waits for R7, PO 12, WB 13

Answer: 13

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
Consider a processor with byte-addressable memory. Assume that all registers, including Program Counter (PC) and Program Status Word (PSW), are of size 2 bytes. A stack in the main memory is implemented from memory location [latex](0100)_{16}[/latex] and it grows upward. The stack pointer (SP) points to the top element of the stack. The current value of SP is [latex](016E)_{16}[/latex]. The CALL instruction is of two words, the first word is the op-code and the second word is the starting address of the subroutine (one word = 2 bytes). The CALL instruction is implemented as follows:

Store the current value of PC in the stack
Store the value of PSW register in the stack
Load the starting address of the subroutine in PC

The content of PC just before the fetch of a CALL instruction is [latex](5FA0)_{16}[/latex]. After execution of the CALL instruction, the value of the stack pointer is
questions.solution:
The stack grows upward and SP points to the top element, so each push adds 2 to SP and then stores.

- Push PC: SP = 016E + 2 = 0170
- Push PSW: SP = 0170 + 2 = 0172

Answer: [latex](0172)_{16}[/latex]

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
The number of min-terms after minimizing the following Boolean Algebra is _________.
[latex]{[{D}'+A{B}'+{A}'C+A{C}'D+{A}'{C}'{D}]}'[/latex]
questions.solution:
Simplify inside the bracket:
- [latex]A\bar CD+\bar A\bar CD=\bar CD[/latex], and [latex]\bar D+\bar CD=\bar D+\bar C[/latex]
- [latex]\bar C+\bar AC=\bar C+\bar A[/latex]
- [latex]\bar A+A\bar B=\bar A+\bar B[/latex]

Inside = [latex]\bar A+\bar B+\bar C+\bar D[/latex], so its complement = ABCD, a single minterm.

Answer: 1

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Let [latex]f(x)=x^{-(1/3)}[/latex] and A denote the area of the region bounded by f(x) and the x-axis, when x varies from -1 to 1. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
I) f is continuous in [-1,1]
II) f is not bounded in [-1,1]
III) A is nonzero and finite
questions.solution:
[latex]f(x)=x^{-1/3}[/latex] blows up at x = 0, so it is not continuous (I false) and not bounded (II true) on [[latex]-[/latex]1, 1].

Area = [latex]2\int_0^1x^{-1/3}dx=2\cdot\frac32=3[/latex], finite and non-zero (III true).

Answer: II and III only

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Perform the following operations on the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 4&45 \\ 7& 9& 105\\ 13&2 & 195 \end{bmatrix}[/latex].
(i) Add the third row to the second row
(ii) Subtract the third column from the first column.
The determinant of the resultant matrix is___________.
questions.solution:
Adding a row to another row, or subtracting a column from another column, does not change the determinant.

In the original matrix the third column is 15 times the first (45 = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 3, 105 = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 7, 195 = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 13), so the determinant is 0.

Answer: 0

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: The number of onto functions (surjective functions) from set x={1,2,3,4} to set Y={a,b,c} is __________.
questions.solution:
Inclusion-exclusion for onto functions from 4 to 3 elements:

[latex]3^4-\binom31 2^4+\binom32 1^4=81-48+3=36[/latex]

Answer: 36

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let X and Y denote the sets containing 2 and 20 distinct objects respectively and F denote the set of all possible functions defined from X to Y. Let f be randomly chosen from F. The probability of f being one-to-one is ________.
questions.solution:
Total functions = [latex]20^2=400[/latex]. One-to-one functions = 20 [latex]\times[/latex] 19 = 380.

Probability = 380 / 400 = 0.95

Answer: 0.95

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the alphabet [latex]\Sigma[/latex]={0, 1}, the null/empty string [latex]\lambda[/latex] and the sets of strings [latex]X_{0}, X_{1}, \; and \; X_{2}[/latex] generated by the corresponding non-terminals of a regular grammar. [latex]X_{0}, X_{1}, \; and \; X_{2}[/latex] are related as follows.
[latex]X_{0}=1X_{1}[/latex]
[latex]X_{1},=0X_{1}+1 X_{2}[/latex]
[latex]X_{2}=0X_{1}+ \{\lambda\}[/latex]
Which one of the following choices precisely represents the strings in [latex]X_{0}[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Substitute [latex]X_2[/latex] into [latex]X_1[/latex]:
[latex]X_1=0X_1+1(0X_1+\lambda)=(0+10)X_1+1[/latex]

By Arden's rule [latex]X_1=(0+10)^*1[/latex], so [latex]X_0=1(0+10)^*1[/latex].

Answer: 1(0 + 10)*1

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: A graph is self-complementary if it is isomorphic to its complement. For all self-complementary graphs on n vertices, n is
questions.solution:
A graph and its complement have equal edges, so each has half of [latex]\binom n2[/latex]: [latex]\frac{n(n-1)}{4}[/latex] must be an integer.

This holds only when n [latex]\equiv[/latex] 0 or 1 (mod 4).

Answer: Congruent to 0 mod 4, or 1 mod 4

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: In a connected graph, a bridge is an edge whose removal disconnects a graph. Which one of the following statements is true?
options: A bridge cannot be part of a simple cycle
Every edge of a clique with size [latex]\geq[/latex] 3 is a bridge (A clique is any complete subgraph of a graph)
A graph with bridges cannot have a cycle
questions.solution:
If an edge were on a cycle, the rest of the cycle would still connect its ends after removing it, so it would not be a bridge.

- Every edge of a tree is a bridge.
- Clique edges (size [latex]\ge[/latex] 3) lie on triangles, so they are not bridges.
- A graph can have both bridges and cycles.

Answer: A bridge cannot be part of a simple cycle

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Which one of the following well formed formulae is a tautology?
options: [latex](\forall x[\exists yR(x,y)\rightarrow S(x,y)])\rightarrow \forall x\exists y S(x,y)[/latex]
[latex][\forall x\exists yP(x,y)\rightarrow R(x,y)]\leftrightarrow [\forall x\exists y(\neg P(x,y))\vee R(x,y)][/latex]
[latex]\forall x \forall y P(x,y) \rightarrow \forall x\forall y P(y,x)[/latex]
questions.solution:
Option 3: [latex]P\rightarrow R\equiv\neg P\vee R[/latex], and both sides apply the same quantifiers to equivalent formulas [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] tautology.

- Option 1: [latex]\forall x\exists y[/latex] does not imply [latex]\exists y\forall x[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not a tautology.
- Option 2: fails, e.g. when nothing satisfies R.

Note: option 4 is also logically valid (the bound variables are only renamed). The official key is option 3.

Answer: Option 3

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.text: Which one of the following assertions concerning code inspection and code walkthrough is true?
options: Code inspection is carried out once the code has been unit tested
Code inspection and code walkthrough are synonyms
Adherence to coding standards is checked during code inspection
Code walkthrough is usually carried out by an independent test team
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Inspection is done before unit testing [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] option 1 false.
- Inspection (formal, checklist based) and walkthrough (informal, led by the author) are different [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] option 2 false.
- Inspections check against checklists including coding standards [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- Walkthroughs are done by the development team, not an independent test team [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] false.

Answer: Adherence to coding standards is checked during code inspection

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: A half adder is implemented with XOR and AND gates. A full Combinational Circuit is implemented with two half Combinational Circuits and one OR gate. The propagation delay of an XOR gate is twice that of an AND/OR gate. The propagation delay of an AND/OR gate is 1.2 microseconds. A 4-bit ripple-carry binary Combinational Circuit is implemented by using four full Combinational Circuits. The total propagation time of this 4-bit binary Combinational Circuit in microseconds is____________.
questions.solution:
XOR = 2.4 [latex]\mu s[/latex], AND = OR = 1.2 [latex]\mu s[/latex].

Carry out of one full adder: XOR (first half adder) + AND (second half adder) + OR = 2.4 + 1.2 + 1.2 = 4.8 [latex]\mu s[/latex].

Taking each of the 4 ripple stages as 4.8 [latex]\mu s[/latex]: 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 4.8 = 19.2 [latex]\mu s[/latex] (as per the official key).

Answer: 19.2

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: We __________ our friends's birthday and we _________ how to make it up to him.
questions.solution:
The adverb "completely" goes before the verb: "completely forgot". "Just" goes before "don't know": "just don't know".

Answer: completely forgot --- just don't know

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Choose the statement where underlined word is used correctly.
options: I write my experience in my [latex]\underline{ \text{personnel }}[/latex] diary.
All [latex]\underline{ \text{personnel} }[/latex] are being given the day off.
questions.solution:
Personnel = the staff of an organisation. Personal = belonging to one person.

Only "All personnel are being given the day off" uses it correctly.

Answer: All personnel are being given the day off

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Consider a function [latex]f(x) = 1- |x| \text{ on } -1 \leq x \leq 1[/latex]. The value of [latex]x[/latex] at which the function attains a maximum, and the maximum value of the function are:
questions.solution:
|x| is smallest (0) at x = 0, so f(x) = 1 [latex]-[/latex] |x| is largest there: f(0) = 1.

Answer: 0, 1

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: A generic term that includes various items of clothing such as a skirt, a pair of trousers and a shirt is
questions.solution:
Apparel is the general word for clothing (skirts, trousers, shirts). Fabric, textile and fiber are materials.

Answer: apparel

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Based on the given statements, select the most appropriate option to solve the given question.
What will be the total weight of 10 poles each of same weight?

Statements:
I. One fourth of the weight of the pole is 5 Kg.
II. The total weight of these poles is 160 Kg more than the total weight of two poles.
options: Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Either I or II alone is sufficient.
Both statements I and II together are not sufficient.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: weight = 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 20 kg [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] total = 200 kg. Sufficient.
- II: 10w = 2w + 160 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] w = 20 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] total = 200 kg. Sufficient.

Answer: Either I or II alone is sufficient

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
If the list of letters [latex]P, R, S, T, U[/latex] is an arithmetic sequence, which of the following are also in arithmetic sequence?
I. [latex]2P,2R,2S,2T,2U[/latex]
II. [latex]P-3,R-3,S-3,T-3,U-3[/latex]
III. [latex]P^2, R^2, S^2, T^2, U^2[/latex]
questions.solution:
If the common difference is d:
- I: doubling gives common difference 2d [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] AP
- II: subtracting 3 keeps difference d [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] AP
- III: squares, e.g. 1, 2, 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1, 4, 9 (differences 3, 5) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not AP

Answer: I and II

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Four branches of a company are located at M, N, O and P. M is north of N at a distance of 4km; P is south of O at a distance of 2 km; N is southeast of O by 1km. What is the distance between M and P in km?
questions.solution:
Take O = (0, 0). Then P = (0, [latex]-[/latex]2) and N = (0.707, [latex]-[/latex]0.707) (1 km south-east). M is 4 km north of N: M = (0.707, 3.293).

MP = [latex]\sqrt{0.707^2+5.293^2}=\sqrt{0.5+28.02}\approx5.34[/latex] km

Answer: 5.34

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: In a triangle [latex]PQR,PS[/latex] is the angle bisector of [latex]\angle QPR \text{ and } \angle QPS =60^\circ[/latex]. What is the length of [latex]PS[/latex] ?
questions.solution:
[latex]\angle QPR=120^\circ[/latex]. Area of PQR = area of PQS + area of PSR:

[latex]\frac12 rq\sin120^\circ=\frac12 r\cdot PS\sin60^\circ+\frac12 q\cdot PS\sin60^\circ[/latex]

Since [latex]\sin120^\circ=\sin60^\circ[/latex]: [latex]rq=PS(r+q)\Rightarrow PS=\frac{qr}{q+r}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac{qr}{q+r}[/latex]

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
If p, q, r, s are distinct integers such that:[latex]f(p,q,r,s)= max (p,q,r,s)[/latex]
[latex]g(p,q,r,s)= min (p,q,r,s) [/latex]
[latex]h (p, q, r, s) = \text {remainder of } \frac{(p \times q)} {(r \times s)} \text{ if } (p \times q) \gt (r \times s)[/latex]
[latex]\text{ or remainder of } \frac {(r \times s)}{(p \times q)} \text{ if } (r \times s) \gt (p \times q)[/latex]

Also a function [latex]fgh(p,q,r,s)=f(p,q,r,s) \times g(p,q,r,s) \times h(p,q,r,s)[/latex]
Also the same operations are valid with two variable functions of the form [latex]f(p,q)[/latex]
What is the value of [latex]fg(h(2,5,7,3),4,6,8)[/latex]?
questions.solution:
h(2, 5, 7, 3): p [latex]\times[/latex] q = 10, r [latex]\times[/latex] s = 21. 21 [latex]\gt[/latex] 10, so h = 21 mod 10 = 1.

fg(1, 4, 6, 8) = max [latex]\times[/latex] min = 8 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 = 8

Answer: 8

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Out of the following 4 sentences, select the most suitable sentence with respect to grammar and usage:
options: Since the report lacked needed information, it was of no use to them.
The report was useless to them because there were no needed information in it.
Since the report did not contain the needed information, it was not real useful to them.
Since the report lacked needed information, it would not had been useful to them.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Option 2: "information" is uncountable, so "were no" is wrong.
- Option 3: "real useful" should be "really useful".
- Option 4: "would not had been" should be "would not have been".

Option 1 is correct.

Answer: Since the report lacked needed information, it was of no use to them

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
p = s1 + 2 points to s1[2] (the character '3'). *p = '0' changes it to '0'.

s1 becomes "1204" (the string still ends at the original '\0').

Answer: 1204

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Suppose U is the power set of the set S={1,2,3,4,5,6}. For any T[latex]\in[/latex]U, let |T| denote the number of elements in T and T' denote the complement of T. For any T,R[latex]\in[/latex]U, let T\R be the set of all elements in T which are not in R. Which one of the following is true?
options: [latex]\exists X\in U \; \exists Y\in U \; [/latex] [latex](|X|=5,\; |Y|=5 \; and \;  X \cap  Y=\phi )[/latex]
[latex]\forall X\in U \; \forall Y\in U \;[/latex] [latex] (|X|=2,\; |Y|=3 \; and \; X \setminus  Y=\phi )[/latex]
[latex]\forall X \in U \; \forall Y\in U\; (X \setminus  Y=Y' \setminus  X')[/latex]
questions.solution:
[latex]X\setminus Y=X\cap Y'[/latex] and [latex]Y'\setminus X'=Y'\cap X[/latex]. These are the same set for every X, Y.

- Option 1 fails for X = {1}.
- Option 2: two 5-element subsets of a 6-element set must overlap.
- Option 3 is not true for all X, Y.

Answer: [latex]\forall X\,\forall Y\,(X\setminus Y=Y'\setminus X')[/latex]

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the relation X(P,Q,R,S,T,U) with the following set of functional dependencies
F= {{P,R}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{S,T}, {P,S,U}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{Q,R} }
Which of the following is the trivial functional dependency in [latex]F^{+}[/latex], where [latex]F^{+}[/latex] is closure of F ?
questions.solution:
A dependency is trivial when its right side is a subset of its left side.

{S} [latex]\subseteq[/latex] {P, S}, so {P, S} [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {S} is trivial. In option 2, T is not in {P, R}.

Answer: {P, S} [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {S}

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: The maximum number of processes that can be in Ready state for a computer system with n CPUs is
questions.solution:
The number of CPUs limits how many processes can be running. Any number of processes can wait in the ready queue.

Answer: Independent of n

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text: Among simple LR (SLR) , canonical LR, and look-ahead LR (LALR), which of the following pairs identify the method that is very easy to implement and the method that is the most powerful , in that order?
questions.solution:
SLR uses LR(0) items with FOLLOW sets, so it is the simplest. Canonical LR(1) has the most states and recognises the largest class of grammars (most powerful). LALR lies in between.

Answer: SLR, canonical LR

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
Let # be a binary operator defined as
X#Y=X'+Y' where X and Y are Boolean variables.
Consider the following two statements.

(S1) (P # Q) # R = P # (Q # R)
(S2) Q # R = R # Q

Which of the following is/are true for the Boolean variables P, Q and R?
options: Both S1 and S2 are true
Neither S1 nor S2 are true
questions.solution:
X # Y = X' + Y' = (XY)', i.e. NAND.

- S2: NAND is commutative [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- S1: (P # Q) # R = PQ + R', while P # (Q # R) = P' + QR. Different (e.g. P = 0, R = 1) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: Only S2 is true

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.text:
Consider a software project with the following information domain characteristics for calculation of function point metric.
Number of external inputs (I) = 30
Number of external outputs (O) = 60
Number of external inquiries (E) = 23
Number of files (F) = 08
Number of external interfaces (N) = 02

It is given that the complexity weighting factors for I, O, E, F and N are 4, 5, 4, 10 and 7, respectively. It is also given that, out of fourteen value adjustment factors that influence the development effort, four factors are not applicable, each of the other four factors have value 3, and each of the remaining factors have value 4. The computed value of function point metric is _____________.
questions.solution:
UFP = 30 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 + 60 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 + 23 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 + 8 [latex]\times[/latex] 10 + 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 7 = 120 + 300 + 92 + 80 + 14 = 606

Sum of factors = 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 0 + 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 + 6 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 = 36

FP = 606 [latex]\times[/latex] (0.65 + 0.01 [latex]\times[/latex] 36) = 606 [latex]\times[/latex] 1.01 = 612.06

Answer: 612.06

questions.subject: Web Technology
questions.text: In a web server, ten WebPages are stored with the URLs of the form http://www.yourname.com/var.html; where, var is a different number from 1 to 10 for each Webpage. Suppose, the client stores the Webpage with var =1 (say W1) in local machine, edits and then tests. Rest of the WebPages remains on the web server. W1 contains several relative URLs of the form "var.html" referring to the other WebPages. Which one of the following statements needs to be added in W1, so that all the relative URLs in W1 refer to the appropriate WebPages on the web server?
questions.solution:
The HTML base tag sets the base URL for all relative links in the page. With base href = "http://www.yourname.com/", the link "var.html" points to the page on the server.

Answer: base href: "http://www.yourname.com/"

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
I. TCP connections are full duplex
II. TCP has no option for selective acknowledgement
III. TCP connections are message streams
options: Only I and III are correct
Only II and III are correct
All of I, II and III are correct
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: TCP connections are full duplex [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II: TCP has a SACK (selective acknowledgement) option [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- III: TCP is a byte stream, not a message stream [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: Only I is correct

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Consider the equality [latex]\sum_{i=0}^{n}i^{3}=X[/latex] and the following choices for X
I.[latex] \Theta (n^{4}) [/latex]
II. [latex] \Theta (n^{5}) [/latex]
III. [latex]O (n^{5}) [/latex]
IV. [latex] \Omega (n^{3})[/latex]
The equality above remains correct if X is replaced by
options: I or III or IV but not II
II or III or IV but not I
questions.solution:
[latex]\sum_{i=0}^n i^3=\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)^2=\Theta(n^4)[/latex]

A [latex]\Theta(n^4)[/latex] function is also [latex]O(n^5)[/latex] and [latex]\Omega(n^3)[/latex], but it is not [latex]\Theta(n^5)[/latex].

Answer: I or III or IV but not II

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: Consider a binary tree T that has 200 leaf nodes. Then, the number of nodes in T that have exactly two children are ________.
questions.solution:
In any binary tree, the number of nodes with two children = leaves [latex]-[/latex] 1.

200 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 199

Answer: 199

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Given a hash table T with 25 slots that stores 2000 elements, the load factor [latex]\alpha[/latex] for T is ____________.
questions.solution:
Load factor [latex]\alpha=\frac{n}{m}=\frac{2000}{25}=80[/latex]

Answer: 80

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: In the given matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1&2 \\ 0& 1 & 0\\ 1&2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex], one of the eigenvalues is 1. The eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue 1 are
questions.solution:
[latex]A-I=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1&2\\0&0&0\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix}[/latex]

- Row 1: [latex]-[/latex]y + 2z = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] y = 2z
- Row 3: x + 2y = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = [latex]-[/latex]4z

z = 1 gives ([latex]-[/latex]4, 2, 1).

Answer: [latex]\alpha(-4,2,1)[/latex]

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: The value of [latex]\lim_{x\rightarrow \infty }(1+x^{2})^{e^{-x}}[/latex] is
questions.solution:
Take logs: [latex]\ln L=\lim e^{-x}\ln(1+x^2)=\lim\frac{\ln(1+x^2)}{e^x}=0[/latex] (the exponential grows much faster).

So [latex]L=e^0=1[/latex].

Answer: 1

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: The number of 4 digit numbers having their digits in non-decreasing order (from left to right) constructed by using the digits belonging to the set {1, 2, 3} is____________.
questions.solution:
A non-decreasing number is fixed once we know how many 1s, 2s and 3s it has. So count solutions of a + b + c = 4 with [latex]a,b,c\ge0[/latex]:

[latex]\binom{4+2}{2}=15[/latex]

Answer: 15

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
In a room there are only two types of people, namely Type 1 and Type 2. Type 1 people always tell the truth and Type 2 people always lie. You give a fair coin to a person in that room, without knowing which type he is from and tell him to toss it and hide the result from you till you ask for it. Upon asking, the person replies the following

"The result of the toss is head if and only if I am telling the truth."

Which of the following options is correct?
options: If the person is of Type 2, then the result is tail
If the person is of Type 1, then the result is tail
questions.solution:
Let H = "result is head".

- Type 1 (truthful): the statement is true and he is telling the truth, so H [latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] True gives H.
- Type 2 (liar): the statement is false and he is not telling the truth. "H [latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] False" is false only when H is true.

Either way the result is head.

Answer: The result is head

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: While inserting the elements 71, 65, 84, 69, 67, 83 in an empty binary search tree (BST) in the sequence shown, the element in the lowest level is
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- 71 root; 65 left, 84 right
- 69: right of 65; 67: left of 69 (level 3)
- 83: left of 84 (level 2)

The deepest element is 67.

Answer: 67

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: The result evaluating the postfix expression 10    5  +  60     6   /  *  8 -   is
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- 10 5 + [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 15
- 60 6 / [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10
- * [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 150
- 8 [latex]-[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 142

Answer: 142

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the following relation

Cinema(theater, address, capacity)

Which of the following options will be needed at the end of the SQL query

SELECT P1.address FROM Cinema P1

such that it always finds the addresses of theaters with maximum capacity?
options: WHERE P1.capacity [latex]\geq[/latex] All (select P2.capacity from Cinema P2)
WHERE P1.capacity [latex]\geq[/latex] Any (select P2.capacity from Cinema P2)
WHERE P1.capacity [latex]\gt[/latex] All (select max(P2.capacity) from Cinema P2)
WHERE P1.capacity [latex]\gt[/latex] Any (select max(P2.capacity) from Cinema P2)
questions.solution:
A theater has maximum capacity when its capacity is [latex]\ge[/latex] every capacity in the table, i.e. [latex]\ge[/latex] ALL.

[latex]\ge[/latex] ANY returns every theater. [latex]\gt[/latex] ALL (max) / [latex]\gt[/latex] ANY (max) returns nothing.

Answer: WHERE P1.capacity [latex]\ge[/latex] All (select P2.capacity from Cinema P2)

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
Consider the following array of elements.
(89,19,50,17,12,15,2,5,7,11,6,9,100)
The minimum number of interchanges needed to convert it into a max-heap is
questions.solution:
Only 100 (at the last position) breaks the heap property. It sifts up:

- swap with parent 15
- swap with parent 50
- swap with root 89

Everything else already satisfies the max-heap rule, so 3 interchanges.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
Two processes X and Y need to access a critical section. Consider the following synchronization construct used by both the processes

Here, varP and varQ are shared variables and both are initialized to false. Which one of the following statements is true?
options: The proposed solution prevents deadlock but fails to guarantee mutual exclusion
The proposed solution guarantees mutual exclusion but fails to prevent deadlock
The proposed solution guarantees mutual exclusion and prevents deadlock
The proposed solution fails to prevent deadlock and fails to guarantee mutual exclusion
questions.solution:
Suppose X sets varP = true and Y sets varQ = true. Now both while conditions are true, so both enter the critical section at the same time [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] mutual exclusion fails.

Neither process ever blocks waiting for the other (the critical section is inside the loop, not after a busy-wait), so there is no deadlock.

Answer: prevents deadlock but fails to guarantee mutual exclusion

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text: Let L be the language represented by the regular expression [latex]\Sigma ^{*}0011\Sigma ^{*}[/latex] where [latex]\Sigma[/latex]={0,1}. What is the minimum number of states in a DFA that recognizes [latex]\bar{L}[/latex] (complement of L)?
questions.solution:
A DFA for "contains 0011" tracks progress: nothing, 0, 00, 001, 0011 (trap accepting) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 states.

The complement uses the same DFA with final and non-final states swapped, so it also needs 5 states.

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Software Engineering
questions.text: Consider a software program that is artificially seeded with 100 faults. While testing this program, 159 faults are detected, out of which 75 faults are from those artificially seeded faults. Assuming that both real and seeded faults are of same nature and have same distribution, the estimated number of undetected real faults is ____________.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Seeded faults found: 75 of 100 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] detection rate 0.75
- Real faults found: 159 [latex]-[/latex] 75 = 84
- Estimated real faults = 84 / 0.75 = 112

Undetected = 112 [latex]-[/latex] 84 = 28

Answer: 28

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: Consider a machine with a byte addressable main memory of [latex]2^{20}[/latex]  bytes, block size of 16 bytes and a direct mapped cache having [latex]2^{12}[/latex] cache lines. Let the addresses of two consecutive bytes in main memory be [latex](E201F)_{16}[/latex] and [latex](E2020)_{16}[/latex]. What are the tag and cache line address (in hex) for main memory address [latex](E201F)_{16}[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Address = 20 bits: offset = 4 bits (16-byte block), line = 12 bits ([latex]2^{12}[/latex] lines), tag = 20 [latex]-[/latex] 16 = 4 bits.

E201F = E | 201 | F [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] tag = E, line = 201

Answer: E, 201

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Consider a CSMA/CD network that transmits data at a rate of 100 Mbps ([latex]10^{8}[/latex] bits per second) over a 1 km (kilometer) cable with no repeaters. If the minimum frame size required for this network is 1250 bytes, what is the signal speed (km/sec) in the cable?
questions.solution:
CSMA/CD needs [latex]T_t\ge2T_p[/latex]:
[latex]\frac{1250\times8}{10^8}=100\,\mu s=2T_p\Rightarrow T_p=50\,\mu s[/latex]

Speed = 1 km / 50 [latex]\mu s[/latex] = 20000 km/s

Answer: 20000

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
The velocity v (in kilometer/minute) of a motorbike which starts from rest, is given at fixed intervals of time t (in minutes) as follows:

The approximate distance (in kilometers) rounded to two places of decimals covered in 20 minutes using Simpson's [latex]1/3^{rd}[/latex] rule is _______________.
questions.solution:
The bike starts from rest, so v = 0 at t = 0. With h = 2 we have 11 points:
v = 0, 10, 18, 25, 29, 32, 20, 11, 5, 2, 0

- Odd positions: 10 + 25 + 32 + 11 + 2 = 80
- Even (inner) positions: 18 + 29 + 20 + 5 = 72

[latex]D=\frac{h}{3}[v_0+v_{10}+4(80)+2(72)]=\frac23(0+0+320+144)=309.33[/latex]

Answer: 309.33

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Assume that a mergesort algorithm in the worst case takes 30 seconds for an input of size 64. Which of the following most closely approximates the maximum input size of a problem that can be solved in 6 minutes?
questions.solution:
Mergesort time [latex]\propto n\log n[/latex]. For n = 64: 64 [latex]\times[/latex] 6 = 384 units in 30 s.

6 minutes = 12 [latex]\times[/latex] 30 s [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 12 [latex]\times[/latex] 384 = 4608 units.

n = 512: 512 [latex]\times[/latex] 9 = 4608 [latex]\checkmark[/latex]

Answer: 512

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
Let C(n) = number of calls made by get(n). C(n) = 1 for n [latex]\lt[/latex] 1, else C(n) = 1 + C(n[latex]-[/latex]1) + C(n[latex]-[/latex]3).

- C(1) = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3
- C(2) = 1 + 3 + 1 = 5
- C(3) = 1 + 5 + 1 = 7
- C(4) = 1 + 7 + 3 = 11
- C(5) = 1 + 11 + 5 = 17
- C(6) = 1 + 17 + 7 = 25

Answer: 25

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text: Consider a B+ tree in which the search key is 12 bytes long, block size is 1024 bytes, record pointer is 10 bytes long and block pointer is 8 bytes long. The maximum number of keys that can be accommodated in each non-leaf node of the tree is ____________.
questions.solution:
A non-leaf node with n block pointers holds n [latex]-[/latex] 1 keys:

[latex]8n+12(n-1)\le1024\Rightarrow20n\le1036\Rightarrow n=51[/latex]

Keys = 51 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 50

Answer: 50

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
Given the function F=P'+QR , where F is a function in three Boolean variables P,Q and R and P'=!P, consider the following statements.
(S1) F=[latex]\Sigma[/latex](4,5,6)
(S2) F=[latex]\Sigma[/latex](0,1,2,3,7)
(S3) F=[latex]\Pi[/latex](4,5,6)
(S4) F=[latex]\Pi[/latex](0,1,2,3,7)
Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
F = P' + QR is 1 for P = 0 (minterms 0, 1, 2, 3) and for P = Q = R = 1 (minterm 7).

- [latex]F=\Sigma(0,1,2,3,7)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S2 True, S1 False
- Maxterms are the rest: [latex]F=\Pi(4,5,6)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] S3 True, S4 False

Answer: (S1) False, (S2) True, (S3) True, (S4) False

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Language [latex]L_{1}[/latex] is polynomial time reducible to language [latex]L_{2}[/latex]. Language [latex]L_{3}[/latex] is polynomial time reducible to [latex]L_{2}[/latex], which in turn is polynomial time reducible to language [latex]L_{4}[/latex]. Which of the following is/are true?
I. if [latex]L_{4} \in P[/latex], then [latex]L_{2} \in P[/latex]
II. if [latex]L_{1} \in P[/latex] or [latex]L_{3} \in P[/latex], then [latex]L_{2} \in P[/latex]
III. [latex]L_{1} \in P[/latex], if and only if [latex]L_{3} \in P[/latex]
IV. if [latex]L_{4} \in P[/latex], then [latex]L_{1} \in P[/latex] and [latex]L_{3} \in P[/latex]
questions.solution:
Reductions: [latex]L_1\le L_2[/latex], [latex]L_3\le L_2\le L_4[/latex]. If the target is in P, the source is in P.

- I: [latex]L_4\in P\Rightarrow L_2\in P[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- IV: then [latex]L_1, L_3\in P[/latex] too [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II and III would need reductions in the other direction [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not implied

Answer: I and IV only

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Which of the following languages are context-free?
[latex]L_{1}=\{a^{m}b^{n}a^{n}b^{m}|m,n\geq 1\}[/latex]
[latex]L_{2}=\{a^{m}b^{n}a^{m}b^{n}|m,n\geq 1\}[/latex]
[latex]L_{3}=\{a^{m}b^{n}|m=2n+1\}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1=a^mb^na^nb^m[/latex]: nested matching (outer m, inner n) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] push a's, push b's, pop on a's, pop on b's [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL.
- [latex]L_2=a^mb^na^mb^n[/latex]: crossed matching, which one stack cannot do [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not CFL.
- [latex]L_3=a^{2n+1}b^n[/latex]: push for a's, pop for b's [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL.

Answer: L1 and L3 only

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
Consider the following policies for preventing deadlock in a system with mutually exclusive resources.
I. Processes should acquire all their resources at the beginning of execution. If any resource is not available, all resources acquired so far are released
II. The resources are numbered uniquely, and processes are allowed to request for resources only in increasing resource numbers
III. The resources are numbered uniquely, and processes are allowed to request for resources only in decreasing resource numbers
IV. The resources are numbered uniquely. A process is allowed to request only for a resource with resource number larger than its currently held resources
Which of the above policies can be used for preventing deadlock?
options: Any one of I and III but not II or IV
Any one of I, III, and IV but not II
Any one of II and III but not I or IV
Any one of I, II, III, and IV
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I removes hold-and-wait (all or nothing).
- II, III and IV each impose a single global order on requests (increasing or decreasing), which removes circular wait.

All four prevent deadlock.

Answer: Any one of I, II, III, and IV

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: In the network 200.10.11.144/27, the fourth octet (in decimal) of the last IP address of the network which can be assigned to a host is ____________.
questions.solution:
/27 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] blocks of 32 addresses. 144 lies in the block 128 to 159.

159 is the broadcast address, so the last usable host is 158.

Answer: 158

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Consider a network connecting two systems located 8000 kilometers apart. The bandwidth of the network is 500x[latex]10^{6}[/latex] bits per second. The propagation speed of the media is 4x[latex]10^{6}[/latex] meters per second. It is needed to design a Go-Back-N sliding window protocol for this network. The average packet size is [latex]10^{7}[/latex] bits. The network is to be used to its full capacity. Assume that processing delays at nodes are negligible. Then, the minimum size in bits of the sequence number field has to be ___________.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]T_p=\frac{8\times10^6}{4\times10^6}=2[/latex] s
- [latex]T_t=\frac{10^7}{5\times10^8}=0.02[/latex] s

Window for full use = [latex]1+\frac{2T_p}{T_t}=1+200=201[/latex]. Go-Back-N needs at least W + 1 = 202 sequence numbers.

[latex]2^8=256\ge202[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 bits

Answer: 8

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
Consider the following reservation table for a pipeline having three stages S1,S2 and S3.

The minimum average latency (MAL) is ________.
questions.solution:
Forbidden latencies: S1 is used at 1 and 5 (gap 4); S2 at 2 and 4 (gap 2). Forbidden = {2, 4}, collision vector = 1010.

- Latency 3 again and again: CV stays 1011 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] cycle (3), average 3
- Cycle (1, 5): average 3

MAL = 3

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
Consider the following code sequence having five instructions I1 to I5. Each of these instructions has the following format.

OP Ri, Rj, Rk

where operation OP is performed on contents of registers Rj and Rk and the result is stored in register Ri.

I1: ADD R1, R2, R3
I2: MUL R7, R1, R3
I3: SUB R4, R1, R5
I4: ADD R3, R2, R4
I5: MUL R7, R8, R9

Consider the following three statements.
S1: There is an anti-dependence between instructions l2 and l5
S2: There is an anti-dependence between instructions l2 and l4
S3: Within an instruction pipeline an anti-dependence always creates one or more stalls

Which one of above statements is/are correct?
options: Only S1 and S3 are true
Only S2 and S3 are true
questions.solution:
Anti-dependence (WAR): a later instruction writes a register an earlier one reads.

- S1: I2 and I5 both write R7, which is output dependence, not anti [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- S2: I2 reads R3 and I4 writes R3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] anti-dependence [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- S3: in an in-order pipeline WAR causes no stall [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: Only S2 is true

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
options: Only S1 and S2 are correct
Only S1 and S3 are correct
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: segment 1 adds X[0][i] = i, and segment 2 adds X[i][0] = i. Same Y [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- S2: X[0][0], X[0][1], ... are one row, contiguous in row-major order [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- S3: X[0][0], X[1][0], ... are n elements apart [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: Only S1 and S2 are correct

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the following partial Schedule S involving two transactions T1 and T2. Only the read and the write operations have been shown. The read operation on data item P is denoted by read(P) and the write operation on data item P is denoted by write(P).

Suppose that the transaction T1 fails immediately after time instance 9. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: T2 must be aborted and then both T1 and T2 must be re-started to ensure transaction atomicity
Schedule S is non-recoverable and cannot ensure transaction atomicity
Only T2 must be aborted and then re-started to ensure transaction atomicity
Schedule S is recoverable and can ensure atomicity and nothing else needs to be done
questions.solution:
T2 reads A (time 7) after T1 wrote it (time 2), and T2 commits at time 8 before T1 commits.

When T1 fails, T2 has already committed using a value of A that must be rolled back. Its effects cannot be undone, so S is non-recoverable.

Answer: Schedule S is non-recoverable and cannot ensure transaction atomicity

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
If the following system has non-trivial solution,
px+qy+rz=0
qx+ry+pz=0
rx+py+qz=0,
then which one of the following options is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Non-trivial solution needs determinant = 0:

[latex]\begin{vmatrix}p&q&r\\q&r&p\\r&p&q\end{vmatrix}=-(p+q+r)(p^2+q^2+r^2-pq-qr-rp)=0[/latex]

The second factor is [latex]\frac12[(p-q)^2+(q-r)^2+(r-p)^2][/latex], zero only when p = q = r.

Answer: p + q + r = 0 or p = q = r

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: If for non-zero  [latex]x,af(x)+bf\left ( \frac{1}{x} \right )=\frac{1}{x}-25[/latex] where [latex] a\neq b[/latex]  then [latex] \int_{1}^{2}f(x)dx[/latex] is
questions.solution:

Integrate from 1 to 2: [latex]a\ln2-25a-\frac{3b}{2}+25b=a(\ln2-25)+\frac{47b}{2}[/latex]

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Let G be a connected undirected graph of 100 vertices and 300 edges. The weight of a minimum spanning tree of G is 500. When the weight of each edge of G is increased by five, the weight of a minimum spanning tree becomes ________.
questions.solution:
Every spanning tree has 99 edges, so each tree's weight rises by exactly 99 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 495. The same tree stays minimum.

500 + 495 = 995

Answer: 995

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Two hosts are connected via a packet switch with [latex]10^{7}[/latex] bits per second links. Each link has a propagation delay of 20 microseconds. The switch begins forwarding a packet 35 microseconds after it receives the same. If 10000 bits of data are to be transmitted between the two hosts using a packet size of 5000 bits, the time elapsed between the transmission of the first bit of data and the reception of the last bit of the data in microseconds is____________.
questions.solution:
Each packet: [latex]T_t=\frac{5000}{10^7}=500\,\mu s[/latex], propagation 20 [latex]\mu s[/latex], switch delay 35 [latex]\mu s[/latex].

- Packet 1: sent 0-500, at switch by 520, forwarded 555-1055, received by 1075
- Packet 2: sent 500-1000, at switch by 1020, forwarded 1055-1555, received by 1575

Answer: 1575

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: For the processes listed in the following table, which of the following scheduling schemes will give the lowest average turnaround time?
options: Round Robin with Quantum value two
questions.solution:
Average turnaround time:

- FCFS: A 0-3, B 3-9, C 9-13, D 13-15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (3 + 8 + 9 + 9)/4 = 7.25
- Non-preemptive SJF: A, B, D, C [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (3 + 8 + 5 + 11)/4 = 6.75
- SRT: A 0-3, B 3-4, C 4-8, D 8-10, B 10-15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (3 + 14 + 4 + 4)/4 = 6.25
- RR (q = 2) is higher than SRT

Answer: Shortest Remaining Time

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: Consider the equation [latex](43)_{x}=(y3)_{8}[/latex] where x and y are unknown. The number of possible solutions is ______________
questions.solution:
[latex](43)_x=4x+3,\quad(y3)_8=8y+3\Rightarrow x=2y[/latex]

Digit 4 needs x [latex]\ge[/latex] 5 and y must be an octal digit (0 to 7). So y = 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 solutions.

Answer: 5

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let R be a relation on the set of ordered pairs of positive integers such that [latex]((p,q),(r,s)) \in R[/latex] if and only if [latex]p-s=q-r[/latex]. Which one of the following is true about R?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Reflexive needs p [latex]-[/latex] q = q [latex]-[/latex] p, i.e. p = q. Fails for (1, 2) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not reflexive.
- Symmetric: ((r,s),(p,q)) needs r [latex]-[/latex] q = s [latex]-[/latex] p, which rearranges to p [latex]-[/latex] s = q [latex]-[/latex] r [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] symmetric.

Answer: Not reflexive but symmetric

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Suppose [latex]X_{i}[/latex] for i =1,2,3 are independent and identically distributed random variables whose probability mass functions are [latex]Pr[X_{i}=0]=Pr[X_{i}=1]=1/2[/latex] for i=1,2,3. Define another random variable [latex]Y=X_{1}X_{2}\oplus X_{3}, \; where \; \oplus[/latex] denotes XOR. Then
[latex]Pr[Y=0|X_{3}=0]=[/latex]_______________.
questions.solution:
If [latex]X_3=0[/latex], then [latex]Y=X_1X_2[/latex]. Y = 0 unless both are 1.

P = 1 [latex]-[/latex] 1/4 = 0.75

Answer: 0.75
