questions.text: The total number of prime implicants of the function f(w,x,y,z)=[latex]\Sigma[/latex](0,2,4,5,6,10) is _______.

Minterms 0, 2, 4, 5, 6, 10. From the K-map, the prime implicants are:

- [latex]\bar wx\bar y[/latex] (4, 5)
- [latex]\bar xy\bar z[/latex] (2, 10)

Suppose c=(c[0],...,c[k-1]) is an array of length k, where all the entries are from the set {0,1}. For any positive integers a and n, consider the following pseudocode.

If k=4, c=(1,0,1,1), a=2 and n=8, then the output of DOSOMETHING(c,a,n) is _____.

z = 1, a = 2, n = 8, c = (1, 0, 1, 1):

- i = 1: z = 4, c = 0

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Let [latex]f(n)=n[/latex] and [latex]g(n)=n^{1+sin \; n}[/latex] where n is a positive integer. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. [latex]f(n)=O(g(n)) [/latex]
II. [latex]f(n)= \Omega (g(n))[/latex]
questions.solution:
[latex]g(n)=n^{1+\sin n}[/latex], and 1 + sin n keeps swinging between about 0 and 2. So g(n) is sometimes near 1 (much smaller than n) and sometimes near [latex]n^2[/latex] (much larger).

Neither bound holds for all large n.

Answer: Neither I nor II

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text:
Consider the following grammar
S [latex] \rightarrow[/latex] F|H
F [latex] \rightarrow[/latex] p|c
H [latex] \rightarrow[/latex] d|c
where S,F, and H are non-terminal symbols, p,d, and c are terminal symbols. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
S1. LL(1) can parse all strings that are generated using grammar G
S2. LR(1) can parse all strings that are generated using grammar G
questions.solution:
The string "c" has two derivations: [latex]S\Rightarrow F\Rightarrow c[/latex] and [latex]S\Rightarrow H\Rightarrow c[/latex]. So the grammar is ambiguous.

No ambiguous grammar is LL(1) or LR(1).

Answer: Neither S1 nor S2

questions.text:
Alexander turned his attention towards India, since he had conquered Persia.

Which one of the statements below is logically valid and can be inferred from the above sentence?

Alexander was not ready to rest on his laurels, and wanted to march to India.
Alexander was not completely in control of his army and could command it to move towards India.
Since Alexander's kingdom extended to Indian borders after the conquest of Persia, he was keen to move further.

questions.text:

Most experts feel that in spite of possessing all the technical skills required to be a batsman of the highest order, he is unlikely to be so due to lack of requisite temperament. questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Let p,q, r, s represent the following propositions.

p: x[latex]\in[/latex]{8,9,10,11,12}
q: x is a composite number
r: x is a perfect square
s: x is a prime number

The integer x[latex]\geq[/latex]2 which satisfies [latex]\neg((p\Rightarrow q)\wedge (\neg r \vee \neg s))[/latex] is ________.
questions.solution:
[latex] eg((p\Rightarrow q)\wedge( eg r\vee eg s))\equiv(p\wedge eg q)\vee(r\wedge s)[/latex]

- [latex]r\wedge s[/latex] (perfect square and prime) is impossible.
- So we need [latex]p\wedge eg q[/latex]: x in {8, 9, 10, 11, 12} and not composite. Only 11 qualifies.

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let [latex]a_{n}[/latex] be the number of n-bit strings that do NOT contain two consecutive 1s. Which one of the following is the recurrence relation for [latex]a_{n}[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Look at the first bit of a valid n-bit string:
- starts with 0: the rest is any valid (n [latex]-[/latex] 1)-bit string [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]a_{n-1}[/latex]
- starts with 1: the next bit must be 0, then any valid (n [latex]-[/latex] 2)-bit string [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]a_{n-2}[/latex]

[latex]a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}[/latex]

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: [latex]\lim_{x\rightarrow 4}\frac{sin(x-4)}{x-4}[/latex]=_________.
questions.solution:
Put [latex]t=x-4\rightarrow0[/latex]: [latex]\lim_{t\to0}\frac{\sin t}{t}=1[/latex].

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
A probability density function on the interval [a,1] is given by 1/[latex]x^{2}[/latex]
 and outside this interval the value of the function is zero.The value of a is __________.
questions.solution:
Total probability must be 1:
[latex]\int_a^1\frac{1}{x^2}dx=\left[-\frac1x\right]_a^1=\frac1a-1=1\Rightarrow a=\frac12[/latex]

Answer: 0.5

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Two eigen values of a 3x3 real matrix P are (2+[latex]\sqrt{-1}[/latex]) and 3.The determinantof P is __________.
questions.solution:
A real matrix has complex eigenvalues in conjugate pairs, so [latex]2-i[/latex] is the third eigenvalue.

[latex]\det P=(2+i)(2-i)\times3=(4+1)\times3=15[/latex]

Answer: 15

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
Consider the Boolean operator with the following properties:
[latex]x \# 0=x, x \# 1=\bar{x}[/latex], [latex]x \# x=0[/latex] and [latex]x \# \bar{x}=1[/latex]. Then [latex]x \# y[/latex] is equivalent to
questions.solution:
[latex]x\#0=x[/latex], [latex]x\#1=\bar x[/latex], [latex]x\#x=0[/latex], [latex]x\#\bar x=1[/latex]: these are exactly the properties of XOR.

[latex]x\#y=x\bar y+\bar xy[/latex]

Answer: [latex]x\bar y+\bar xy[/latex]

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: The 16 bit 2's complement representation of an integer is 1111 1111 1111 0101;   its decimal representation is__________ .
questions.solution:
The MSB is 1, so the number is negative. Take the 2's complement of 1111 1111 1111 0101:
invert [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0000 0000 0000 1010, add 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0000 0000 0000 1011 = 11.

Answer: -11

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: We want to design a synchronous counter that counts these quence 0-1-0-2-0-3 and then repeats. The minimum number of J-K flip flop srequired to implement this counteris ________.
questions.solution:
The sequence 0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 3 has 6 steps, and the three 0s are followed by different numbers, so the counter needs 6 different internal states.

6 states need [latex]\lceil\log_2 6\rceil=3[/latex] flip-flops (the output is then decoded from the state).

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: A processor can support a maximum memory of 4GB, where the memory is word-addressable (a word consists of two bytes). The size of the address bus of the process or is at least bits________.
questions.solution:
4 GB = [latex]2^{32}[/latex] bytes. One word = 2 bytes, so there are [latex]2^{31}[/latex] words.
Word addressable [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]2^{31}[/latex] addresses [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 31 address bits.

Answer: 31

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: A queue is implemented using an array such that ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE operations are performed efficiently. Which one of the following statements is CORRECT (n refers to the number of items in the queue)?
options: Both operations can be performed in O(1) time

At most one operation can be performed in O(1) time but the worst case time for
the other operation will be [latex]\Omega[/latex](n)
The worst case time complexity for both operations will be [latex]\Omega[/latex](n)
Worst case time complexity for both operations will be [latex]\Omega[/latex](logn)
questions.solution:
Use a circular array with front and rear indices: ENQUEUE writes at rear and moves it, DEQUEUE reads at front and moves it (both modulo the array size). No shifting is needed, so both are [latex]O(1)[/latex].

Answer: Both operations can be performed in O(1) time

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Consider the following directed graph:

The number of different topological orderings of the vertices of the graph is
questions.solution:
a must come first and f last. In between, b must come before c, and d before e, but the two chains are independent.

Number of ways to interleave b c with d e = [latex]\binom42=6[/latex].

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
f takes (int, short) and returns void.
- f(s, *s): s is a short, not a pointer, so *s is invalid.
- i = f(i, s): f returns void, so it cannot be assigned.
- f(i, *s): again *s is invalid.
- f(i, *p): i is int, *p is the short s True

Answer: f(i,*p)

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: The worst case running times of Insertion sort, Mergesort and Quicksort, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Insertion sort worst case (reverse sorted): [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex]
- Merge sort is always [latex]\Theta(n\log n)[/latex]
- Quicksort worst case (bad pivots every time): [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n^2),\Theta(n\log n),\Theta(n^2)[/latex]

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Let G be a weighted connected undirected graph with distinct positive edge weights. If every edge weight is increasedby the same value ,then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
P: Minimum spanning tree of G does not change
Q: Shortest path between any pair of vertices does not change
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- P: adding the same value to every edge keeps their relative order, so Kruskal picks the same edges [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] the MST does not change [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Q: a path with more edges gains more. E.g. a path 1 + 1 = 2 vs a direct edge 3 becomes 11 + 11 = 22 vs 13 (adding 10) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] shortest paths can change [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: P only

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
mystery only swaps its local pointer copies (ptra, ptrb); it never changes *ptra or *ptrb. So a, b, c, d in main never change.

a is still 2016.

Answer: 2016

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Which of the following languages is generated by the given grammar?
[latex]S\rightarrow aS|bS|\varepsilon[/latex]
options: {[latex]\{w\in \{a,b\}^*| w [/latex] has equal number of a's and b's}
questions.solution:
[latex]S\rightarrow aS\mid bS\mid\varepsilon[/latex] adds any a or b at each step, in any order and any number of times, so it generates every string over {a, b}, including [latex]\varepsilon[/latex].

Answer: {a,b}*

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Which of the following decision problems are undecidable?
I. Given NFAs N1 and N2, is L(N1)[latex]\cap[/latex]L(N2) = [latex]\phi[/latex]?
II. Given a CFG G = (N,[latex]\Sigma [/latex],P,S) and a string [latex]x \in\Sigma ^*[/latex], does [latex]x \in[/latex] L(G)?
III. Given CFGs G1 and G2, is L(G1) = L(G2)?
IV. Given a TM M, is L(M) = [latex]\phi[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: NFA intersection emptiness: build the product automaton and check reachability [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decidable.
- II: CFG membership: CYK algorithm [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decidable.
- III: equivalence of two CFGs [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.
- IV: emptiness of a TM's language (Rice) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.

Answer: III and IV only

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text: Which one of the following regular expressions represents the language: the set of all binary strings having two consecutive 0s and two consecutive 1s?
questions.solution:
The string must contain "00" somewhere and "11" somewhere, in either order:
[latex](0+1)^*\big(00(0+1)^*11+11(0+1)^*00\big)(0+1)^*[/latex] True

- Option 1 forces 00 and 11 to be adjacent (0011 or 1100).
- Option 3 needs only one of them.
- Option 4 forces them at the very start and end.

Answer: Option 2

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text:
Consider the following code segment.
x =u-t;
y =x*v;
x =y+w;
y =t-z;
y =x*y;
The minimum number of total variables required to convert the above code segment to static single assignment form is__________ .
questions.solution:
In SSA form every assignment gets a new variable:
[latex]x_1=u-t;\ y_1=x_1v;\ x_2=y_1+w;\ y_2=t-z;\ y_3=x_2y_2[/latex]

New variables: [latex]x_1,y_1,x_2,y_2,y_3[/latex] (5), plus the inputs u, t, v, w, z (5).

Total = 10

Answer: 10

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
Consider an arbitrary set of CPU-bound processes with unequal CPU burst lengths
submitted at the same time to a computer system.Which one of the following process scheduling algorithms would minimize the average waiting time in the ready queue?
options: Round-robin with time quantum less than the shortest CPU burst
Highest priority first with priority proportional to CPU burst length
questions.solution:
All processes arrive together, so shortest remaining time first behaves like SJF, which is optimal for average waiting time. Round robin, random order or "long jobs first" make short jobs wait longer.

Answer: Shortest remaining time first

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Which of the following is NOT a superkey in a relational schema with attributes
V,W, X, Y, Z and primary key V Y?
questions.solution:
A superkey must contain the whole primary key {V, Y}.
VWXZ has V but no Y [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not a superkey. The others all contain both V and Y.

Answer: VWXZ

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the ACID properties of database transactions?
questions.solution:
ACID = Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability. Deadlock-freedom is not one of them.

Answer: Deadlock-freedom

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
A database of resear charticles in a journal uses the following schema.

Which is the weakest normal form that the new database satisfies,but the old one does not?
questions.solution:
Old schema: key (VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE), and (VOLUME, NUMBER) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] YEAR is a partial dependency (part of the key determines a non-key attribute) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] only 1NF.

New schemas: YEAR moves to (VOLUME, NUMBER, YEAR), so the partial dependency is gone [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2NF (in fact both are in BCNF).

The weakest form the new one satisfies but the old one does not is 2NF.

Answer: 2NF

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Which one of the following protocols is NOT used to resolve one form of address to another one?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- DNS: hostname [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] IP
- ARP: IP [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] MAC
- RARP: MAC [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] IP
- DHCP assigns IP configuration to hosts; it does not translate one address form into another.

Answer: DHCP

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
Which of the following is/are example(s) of stateful application layer protocols?
(i) HTTP
(ii) FTP
(iii) TCP
(iv) POP3
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- HTTP is stateless (each request is independent).
- FTP keeps session state (login, current directory) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] stateful.
- TCP is a transport protocol, not application layer.
- POP3 keeps session state (authorization, transaction states) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] stateful.

Answer: (ii) and (iv) only

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: The coefficient of [latex]x^{12}[/latex] in [latex](x^{3}+x^{4}+x^{5}+x^{6}+. . . )^{3}[/latex] is ______.
questions.solution:
[latex](x^3+x^4+\cdots)^3=x^9(1+x+x^2+\cdots)^3=x^9(1-x)^{-3}[/latex]

We need the coefficient of [latex]x^3[/latex] in [latex](1-x)^{-3}[/latex]: [latex]\binom{3+2}{2}=10[/latex].

Answer: 10

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Consider the recurrence relation [latex]a_{1}[/latex]=8, [latex]a_{n}=6n^{2}+2n+a_{n-1}[/latex]. Let [latex]a_{99}= K  \times  10^{4}[/latex]. The value of K is .
questions.solution:
Since [latex]a_1=8=6+2[/latex], [latex]a_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}(6k^2+2k)=n(n+1)(2n+1)+n(n+1)=2n(n+1)^2[/latex].

[latex]a_{99}=2\times99\times100^2=1980000=198\times10^4[/latex]

Answer: 198

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
A function [latex]f:\mathbb{N}^{+}\rightarrow \mathbb{N}^{+}[/latex], defined on the set of positive integers [latex]\mathbb{N}^{+}[/latex], satisfies the following properties:
f(n)=f(n/2) if n is even
f(n)=f(n+5) if n is odd
Let R={[latex]i|\exists j:f(j)=i[/latex]} be the set of distinct values that f takes. The maximum possible size of R is ____.
questions.solution:
Both rules keep a number inside its class:
- If n is a multiple of 5, n/2 (when even) and n + 5 are still multiples of 5.
- If n is not a multiple of 5, neither are n/2 and n + 5.

Within each class all values are linked (e.g. 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1, and 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5), so f can take at most one value per class: at most 2 values.

Answer: 2

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider the following experiment.
Step 1. Flip a fair coin twice.
Step 2. If the outcomes are(TAILS, HEADS) then output Y and stop.
Step 3. If the outcomes are either(HEADS, HEADS) or(HEADS, TAILS), then output N and stop.
Step 4. If the out comes are(TAILS, TAILS), then go to Step1.
The probability that the output of the experiment is Y is (up to two decimal places)_____.
questions.solution:
In each round of two flips: Y with probability 1/4 (TH), N with 1/2 (HH or HT), repeat with 1/4 (TT).

[latex]P(Y)=\frac{1/4}{1/4+1/2}=\frac13\approx0.33[/latex]

Answer: 0.33

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
Consider the two cascaded 2-to-1 multiplexers as shown in the figure.

The minimal sum of products form of the output X is
questions.solution:
First mux (select P): output = R if P = 1, else 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] PR.
Second mux (select Q): X = PR if Q = 1, else [latex]\bar R[/latex].

[latex]X=\bar Q\bar R+QPR[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\bar Q\bar R+PQR[/latex]

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: The size of the data count register of a DMA controller is 16 bits.The processor needs to transfer a file of 29,154 kilobytes from disk to main memory.The memory is byte addressable. The minimum number of times the DMA control lerneeds to get the control of the systembus from the processor to transfer the file from the disk to main memory is ____.
questions.solution:
A 16-bit count register lets the DMA move at most [latex]2^{16}[/latex] bytes = 64 KB each time it takes the bus.

[latex]\lceil29154/64\rceil=\lceil455.5\rceil=456[/latex]

Answer: 456

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: The stage delays in a 4-stage pipeline are 800,500,400 and 300 picoseconds.The first stage (with delay 800 picoseconds)is replaced with a functionally equivalent design involving two stages with respective delays 600 and 350 picoseconds.The throughput increase of the pipeline is ________ percent.
questions.solution:
Throughput is 1 / (slowest stage).
- Before: max delay 800 ps.
- After: stages 600, 350, 500, 400, 300 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] max 600 ps.

Increase [latex]=\frac{1/600-1/800}{1/800}=\frac{800}{600}-1=33.3\%[/latex]

Answer: 33.33

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Consider a carry lookahead adder for adding two n-bit integers,built using gates of fan-in at most two. The time to perform addition using this adder is
questions.solution:
Carry lookahead computes all carries from the generate/propagate signals. With gates of fan-in 2, combining n signals needs a tree of depth [latex]\log_2 n[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(\log n)[/latex]

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
Two pointers start at the ends; each step discards the smaller of p[a] and p[b] (the maximum is never discarded). The loop must stop when only one candidate is left, i.e. when a and b meet.

Loop condition: b != a.

Answer: b != a

questions.solution:

- count(3): prints 3, 1; d = 2; calls count(2)

- count(1): prints 1, 3; d = 4; prints 4

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
Read "a = 1" in m as declaring a local a of m. y refers to the global a (= 3).
- m: local a = 1, then a = y [latex]-[/latex] a = 3 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 2.
- n(a): x refers to m's local a. With dynamic scoping, the a inside n is also m's a (the most recent active a). x = x [latex]\times[/latex] a = 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 4, and since x is that same a, a becomes 4. Prints 4.
- Back in m: print(a) prints 4.

Answer: 4,4

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: An operator delete(i) for a binary heap data structure is to be designed to delete the item in the i-th node.Assume that the heap is implemented in an array and i refers to the i-th index of thearray.If the heap tree has depth d (number of edges on the path from the root to the farthest leaf),the n what is the time complexity to re-fix the heap efficiently after the removal of the element?
questions.solution:
To delete node i: move the last element into position i, then either sift it up or down. Either way it moves along one root-to-leaf path, at most d levels [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(d)[/latex]. It can take that long, so it is not [latex]O(1)[/latex].

Answer: O(d) but not O(1)

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Consider the weighted undirected graph with 4 vertices,where the weigh to edge {i, j} is given by the entry Wij in the matrix W.
[latex]W=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2&8 & 5\\ 2& 0& 5 &8 \\ 8 & 5 & 0& x\\ 5&8 & x&0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
The largest possible integer value of x, for which at least one shortest path between some pair of vertices will contain the edge with weight x is ____.
questions.solution:
Without edge {3, 4}, the shortest path from 3 to 4 is 3-2-1-4 = 5 + 2 + 5 = 12.

The edge of weight x lies on a shortest path (at least one, possibly tied) only if [latex]x\le12[/latex]. The largest integer is 12.

Answer: 12

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Let G be a complete undirected graph on 4 vertices, having 6 edges  with weights being 1,2,3,4,5, and 6. The maximum possible weight that a minimum weight spanning tree of G can haveis .
questions.solution:
An MST of 4 vertices has 3 edges; edges 1 and 2 are always taken (two edges cannot form a cycle).

To make the third edge as heavy as possible, put edges 1, 2, 3 in a triangle, so 3 is rejected. The 4th vertex must then be joined by the next lightest edge, 4.

Maximum MST weight = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7

Answer: 7

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
G = (V,E) is an undirected simple graph in which each edge has a distinct weight,and e is a particular edgeof G. Which of the following statements about the minimum spanning trees (MSTs) of G is/are TRUE?
I. If e is the lightest edge of some cycle in G, then every MST of G includes e
II. If e is the heaviest edge of some cycle in G, then every MST of G excludes e
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: the lightest edge of one cycle can still be the heaviest edge of another cycle and be excluded [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: cycle property: with distinct weights, the heaviest edge of any cycle is in no MST [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: II only

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
Let Q denote a queue containing sixteen numbers and S be an empty stack. Head(Q) returns the element at the head of the queue Q without removing it from Q. Similarly Top(S) returns the element at the top of S without removing it from S. Consider the algorithm given below.

The maximum possible number of iterations of the while loop in the algorithm is_________.
questions.solution:
The loop keeps the stack in sorted order, sending larger stack tops back to the queue. The worst case is when the queue is in decreasing order: every element has to be cycled between the stack and the queue many times.

For n elements the worst case is [latex]n^2[/latex] iterations (check n = 2 with queue [2, 1]: 4 iterations). For n = 16: [latex]16^2=256[/latex].

Answer: 256

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the following context-free grammars:

G1: S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]aS|B,
B[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]b|bB
G2: S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]aA|bB,
A[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]aA|B|[latex]\varepsilon[/latex],
B[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]bB|[latex]\varepsilon[/latex]

Which one of the following pair of languages is generated by G1 and G2, respectively?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- G1: [latex]S\rightarrow aS\mid B[/latex], [latex]B\rightarrow b\mid bB[/latex] gives [latex]a^*b^+[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\{a^mb^n\mid m\ge0,\ n \gt 0\}[/latex].
- G2: aA gives [latex]a^+b^*[/latex] and bB gives [latex]b^+[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\{a^mb^n\mid m \gt 0\text{ or }n \gt 0\}[/latex].

Answer: Option 4

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the transition diagram of a PDA given below with input alphabet [latex]\Sigma [/latex]={a,b} and stack alphabet [latex]\Gamma[/latex]={X,Z}. Z is the initial stack symbol. Let L denote the language accepted by the PDA.

Which one of the following is TRUE?
options: [latex]L=\{a^{n}b^{n}|n\geq 0\}[/latex] is not accepted by any finite automata
[latex]L=\{a^{n}|n\geq 0\}\cup \{a^{n}b^{n}|n\geq 0\}[/latex] is not accepted by any deterministic PDA
L is not accepted by any Turing machine that halts one very input
questions.solution:
The PDA pushes an X for every a in the start state (which is final), then pops one X per b, and accepts when only Z is left.
So [latex]L=\{a^n\mid n\ge0\}\cup\{a^nb^n\mid n\ge1\}[/latex], and every move is deterministic [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] L is a deterministic CFL.

Answer: L is deterministic context-free

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text: Let X be a recursive language and Y be a recursively enumerable but not recursive language. Let W and Z be two languages such that [latex]\bar{Y}[/latex]  reduces to W, and Z reduces to [latex]\bar{X}[/latex] (reduction means the standard many-one-reduction). Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: W can be recursively enumerable and Z is recursive.
W can be recursive and Z is recursively enumerable
W is not recursively enumerable and Z is recursive
W is not recursively enumerable and Z is not recursive.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Y is RE but not recursive, so [latex]\bar Y[/latex] is not RE. Since [latex]\bar Y[/latex] reduces to W, W cannot be RE (otherwise [latex]\bar Y[/latex] would be).
- X is recursive, so [latex]\bar X[/latex] is recursive. Z reduces to [latex]\bar X[/latex], so Z is recursive.

Answer: W is not recursively enumerable and Z is recursive

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
The attributes of three arithmetic operators in some programming language are given below.

The value of the expression 2-5+1-7*3 in this language is_______ .
questions.solution:
Precedence: + (highest) [latex]\gt[/latex] [latex]-[/latex] [latex]\gt[/latex] * (lowest). So * is applied last:
[latex](2-5+1-7)*3[/latex]

Inside: + first, 5 + 1 = 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 [latex]-[/latex] 6 [latex]-[/latex] 7. [latex]-[/latex] is right associative: [latex]2-(6-7)=2-(-1)=3[/latex].

[latex]3*3=9[/latex]

Answer: 9

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text:
Consider the following Syntax Directed Translation Scheme(SDTS),with non-terminals {S, A} and terminals {a, b}.
S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] aA {print 1}
S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a { print 2}
A [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Sb { print 3}
Using the above SDTS, the output printed by a bottom-up parser, for the input aab is:
questions.solution:
Parse aab bottom-up:
1. The second a is reduced by [latex]S\rightarrow a[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] prints 2
2. S b is reduced by [latex]A\rightarrow Sb[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] prints 3
3. a A is reduced by [latex]S\rightarrow aA[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] prints 1

Answer: 231

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
Consider a computer system with 40-bit virtual addressing and page size of sixteen
kilobytes. If the computer system has a one level page table per process and each page table entry requires 48 bits, then the size of the per-process page table is _________ mega bytes.
questions.solution:
Entries = [latex]\frac{2^{40}}{2^{14}}=2^{26}[/latex]. Each entry = 48 bits = 6 bytes.

Size [latex]=2^{26}\times6=6\times64\text{ MB}=384[/latex] MB

Answer: 384

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: Consider a disk queue with requests for I/O to blocks on cylinders 47,38,121,191,87,11, 92, 10. The C-LOOK scheduling algorithm is used. The head is initially at cylinder number 63, moving to wards larger cylinder numbers on its servicing pass. The cylinders are numbered from 0to 199. The total head movement (in number of cylinders) incurred while servicing these requests is____ .
questions.solution:
C-LOOK from 63 going up: 87, 92, 121, 191 (movement 191 [latex]-[/latex] 63 = 128), then jump to the lowest request 10 (191 [latex]-[/latex] 10 = 181), then 11, 38, 47 (47 [latex]-[/latex] 10 = 37).

Total = 128 + 181 + 37 = 346

Answer: 346

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: Consider a computer system with ten physical page frames. The system is provided with an accessse quence [latex](a_{1},a_{2},...,a_{20},a_{1},a_{2},...,a_{20})[/latex], where each [latex]a_{i}[/latex] is a distinct virtual page number. The difference in the number of page faults between the last-in-first-outpage replacement policy and the optimal page replacement policy is ______.
questions.solution:
LIFO: the first pass gives 20 faults; a1-a9 stay in memory and the 10th frame keeps getting replaced (ends with a20). Second pass: a1-a9 hit, a10-a20 fault (11). Total 31.

Optimal: 20 faults in the first pass and only 10 in the second (it keeps 10 of the pages needed next). Total 30.

Difference = 31 [latex]-[/latex] 30 = 1

Answer: 1

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
Consider the following proposed solution for the critical section problem. There are n processes: [latex]P_{0}...P_{n-1}[/latex] . In the code,function [latex]pmax[/latex] returns an integer not smaller than any of its arguments. For all i, t[i] is initialized to zero.

Which one of the following is TRUE about the above solution?
options: At most one process can be in the critical section at any time
The bounded wait condition is satisfied
questions.solution:
This is a bakery-style algorithm: a process enters only after every other process with a smaller (non-zero) ticket has finished, so mutual exclusion holds.

But two processes can pick the same ticket (pmax is not atomic). Then each waits for the other (t[j] [latex]\le[/latex] t[i] holds both ways) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] deadlock, so progress and bounded waiting also fail.

Answer: At most one process can be in the critical section at any time

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the following two phase locking protocol. Suppose a transaction T accesses (for read or write operations), a certain set of objects {O1,... ,Ok}. This is done in the following manner:
Step 1. T acquires exclusive locks to O1,...,Ok in increasing order of their addresses.
Step 2. The required operations are performed.
Step 3. All locks are released.
This protocol will
questions.solution:
All locks are taken before any operation and released only at the end [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a two-phase locking schedule [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] serializable.

Locks are always requested in increasing address order, so no circular wait can form [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] deadlock-free.

Answer: guarantee serializability and deadlock-freedom

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
Consider that B wants to send a message m that is digitally signed to A. Let the pair of private and public keys for A and B be denoted by [latex]K_{x}^{-}[/latex]
 and [latex]K_{x}^{+}[/latex] for x = A,B, respectively. Let  [latex]K_{x}(m)[/latex] 
represent the operation of encrypting m with a key [latex]K_{x}[/latex] and H(m) represent the message digest. Which one of the following indicates the CORRECT way of sending the message m along with the digital signature to A?
questions.solution:
B signs by encrypting the digest with B's private key: [latex]K_B^-(H(m))[/latex]. A checks it with B's public key [latex]K_B^+[/latex] and compares with H(m).

Answer: {m, [latex]K_B^-(H(m))[/latex]}

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
An IP datagram of size 1000 bytes arrives at a router. The router has to forward this packet on a link whose MTU (maximum transmission unit)is 100bytes. Assume that the size of the IP header is 20bytes.
The number of fragments that the IP datagram will be divided into for transmission is _________.
questions.solution:
Data = 1000 [latex]-[/latex] 20 = 980 bytes. Per fragment: 100 [latex]-[/latex] 20 = 80 bytes of data (already a multiple of 8).

Fragments = [latex]\lceil980/80\rceil=\lceil12.25\rceil=13[/latex]

Answer: 13

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: For a host machine that uses the token bucket algorithm for congestion control, the token bucket has a capacity of 1 megabyte and the maximum output rate is 20 megabytes per second. Tokens arrive at a rate to sustain output at a rate of 10megabytes per second. The  token bucket is currently full and the machine needs to send 12megabytes of data. The minimum time required to transmit the data is _____seconds.
questions.solution:
Bucket starts full (1 MB). While it drains, the host sends at 20 MB/s while tokens arrive at 10 MB/s:
[latex]20t=1+10t\Rightarrow t=0.1[/latex] s, sending 2 MB.

The remaining 10 MB go at 10 MB/s = 1 s.

Total = 0.1 + 1 = 1.1 s

Answer: 1.1

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
A sender uses the Stop-and Wait ARQ protocol for reliable transmission of frames. Frames are of size 1000bytes and the transmission rate at the sender is 80Kbps(1Kbps=1000 bits/second). Size of anacknowledgement is 100bytes and the transmission rate at the receiver is 8Kbps. The one-way propagation delay is 100milliseconds.
Assuming no frame is lost, the sender throughput is _____bytes/second.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Frame transmission: 8000 bits / 80 Kbps = 0.1 s
- ACK transmission: 800 bits / 8 Kbps = 0.1 s
- Propagation: 0.1 s each way

One frame every 0.1 + 0.1 + 0.1 + 0.1 = 0.4 s [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] throughput = 1000 / 0.4 = 2500 bytes/s

Answer: 2500

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Out of the following four sentences, select the most suitable sentence with respect to grammar and usage.
options: I will not leave the place until the minister does not meet me.
I will not leave the place until the minister doesn't meet me.
I will not leave the place until the minister meet me.
I will not leave the place until the minister meets me.
questions.solution:
"Until" already carries the negative idea, so no "not" after it, and the singular subject "minister" needs "meets".

Answer: I will not leave the place until the minister meets me.

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: rewording of something written or spoken is a __________.
questions.solution:
A paraphrase restates something in different words. (Paradox = self-contradiction, paradigm = model, paraffin = a wax.)

Answer: paraphrase

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Archimedes said, "Give me a lever long enough and a fulcrum on which to place it, and I will move the world."

The sentence above is an example of a ____________ statement.
questions.solution:
Archimedes did not literally plan to move the world; he used the image to show the power of a lever. That is a figurative statement.

Answer: figurative

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: If 'relftaga' means carefree, 'otaga' means careful and 'fertaga' means careless, which of the following could mean 'aftercare'?
questions.solution:
From the words: taga = care, and the modifier comes before taga: relf-taga = free + care (carefree), o-taga = ful + care, fer-taga = less + care.

In "aftercare", after comes before care in English, so in this code it comes after taga: taga + (after). Only "tagazen" has that form.

Answer: tagazen

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: A cube is built using 64 cubic blocks of side one unit. After it is built, one cubic block is removed from every corner of the cube. The resulting surface area of the body (in square units) after the removal is ________.
questions.solution:
The 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 cube has surface area 6 [latex]\times[/latex] 16 = 96.

Removing a corner block removes 3 outer unit faces but exposes 3 new unit faces inside the notch. So the area does not change.

Answer: 96

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
A shaving set company sells 4 different types of razors- Elegance, Smooth, Soft and Executive.
Elegance sells at Rs. 48, Smooth at Rs. 63, Soft at Rs. 78 and Executive at Rs. 173 per piece. The table below shows the numbers of each razor sold in each quarter of a year.

[latex]\begin{array}{|c|r|r|r|r|} \hline \textbf{Quarter/Product} & \textbf{Elegance} &\textbf{Smooth} &\textbf{Soft} & \textbf{Executive}\\\hline \text{Q1} & \text{27300} &\text{20009} &\text{17602} &\text{9999}\\\hline \text{Q2} & \text{25222} &\text{19392} & \text{18445}& \text{8942}\\\hline \text{Q3} & \text{28976} &\text{22429} & \text{19544} & \text{10234}\\\hline \text{Q4} &\text{21012} & \text{18229} & \text{16595} & \text{10109}\\\hline \end{array}[/latex]

Which product contributes the greatest fraction to the revenue of the company in that year?
questions.solution:
Yearly revenue = price [latex]\times[/latex] total units:
- Elegance: 48 [latex]\times[/latex] 102510 [latex]\approx[/latex] 49.2 lakh
- Smooth: 63 [latex]\times[/latex] 80059 [latex]\approx[/latex] 50.4 lakh
- Soft: 78 [latex]\times[/latex] 72186 [latex]\approx[/latex] 56.3 lakh
- Executive: 173 [latex]\times[/latex] 39284 [latex]\approx[/latex] 68.0 lakh

Answer: Executive

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Indian currency notes show the denomination indicated in at least seventeen languages. If this is not an indication of the nation's diversity, nothing else is.

Which of the following can be logically inferred from the above sentences?
options: India is a country of exactly seventeen languages.
Linguistic pluralism is the only indicator of a nation's diversity.
Indian currency notes have sufficient space for all the Indian languages.
Linguistic pluralism is strong evidence of India's diversity.
questions.solution:
The sentence says the many languages on the notes are a clear sign of diversity, so linguistic plurality is strong evidence of India's diversity. It does not say exactly 17 languages, or that language is the only indicator.

Answer: Linguistic pluralism is strong evidence of India's diversity.

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Consider the following statements relating to the level of poker play of four players P, Q, R and S.

I. P always beats Q
II. R always beats S
III. S loses to P only sometimes.
IV. R always loses to Q

Which of the following can be logically inferred from the above statements?

(i). P is likely to beat all the three other players
(ii). S is the absolute worst player in the set
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- (i): P beats Q always and S only sometimes; nothing is said about P vs R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] cannot conclude P beats all three.
- (ii): S loses to R, but S sometimes beats P, so S is not clearly the worst; there is also no information on S vs Q.

Answer: neither (i) nor (ii)

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: If [latex]f(x) = 2x^{7}+3x-5[/latex], which of the following is a factor of [latex]f(x)[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Factor theorem: [latex]f(1)=2+3-5=0[/latex], so [latex](x-1)[/latex] is a factor.
(f([latex]-[/latex]1) = [latex]-[/latex]2 [latex]-[/latex] 3 [latex]-[/latex] 5 [latex]\ne[/latex] 0, so x + 1 is not.)

Answer: x-1

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: In a process, the number of cycles to failure decreases exponentially with an increase in load. At a load of 80 units, it takes 100 cycles for failure. When the load is halved, it takes 10000 cycles for failure.The load for which the failure will happen in 5000 cycles is _________
questions.solution:
Let cycles [latex]N=Ae^{-kL}[/latex]. Halving the load from 80 to 40 multiplies N by 100, so [latex]e^{40k}=100[/latex].

From L = 40 (10000 cycles) to 5000 cycles: [latex]e^{k(L-40)}=2\Rightarrow L-40=\frac{40\ln2}{\ln100}=40\times\frac{0.301}{2}=6.02[/latex]

L = 46.02

Answer: 46.02

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider the following expressions:
(i) false
(ii) Q
(iii) true
(iv) [latex]P\vee Q[/latex]
(v) [latex]\neg Q \vee P[/latex]
The number of expressions given above that are logically implied by [latex]P \wedge (P \Rightarrow Q)[/latex] is ________.
questions.solution:
[latex]P\wedge(P\Rightarrow Q)[/latex] means P is true and Q is true. Check each expression with P = Q = true:
- false False
- Q True, true True, [latex]P\vee Q[/latex] True, [latex]\neg Q\vee P[/latex] True

4 expressions are implied.

Answer: 4

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let f(x) be a polynomial and g(x) = f'(x) be its derivative. If the degree of (f(x)+ f(-x)) is 10, then the degree of (g(x)-g(-x)) is ________.
questions.solution:
[latex]f(x)+f(-x)[/latex] keeps only the even powers of f (times 2). Its degree is 10, so f has an [latex]x^{10}[/latex] term (and no higher even power).

[latex]g(x)-g(-x)[/latex] keeps only the odd powers of g = f'. Even powers of f become odd powers of g: [latex]x^{10}\rightarrow10x^9[/latex] is the highest.

Degree = 9

Answer: 9

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: The minimum number of colours that is sufficient to vertex-colour any planar graph is _________.
questions.solution:
By the four colour theorem, every planar graph can be properly coloured with 4 colours, and some (e.g. [latex]K_4[/latex]) need all 4.

Answer: 4

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider the systems,each consisting of m linear equations in n variables.
I. If m [latex]\lt[/latex] n, then all such systems have a solution
II. If m [latex]\gt[/latex] n, then none of these systems has a solution
III. If m = n, then there exists a system which has a solution
Which one of the following is CORRECT?
options: I, II and III are true
Only II and III are true
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: m [latex]\lt[/latex] n does not guarantee a solution: x + y = 1 and x + y = 2 are inconsistent [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: m [latex]\gt[/latex] n systems can have solutions (e.g. the same equation repeated) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- III: with m = n, the homogeneous system Ax = 0 always has x = 0 as a solution [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Only III is true

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Suppose that a shop has an equal number of LED bulbs of two different types. The probability of an LED bulb lasting more than 100 hours given that it is of Type 1 is 0.7, and given that it is of Type 2 is 0.4. The probability that an LED bulb chosen uniformly at random lasts more than 100 hours is _________.
questions.solution:
Both types are equally likely (0.5 each). Total probability:
[latex]P=0.5\times0.7+0.5\times0.4=0.35+0.2=0.55[/latex]

Answer: 0.55

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Suppose that the eigen values of matrix A are 1, 2, 4. The determinant of [latex](A^{-1})^{T}[/latex] is _________.
questions.solution:
[latex]\det A=1\times2\times4=8[/latex]. Transpose does not change the determinant, and [latex]\det(A^{-1})=\frac{1}{\det A}[/latex].

[latex]\det(A^{-1})^T=\frac18=0.125[/latex]

Answer: 0.125

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: Consider an eight-bit ripple-carry Combinational Circuit for computing the sum of A and B, where A and B are integers represented in 2's complement form. If the decimal value of  A is one, the decimal value of B that leads to the longest latency for the sum to stabilize is ________.
questions.solution:
The longest delay happens when a carry is generated at bit 0 and has to ripple through all 8 bits. A = 0000 0001, so B should be all 1s: 1111 1111 = [latex]-[/latex]1.

Answer: -1

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
Let, [latex]x_{1} \oplus x_{2} \oplus
x_{3} \oplus x_{4}=0[/latex] where [latex]x_{1},  x_{2} ,
x_{3} , x_{4}[/latex]  are Boolean variables, and  [latex]\oplus[/latex] is the XOR operator.
Which one of the following must always be TRUE?
questions.solution:
[latex]x_1\oplus x_2\oplus x_3\oplus x_4=0\Rightarrow x_1\oplus x_3=x_2\oplus x_4[/latex].

Complementing both inputs of an XOR does not change it ([latex]\bar a\oplus\bar b=a\oplus b[/latex]), so [latex]\bar x_1\oplus\bar x_3=\bar x_2\oplus\bar x_4[/latex] is always true.

The other options fail for x = 1111 (XOR = 0, but the product is 1, and so on).

Answer: Option 3

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: Let X be the number of distinct 16-bit integers in 2's complement representation. Let Y be the number of distinct 16 bit integers in sign magnitude representation. Then X-Y is ________.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- 2's complement: all [latex]2^{16}[/latex] bit patterns are different numbers.
- Sign-magnitude: +0 and [latex]-[/latex]0 are both zero, so only [latex]2^{16}-1[/latex] distinct numbers.

X [latex]-[/latex] Y = 1

Answer: 1

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: A processor has 40 distinct instructions and 24 general purpose registers. A 32-bit instruction word has an opcode, two register operands and an immediate operand. The number of bits available for the immediate operand field is _______ .
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- 40 instructions [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] opcode [latex]\lceil\log_2 40\rceil=6[/latex] bits
- 24 registers [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 bits each, two operands = 10 bits

Immediate = 32 [latex]-[/latex] 6 [latex]-[/latex] 10 = 16 bits

Answer: 16

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Breadth First Search(BFS) is started on a binary tree beginning from the root vertex. There is a vertex t at a distance four from the root. If t is the n-th vertex in this BFS traversal, then the maximum possible value of n is______ .
questions.solution:
BFS visits level by level. To make t as late as possible, levels 0-3 are full (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 nodes) and t is the last of the 16 nodes at level 4.

n = 15 + 16 = 31

Answer: 31

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
m is a copy of j: m = 10 + 5 = 15. *p is i: i = 5 + 15 = 20. j stays 10.

i + j = 20 + 10 = 30

Answer: 30

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Assume that the algorithms considered here sort the input sequences in ascending order. If the input is already in ascending order, which of the following are TRUE?
I. Quicksort runs in [latex]\Theta (n^{2})[/latex] time
II. Bubblesort runs in [latex]\Theta (n^{2})[/latex] time
III. Merge sort runs in [latex]\Theta (n)[/latex] time
IV. Insertion sort runs in [latex]\Theta (n)[/latex] time
questions.solution:
On already sorted input:
- Quicksort (first/last element as pivot) makes the most unbalanced splits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex] True
- Bubble sort with the "no swap" check stops after one pass [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] False
- Merge sort is always [latex]\Theta(n\log n)[/latex] False
- Insertion sort compares each element once [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] True

Answer: I and IV only

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: The Floyd-Warshall algorithm for all-pair shortest paths computation is based on
options: neither Greedy nor Divide-and-Conquer nor Dynamic Programming paradigm.
questions.solution:
Floyd-Warshall builds [latex]d_k[i][j]=\min(d_{k-1}[i][j],\ d_{k-1}[i][k]+d_{k-1}[k][j])[/latex], reusing answers of smaller subproblems. That is dynamic programming.

Answer: Dynamic Programming paradigm

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
N items are stored in a sorted doubly linked list. For a delete operation, a pointer is provided to the record to be deleted. For a decrease-key operation, a pointer is provided to the record on which the operation is to be performed.
An algorithm performs the following operations on the list in this order: [latex]\Theta(N) \; delete [/latex] , [latex] O(logN) \; insert [/latex], [latex] O(logN) \; find [/latex], and [latex] \Theta(N) \; decrease-key[/latex]. What is the time complexity of all these operations put together?
questions.solution:
In a sorted doubly linked list (pointers given for delete and decrease-key):
- delete: [latex]O(1)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(N)[/latex] in total
- insert: find the position, [latex]O(N)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N\log N)[/latex]
- find: [latex]O(N)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N\log N)[/latex]
- decrease-key: the node may have to move back towards the front, [latex]O(N)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N^2)[/latex]

Total = [latex]O(N^2)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]O(N^2)[/latex]

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
The number of states in the minimum sized DFA that accepts the language defined by the regular expression
(0+1)* (0+1)(0+1)*
is _______.
questions.solution:
[latex](0+1)^*(0+1)(0+1)^*=(0+1)^+[/latex]: every non-empty string. The DFA needs a non-final start state (for [latex]\epsilon[/latex]) and one final state that loops on 0 and 1.

Answer: 2

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Language L1 is defined by the grammar: [latex]S_{1}\rightarrow aS_{1}b|\varepsilon [/latex]
Language L2 is defined by the grammar: [latex]S_{2}\rightarrow abS_{2}|\varepsilon[/latex]
Consider the following statements:
P: L1 is regular
Q: L2 is regular
Which one of the following is TRUE?
options: Both P and Q are true
P is true and Q is false
P is false and Q is true
Both P and Q are false
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1=\{a^nb^n\}[/latex]: needs counting [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not regular (P false).
- [latex]L_2=(ab)^*[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] regular (Q true).

Answer: P is false and Q is true

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the following types of languages: [latex]L_{1}[/latex]:Regular, [latex]L_{2}[/latex]:Context-free, [latex]L_{3}[/latex]:Recursive, [latex]L_{4}[/latex]:Recursively enumerable.
Which of the following is/are TRUE?
I. [latex]\bar{L}_{3}\cup L_{4}[/latex] is recursivelyenumerable
II. [latex]\bar{L}_{2}\cup L_{3}[/latex] is recursive
III. [latex]L_{1}^{*}\cup L_{2}[/latex] is context-free
IV. [latex]L_{1}\cup \bar{L}_{2}[/latex] is context-free
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: [latex]\bar L_3[/latex] is recursive (so RE), and RE is closed under union [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] RE True
- II: a CFL is recursive, so [latex]\bar L_2[/latex] is recursive; union of recursive languages is recursive True
- III: [latex]L_1^*[/latex] is regular (so CFL); CFL [latex]\cup[/latex] CFL is CFL True
- IV: [latex]\bar L_2[/latex] need not be CFL, so the union need not be False

Answer: I, II and III only

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text: Match thefollowing:
options: P[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex]i, Q [latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] ii, R[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] iv,S[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] iii
P[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] iii, Q[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex]i, R[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] ii, S[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] iv
P[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] ii, Q[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] iii, R[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] i, S[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] iv
P[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] iv,Q[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] i, R[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] ii, S[latex]\leftrightarrow[/latex] iii
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- P. Lexical analysis [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (iii) regular expressions (token patterns)
- Q. Top-down parsing [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (i) leftmost derivation
- R. Semantic analysis [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (ii) type checking
- S. Runtime environments [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (iv) activation records

Answer: P-iii, Q-i, R-ii, S-iv

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: In which one of the following page replacement algorithms it is possible for the page fault rate to increase even when the number of allocated frames increases?
questions.solution:
This is Belady's anomaly, which happens with FIFO. LRU, OPT and MRU are stack algorithms: with more frames the set of pages in memory only grows, so faults never increase.

Answer: FIFO

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text: B+ Trees are considered BALANCED because
options: the lengths of the paths from the root to all leaf nodes are all equal.
the lengths of the paths from the root to all leaf nodes differ from each other by at most 1.
the number of children of any two non-leaf sibling nodes differ by at most 1
the number of records in any two leaf nodes differ by at most 1.
questions.solution:
In a B+ tree all leaves are always at the same depth (splits and merges happen at the root level), so every root-to-leaf path has the same length.

Answer: the lengths of the paths from the root to all leaf nodes are all equal

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text: Suppose  a database schedule S involves transactions T1,...,Tn. Construct the precedence graph of S with vertices representing the transactions and edges representing the conflicts. If S is serializable, which one of the following orderings of the vertices of the precedence graph is guaranteed to yield a serial schedule?
questions.solution:
Each edge [latex]T_i\rightarrow T_j[/latex] means [latex]T_i[/latex] must come first. A serializable schedule has an acyclic precedence graph, and any topological order respects every edge, so it gives an equivalent serial schedule.

Answer: Topological order

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Anarkali digitally signs a message and sends it to Salim. Verification of the signature by Salim requires
questions.solution:
Anarkali signs with her private key, so anyone (Salim) verifies with her public key.

Answer: Anarkali's public key

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: In an Ethernet local area network,which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: A station stops to sense the channel once it starts transmitting a frame.
The purpose of the jamming signal is to pad the frames that are smaller than the minimum framesize.
A station continues to transmit the packet even after the collision is detected.

The exponential backoff mechanism reduces the probability of collisionon
retransmissions.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- A station keeps sensing while transmitting (that is how it detects collisions) False
- The jam signal tells everyone a collision happened; padding is something else False
- After a collision the station stops transmitting False
- Exponential backoff makes stations wait random, growing times, so they are less likely to collide again True

Answer: The exponential backoff mechanism reduces the probability of collision on retransmissions

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Identify the correct sequence in which the following packets are transmitted on the network by a host when a browser requests a webpage from a remote server,assuming that the host has just been restarted.
options: HTTP GET request, DNS query, TCP SYN
DNS query, HTTP GET request, TCP SYN
DNS query,TCP SYN, HTTP GET request
TCP SYN, DNS query, HTTP GET request
questions.solution:
After a restart, nothing is cached:
1. DNS query to get the server's IP
2. TCP SYN to open the connection
3. HTTP GET on that connection

Answer: DNS query, TCP SYN, HTTP GET request

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
A binary relation R on [latex]\mathbb{N}\times \mathbb{N}[/latex] is defined as follows: (a,b)R(c,d) if [latex]a \leq c[/latex] or [latex]b \leq d[/latex]. Consider the following propositions:
P: R is reflexive
Q: R is transitive
Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Both P and Q are true
P is true and Q is false.
P is false and Q is true
Both P and Q are false
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Reflexive: (a, b) R (a, b) since [latex]a\le a[/latex] True
- Transitive fails: (3, 2) R (1, 3) because 2 [latex]\le[/latex] 3, and (1, 3) R (2, 1) because 1 [latex]\le[/latex] 2, but (3, 2) R (2, 1) needs 3 [latex]\le[/latex] 2 or 2 [latex]\le[/latex] 1 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] both false.

Answer: P is true and Q is false

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Which one of the following well-formed formulae in predicate calculus is NOT valid?
options: [latex](\forall x p(x)\Rightarrow \forall xq(x))\Rightarrow (\exists x\neg p(x) \vee \forall xq(x))[/latex]
[latex]\forall x (p(x)\vee q(x))\Rightarrow (\forall x p(x) \vee \forall x q(x)) [/latex]
questions.solution:
Option 4 is not valid: take a domain {1, 2} with p(1), q(2) true and p(2), q(1) false. Then every x satisfies p(x) [latex]\vee[/latex] q(x), but neither "all p" nor "all q" holds.

Options 1-3 are standard valid implications.

Answer: Option 4

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider a set U of 23 different compounds in a Chemistry lab. There is a subset S of U of 9 compounds, each of which reacts with exactly 3 compounds of U. Consider the following statements:

I. Each compound in U \ S reacts with an odd number of compounds.
II. At least one compound in U \ S reacts with an odd number of compounds.
III. Each compound in U n S reacts with an even number of compounds.

Which one of the above statements is ALWAYS TRUE?
questions.solution:
Model compounds as vertices and reactions as edges. The sum of all degrees is even (handshake lemma).

The 9 compounds in S have degree 3 each: total 27 (odd). So the degrees of U \ S must add to an odd number, which needs at least one odd degree there. Nothing forces every one to be odd.

Answer: Only II

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: The value of the expression [latex]13^{99}[/latex](mod 17), in the range 0 to 16, is _________.
questions.solution:
[latex]13\equiv-4\pmod{17}[/latex], so [latex]13^2\equiv16\equiv-1[/latex] and [latex]13^4\equiv1[/latex].

[latex]99=4\times24+3\Rightarrow13^{99}\equiv13^3=13^2\cdot13\equiv-13\equiv4\pmod{17}[/latex]

Answer: 4

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: Suppose the functions F and G can be computed in 5 and 3 nano seconds by functional units [latex]U_{F}[/latex] and [latex]U_{G}[/latex], respectively. Given two instances of [latex]U_{F}[/latex] and two instances of [latex]U_{G}[/latex], it is required to implement the computation [latex]F(G(X_{i}))[/latex] for [latex]1\leq i\leq 10[/latex]. Ignoring all other delays, the minimum time required to complete this computation is ________ nanoseconds.
questions.solution:
Each item needs G (3 ns) then F (5 ns). With 2 units of each, the F units are the bottleneck: 10 F computations on 2 units = 5 rounds [latex]\times[/latex] 5 ns = 25 ns.

F can start only after the first G results are ready (3 ns), and the G units keep feeding F in time after that.

Total = 3 + 25 = 28 ns

Answer: 28

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: Consider a processor with 64 registers  and an instruction set of size twelve. Each instruction has five distinct fields, namely, opcode, two source register identifiers, one destination register identifier, and a twelve-bit immediate value. Each instruction must be stored in memory in  byte-aligned fashion. If a program has 100 instructions, the amount of memory(in bytes) consumed by the program text is _____ .
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Opcode: 12 instructions [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 bits
- 3 register fields: 64 registers [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 bits each = 18 bits
- Immediate: 12 bits

Total = 34 bits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] byte-aligned = 5 bytes per instruction. 100 instructions [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 500 bytes.

Answer: 500

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: The width of the physical address on a machine is 40 bits. The width of the tag field in a 512KB 8-way set associative cache is ________ bits.
questions.solution:
One way = 512 KB / 8 = 64 KB = [latex]2^{16}[/latex] bytes, so index + offset = 16 bits.

Tag = 40 [latex]-[/latex] 16 = 24 bits

Answer: 24

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: Consider a 3GHz (gigahertz) processor with a three-stage pipeline and stage latencies [latex]\tau _{1}[/latex], [latex]\tau _{2}[/latex], and [latex]\tau _{3}[/latex] such that [latex]\tau _{1}=3\tau _{2}/4=2\tau _{3}[/latex]. If the longest pipeline stage is split into two pipeline stages of equal latency, the new frequency is _____GHz, ignoring delays in the pipeline registers.
questions.solution:
Let [latex]\tau_1=6k[/latex]: then [latex]\tau_2=8k[/latex] and [latex]\tau_3=3k[/latex]. The clock is set by the longest stage, 8k, at 3 GHz.

Split [latex]\tau_2[/latex] into two stages of 4k. Now the longest is [latex]\tau_1=6k[/latex].

New frequency [latex]=3\times\frac{8k}{6k}=4[/latex] GHz

Answer: 4

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
A complete binary min-heap is made by including each integer in [1,1023] exactly once. The depth of a node in the heap is the length of the path from the root of the heap to that node. Thus, the root is at depth 0. The maximum depth at which integer 9 can appear is_____.
.
questions.solution:
In a min-heap every ancestor of 9 must be smaller than 9. Only 1-8 are smaller, so 9 can have at most 8 ancestors [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] depth at most 8. This is possible: put 1, 2, [latex]\ldots[/latex], 8, 9 down one path (the heap of 1023 nodes has depths 0-9).

Answer: 8

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
Check that [latex]res\cdot a^b[/latex] stays equal to [latex]X^Y[/latex]:
- Start: [latex]1\cdot X^Y[/latex] True
- b even: [latex]a\rightarrow a^2,\ b\rightarrow b/2[/latex], and [latex](a^2)^{b/2}=a^b[/latex] True
- b odd: [latex]res\rightarrow res\cdot a,\ b\rightarrow b-1[/latex], and [latex](res\cdot a)a^{b-1}=res\cdot a^b[/latex] True

When b = 0, res = [latex]X^Y[/latex].

Answer: [latex]X^Y=res*a^b[/latex]

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
Consider the following New-order strategy for traversing a binary tree:
Visit the root;
Visit the right sub tree using New-order;
Visit the left sub tree using New-order;
The New-order traversal of the expression tree corresponding to the reverse polish expression
3 4 * 5 - 2 ^ 6 7 * 1 + - is given by:
questions.solution:
Expression tree of 3 4 * 5 - 2 ^ 6 7 * 1 + - :
root [latex]-[/latex], left = ((3*4) [latex]-[/latex] 5) ^ 2, right = (6*7) + 1.

New-order = root, right subtree, left subtree:
- root: [latex]-[/latex]
- right: + 1 * 7 6
- left: ^ 2 [latex]-[/latex] 5 * 4 3

Answer: - + 1 * 7 6 ^ 2 - 5 * 4 3

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
f returns the largest value of p[i] [latex]-[/latex] p[i+1] over neighbouring pairs (or 0):
3 [latex]-[/latex] 5 = [latex]-[/latex]2, 5 [latex]-[/latex] 2 = 3, 2 [latex]-[/latex] 6 = [latex]-[/latex]4, 6 [latex]-[/latex] 4 = 2

max = 3

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: Let A1,A2,A3, and A4 be four matrices of dimensions 10x5, 5x20, 20x10, and 10x5, respectively. The minimum number of scalar multiplications required to find the product A1A2A3A4 using the basic matrix multiplication method is __________.
questions.solution:
Dimensions 10, 5, 20, 10, 5. Matrix chain DP:
- Pairs: A1A2 = 1000, A2A3 = 1000, A3A4 = 1000
- A2A3A4: (A2A3)A4 = 1000 + 5[latex]\cdot[/latex]10[latex]\cdot[/latex]5 = 1250
- A1A2A3A4: A1((A2A3)A4) = 1250 + 10[latex]\cdot[/latex]5[latex]\cdot[/latex]5 = 1500 (other splits give 3000 and 2000)

Answer: 1500

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: The given diagram shows the flowchart for a recursive function A(n). Assume that all statements, except for the recursive calls,have O(1) Asymptotic Notation. If the worst case Asymptotic Notation of this functionis [latex]O(n^{\alpha })[/latex], then the least possible value(accurate upto two decimal positions) of [latex]\alpha[/latex] is .
questions.solution:
Worst-case path in the flowchart: A(n/2) at the start, then the right branch with two calls, then down with one more call, then the left branch with one more call. That is 5 calls to A(n/2).

[latex]T(n)=5T(n/2)+O(1)\Rightarrow T(n)=O(n^{\log_2 5})=O(n^{2.32})[/latex]

Answer: 2.32

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
The number of ways in which the numbers 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 can be inserted in an empty binary search tree, such that the resulting tree has height 6, is _____.
Note: The height of a tree with a single node is 0.
questions.solution:
Height 6 with 7 nodes means the tree is a single path. After each insertion, the next number must be the smallest or the largest of the numbers still left (2 choices each), and the last number is forced.

[latex]2^6=64[/latex]

Answer: 64

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text: In an adjacency list representation of an undirected simple graph G = (V,E), each edge (u,v) has two adjacency list entries: [v] in the adjacency list of u, and [u] in the adjacency list of v. These are called twins of each other. A twin pointer is a pointer from an adjacency list entry to its twin. If |E|=m and |V|=n, and the memory size is not a constraint, what is the Asymptotic Notation of the most efficient algorithm to set the twin pointer in each entry in each adjacency list?
questions.solution:
Go through all edges once (scanning every adjacency list), using an n [latex]\times[/latex] n table (memory is no problem) to remember where entry [v] in u's list is. When you meet [u] in v's list, look up its twin and link them. Each of the 2m entries is handled once, plus [latex]O(n)[/latex] to scan the lists.

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n+m)[/latex]

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the following two statements:
I. If all states of an NFA are accepting states then the language accepted by the NFA is [latex]\sum ^{*}[/latex] .
II. There exists a regular language A such that for all languages B, A[latex]\cap[/latex]B is regular.
Which one of the following is CORRECT?
options: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: an NFA may simply have no transition for some symbol, so some strings have no path and are rejected even if every state is accepting [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: take [latex]A=\phi[/latex]: [latex]A\cap B=\phi[/latex] is regular for every B [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Only II is true

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the following languages:
[latex]L_{1}=\{a^{n}b^{m}c^{n+m}:m,n\geq 1\}[/latex]
[latex]L_{2}=\{a^{n}b^{n}c^{2n}:n\geq 1\}[/latex]
Which one of the following is TRUE?
options: Both L1 and L2 are context-free.
L1 is context-free while L2 is not context-free.
L2 is context-free while L1 is not context-free.
Neither L1 nor L2 is context-free.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1=a^nb^mc^{n+m}[/latex]: push for every a and b, pop one per c [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] context-free.
- [latex]L_2=a^nb^nc^{2n}[/latex]: needs to match a with b and with c [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not context-free.

Answer: L1 is context-free while L2 is not context-free

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the following languages.
L1 = {[latex]\lt[/latex]M[latex]\gt[/latex] |M takes at least 2016 steps on some input},
L2 = {[latex]\lt[/latex]M[latex]\gt[/latex]| M takes at least 2016 steps on all inputs} and
L3 = {[latex]\lt[/latex]M|M accepts [latex]\varepsilon[/latex]},
where for each Turing machine M, [latex]\lt[/latex]M[latex]\gt[/latex] denotes a specific encoding of M. Which one of the following is TRUE?
options: L1 is recursive and L2,L3 are notrecursive
L2 is recursiveand L1,L3 are notrecursive
L1,L2 are recursiveand L3 is notrecursive
questions.solution:
In 2016 steps a TM reads at most the first 2016 input symbols, so only inputs of length up to 2016 matter. Simulating M on all of them for 2016 steps decides both L1 and L2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] recursive.

L3 (M accepts [latex]\varepsilon[/latex]) is a non-trivial property of L(M) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable (Rice).

Answer: L1, L2 are recursive and L3 is not recursive

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text: Which one of the following grammars is free from left recursion?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Option 1: [latex]A\rightarrow Aa[/latex] is directly left recursive.
- Option 2: S, A, B never start with themselves, directly or indirectly True
- Option 3: [latex]S\rightarrow Aa[/latex] and [latex]A\rightarrow Sc[/latex] give [latex]S\Rightarrow Sca[/latex] (indirect).
- Option 4: [latex]A\rightarrow Bd[/latex] and [latex]B\rightarrow Ae[/latex] give [latex]A\Rightarrow Aed[/latex] (indirect).

Answer: Option 2

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text:
A student wrote two context-free grammars G1 and G2 for generating a single C-like array declaration. The dimension of the array is at least one. For example,
int a[10][3];
The grammars use D as the start symbol,and use six terminal symbols int ;id[]num.

Which of the grammars correctly generate the declaration mentioned above?
questions.solution:
Derive int a[10][3]; with each grammar:
- G1: D [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int L; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id [ E ; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id [ num ] [ E ; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id [num] [num] ; True
- G2: D [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int L; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id E ; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id E [num] ; [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] int id [num] [num] ; True

Both also give one or more dimensions in general.

Answer: Both G1 and G2

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
Consider the following processes, with the arrival time and the length of the CPU burst given in milli seconds.The scheduling algorithm used is preemptive shortest remaining-time first.

The average turn around time of these processes is milliseconds.
questions.solution:
SRTF: P1 0-3 (7 left); P2 arrives (6 [latex]\lt[/latex] 7) and runs 3-7 (2 left); P3 (1) runs 7-8; P2 runs 8-10; P4 runs 10-13; P1 runs 13-20.

Turnaround: P1 20, P2 10 [latex]-[/latex] 3 = 7, P3 8 [latex]-[/latex] 7 = 1, P4 13 [latex]-[/latex] 8 = 5.

Average = 33 / 4 = 8.25

Answer: 8.25

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
Consider the following two-process synchronization solution.


The shared variable turn is initialized to zero.Which one of the following is TRUE?
options: This is a correct two-process synchronization solution.
This solution violates mutual exclusion requirement
This solution violates bounded wait requirement
questions.solution:
This is strict alternation: the processes must take turns. Mutual exclusion holds, but if process 0 wants to enter twice while process 1 does not want to enter at all, process 0 is blocked (turn = 1) by a process that is not even trying. That violates progress.

Answer: This solution violates progress requirement

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: Consider a non-negative counting semaphore S. The operation P(S) decrements S, and V(S) increments S. During an execution, 20 P(S) operations and 12V(S) operations are issued in some order. The largest initial value of S for which at least one P(S) operation will remain blocked is ________.
questions.solution:
With initial value x, the 12 V operations can supply at most 12 more units, so at most x + 12 P operations can succeed. For at least one of the 20 P operations to stay blocked: [latex]x+12 \lt 20\Rightarrow x\le7[/latex].

Answer: 7

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
A file system uses an in-memory cache to cache disk blocks.The miss rate of the cache is shown in the figure. The latency to read a block from the cache is 1 ms and to read a block from the disk is 10ms. Assume that the cost of checking whether a block exists in the cache is negligible. Available cache sizes are in multiples of 10MB.

The smallest cache size required to ensure an average read latency of less than 6ms is_________ MB.
questions.solution:
Average latency = (1 [latex]-[/latex] m) [latex]\times[/latex] 1 + m [latex]\times[/latex] 10 = 1 + 9m (m = miss rate). We need [latex]1+9m \lt 6\Rightarrow m \lt 0.556[/latex].

From the graph: 20 MB gives 60% (too high), 30 MB gives 40% [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] latency 1 + 3.6 = 4.6 ms True

Answer: 30

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the following databases chedule with two transactions, T1 and T2.
[latex]S=r_{2}(X);r_{1}(X);r_{2}(Y);w_{1}(X);r_{1}(Y);w_{2}(X);a_{1};a_{2}[/latex]
where [latex]r_{i}(Z)[/latex] denotes a read operation by transaction [latex]T_{i}[/latex] on avariable Z, [latex]w_{i}(Z)[/latex] denotes a write operation by [latex]T_{i}[/latex] on avariable Z and [latex]a_{i}[/latex] denotes an abort by transaction [latex]T_{i}[/latex].
Which one of the following statements about the above schedule is TRUE?
options: S is recoverable,but has a cascading abort
S does not have a cascading abort
questions.solution:
No transaction reads a value written by the other before it ends: T1 reads X before T2 writes it, and T2's reads happen before T1's write. So when T1 aborts, T2 does not need to be aborted: no cascading abort.

It is not strict, because [latex]w_2(X)[/latex] overwrites [latex]w_1(X)[/latex] while T1 is still active.

Answer: S does not have a cascading abort

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the following database table named water_schemes :

The number of tuples returned by the following SQL query is __________.
questions.solution:
District totals: Ajmer 20, Bikaner 10 + 10 + 20 = 40, Churu 10 + 20 = 30, Dungargarh 10.
Average of totals = (20 + 40 + 30 + 10) / 4 = 25.

Districts with total [latex]\ge[/latex] 25: Bikaner and Churu [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 rows.

Answer: 2

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: A network has a data transmission bandwidth of [latex]20 \times 10^{6}[/latex] bits per second. It uses CSMA/CD in the MAClayer. The maximum signal propagation time from one node to another node is 40 microseconds. The minimum size of a frame in the network is  ______ bytes.
questions.solution:
For CSMA/CD the frame must still be sending when news of a collision returns: [latex]T_t\ge2T_p[/latex].

Min frame = [latex]2\times40\times10^{-6}\times20\times10^6=1600[/latex] bits = 200 bytes

Answer: 200

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
For the IEEE802.11 MAC protocol for wireless communication,which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
I. At least three non-overlapping channels are available for transmissions.
II. The RTS-CTS mechan is misused for collision detection.
III. Unicast frames are ACKed.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: 802.11 (2.4 GHz) has 3 non-overlapping channels (1, 6, 11) True
- II: RTS/CTS is for collision avoidance (hidden terminals); wireless stations cannot detect collisions False
- III: unicast frames are acknowledged True

Answer: I and III only

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Consider a [latex]128 \times 10^{3}[/latex] bits/second satellite communication link with one way propagation delay of 150 milliseconds. Selective retransmission(repeat) protocol is used on this link to send data with a frame size of 1 kilobyte. Neglect the transmission time of acknowledgement. The minimum number of bits required for the sequence number field to achieve 100% utilization is ________.
questions.solution:
Frame = 1 KB = 8192 bits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]T_t=\frac{8192}{128000}=64[/latex] ms. RTT = 300 ms.
For 100% utilization the window must cover [latex]\frac{64+300}{64}\approx5.7[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 frames.

Selective repeat needs window [latex]\le2^{k-1}[/latex]: [latex]2^{k-1}\ge6\Rightarrow k=4[/latex].

Answer: 4

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: The man who is now Municipal Commissioner worked as _____________
options: the security guard at a university
a security guard at the university
the security guard at the university
questions.solution:
He was a security guard (one of several, not a specific one) at the university (the particular university in the context).

Answer: a security guard at the university

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Nobody knows how the Indian cricket team is going to cope with the difficult and seamer-friendly wickets in Australia.

Choose the option which is closest in meaning to the underlined phrase in the above sentence.
questions.solution:
To cope with something means to manage or tolerate it, i.e. to put up with it.

Answer: Put up with

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Find the odd one in the following group of words.

mock, deride, praise, jeer
questions.solution:
Mock, deride and jeer all mean to make fun of someone. Praise is the opposite.

Answer: Praise

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Pick the odd one from the following options.
questions.solution:
Letter positions:
- CADBE = 3, 1, 4, 2, 5 (steps [latex]-[/latex]2, +3, [latex]-[/latex]2, +3)
- JHKIL = 10, 8, 11, 9, 12 (same steps)
- XVYWZ = 24, 22, 25, 23, 26 (same steps)
- ONPMQ = 15, 14, 16, 13, 17 (different steps)

Answer: ONPMQ

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
In a quadratic function, the value of the product of the roots [latex](\\alpha ,\\beta )[/latex] is 4. Find the value of

[latex]\\frac{\\alpha^{n}+\\beta^{n}}{\\alpha^{-n}+\\beta^{-n}}[/latex]
questions.solution:
[latex]\alpha^{-n}+\beta^{-n}=\frac{\alpha^n+\beta^n}{(\alpha\beta)^n}[/latex], so the ratio is [latex](\alpha\beta)^n=4^n[/latex].

Answer: [latex]4^n[/latex]

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Among 150 faculty members in an institute, 55 are connected with each other through Facebook and 85 are connected through Whatsapp. 30 faculty members do not have Facebook or Whatsapp accounts. The numbers of faculty members connected only through Facebook accounts is _______.
questions.solution:
Members with at least one account = 150 [latex]-[/latex] 30 = 120.
Both = 55 + 85 [latex]-[/latex] 120 = 20.
Only Facebook = 55 [latex]-[/latex] 20 = 35.

Answer: 35

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Computers were invented for performing only high-end useful computations. However, it is no understatement that they have taken over our world today. The internet, for example, is ubiquitous. Many believe that the internet itself is an unintended consequence of the original invention. With the advent of mobile computing on our phones, a whole new dimension is now enabled. One is left wondering if all these developments are good or, more importantly, required.
