questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the following context-free grammar where the set of terminals is [latex]\{a,b,c,d,f\}[/latex].

[latex]\begin{array}{lll} S & \rightarrow & d \: a \: T \mid R \: f \\ T & \rightarrow & a \: S \: \mid \: b \: a \: T \: \mid \epsilon \\ R & \rightarrow & c \: a \: T \: R \: \mid \epsilon \end{array}[/latex]

The following is a partially-filled LL(1) parsing table.

Which one of the following choices represents the correct combination for the numbered cells in the parsing table ("blank" denotes that the corresponding cell is empty)?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]FIRST(Rf)=\{c,f\}[/latex] (R can be [latex]\epsilon[/latex]) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (1) [S, c] and (2) [S, f] are both [latex]S\rightarrow Rf[/latex].
- [latex]T\rightarrow\epsilon[/latex] goes in FOLLOW(T). T is followed by R in [latex]R\rightarrow caTR[/latex] (gives c, and FOLLOW(R) = {f}), and FOLLOW(T) includes FOLLOW(S) = {$}. So FOLLOW(T) = {c, f, $}.
- (3) [T, c] = [latex]T\rightarrow\epsilon[/latex] and (4) [T, $] = [latex]T\rightarrow\epsilon[/latex].

Answer: A

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Let [latex]r_i(z)[/latex] and [latex]w_i(z)[/latex] denote read and write operations respectively on a data item [latex]z[/latex] by a transaction [latex]T_i[/latex]. Consider the following two schedules.

[latex]S1: r_1(x)r_1(y)r_2(x)r_2(y)w_2(y)w_1(x)[/latex]
[latex]S2: r_1(x)r_2(x)r_2(y)w_2(y)r_1(y)w_1(x)[/latex]

Which one of the following options is correct?
options: S1 is conflict serializable, and S2 is not conflict serializable
S1 is not conflict serializable, and S2 is conflict serializable
Both S1 and S2 are conflict serializable
Niether S1 nor S2 is conflict serializable
questions.solution:
S1: [latex]r_1(y)[/latex] before [latex]w_2(y)[/latex] gives T1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T2; [latex]r_2(x)[/latex] before [latex]w_1(x)[/latex] gives T2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T1. Cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not conflict serializable.

S2: [latex]r_2(x)[/latex] before [latex]w_1(x)[/latex] gives T2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T1; [latex]w_2(y)[/latex] before [latex]r_1(y)[/latex] gives T2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T1. No cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] conflict serializable (T2, T1).

Answer: S1 is not conflict serializable, and S2 is conflict serializable

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the relation [latex]R(P,Q,S,T,X,Y,Z,W)[/latex] with the following functional dependencies.

[latex]PQ\rightarrow X;\quad P\rightarrow YX;\quad Q\rightarrow Y; \quad Y\rightarrow ZW[/latex]

Consider the decomposition of the relation R into the constituent relations according to the following two decomposition schemes.

[latex]D1:\quad R=[(P,QS,T);\;(P,T,X);\;(Q,Y);\;(Y,Z,W)][/latex]
[latex]D2:\quad R=[(P,Q,S);\;(T,X);\;(Q,Y);\;(Y,Z,W)][/latex]

Which one of the following options is correct?
options: D1 is a lossless decomposition, but D2 is a lossy decomposition.
D1 is a lossy decomposition, but D2 is a lossless decomposition.
Both D1 and D2 are lossless decompositions.
Both D1 and D2 are lossy decompositions.
questions.solution:
D1: join step by step on common attributes that are keys of one side:
- (P, Q, S, T) with (P, T, X) on PT: [latex]P\rightarrow X[/latex] so PT [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] X True
- with (Q, Y) on Q: [latex]Q\rightarrow Y[/latex] True
- with (Y, Z, W) on Y: [latex]Y\rightarrow ZW[/latex] True
So D1 is lossless.

D2: (T, X) shares no attribute with the other relations, so joining it gives a cross product [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] lossy.

Answer: D1 is lossless, but D2 is lossy

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let G be a group of order 6, and H be a subgroup of G such that 1 < |H| < 6. Which one of the following options is correct?
options: Both G and H are always cyclic.
G may not be cyclic, but H is always cyclic.
G is always cyclic, but H may not be cyclic.
Both G and H may not be cyclic.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- G can be the non-abelian group [latex]S_3[/latex] (order 6), which is not cyclic.
- By Lagrange, |H| divides 6 and is strictly between 1 and 6, so |H| = 2 or 3, which are primes. Every group of prime order is cyclic.

Answer: G may not be cyclic, but H is always cyclic

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider the two statements.

S1: There exist random variables [latex]X[/latex] and [latex]Y[/latex] such that [latex]\left(\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E(X))(Y-\mathbb E(Y))]\right)^2 > \textsf{Var}[X]\textsf{Var}[Y][/latex]
S2: For all random variables [latex]X[/latex] and [latex]Y[/latex], [latex]\textsf{Cov}[X,Y]=\mathbb E \left[|X-\mathbb E[X]||Y-\mathbb E[Y]|\right ][/latex]

Which one of the following choices is correct?
options: Both S1 and S2 are true.
S1 is true, but S2 is false.
S1 is false, but S2 is true.
Both S1 and S2 are false.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: the left side is [latex]Cov(X,Y)^2[/latex]. By Cauchy-Schwarz, [latex]Cov(X,Y)^2\le Var(X)Var(Y)[/latex] always, so S1 is FALSE.
- S2: the right side is always [latex]\ge0[/latex], but covariance can be negative (e.g. Y = [latex]-[/latex]X) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Both S1 and S2 are false

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Let [latex]G=(V,E)[/latex] be an undirected unweighted connected graph. The diameter of [latex]G[/latex] is defined as:
[latex]diam(G)=\displaystyle \max_{u,v \in V} \{ \text{the length of shortest path between }u \text{ and }v \}[/latex]

Let [latex]M[/latex] be the adjacency matrix of [latex]G[/latex].
Define graph [latex]G_2[/latex] on the same set of vertices with adjacency matrix [latex]N[/latex], where

[latex]N_{ij}=\left\{\begin{array} {lcl} 1 &\text{if}\; M_{ij}>0 \text{ or } P_{ij}>0, \text{ where }P=M^2\\0 &\text{otherwise} \end{array}\right.[/latex]

Which one of the following statements is true?
questions.solution:
[latex]P=M^2[/latex] has [latex]P_{ij} \gt 0[/latex] exactly when there is a path of length 2. So in [latex]G_2[/latex], u and v are adjacent whenever their distance in G is 1 or 2.

A shortest path of length d in G can be covered with [latex]\lceil d/2\rceil[/latex] such jumps, so [latex]diam(G_2)=\lceil diam(G)/2\rceil[/latex].

Answer: [latex]diam(G_2)\le\lceil diam(G)/2\rceil[/latex]

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
options: The program will not compile successfully
The program will compile successfully and output 10 when executed
The program will compile successfully and output 8 when executed
The program will compile successfully and output 13 when executed
questions.solution:
(The loop runs j = [latex]-[/latex]3 to 3; the program compiles.) For j [latex]\lt[/latex] 0, && short-circuits, so i++ does not run.
For j [latex]\ge[/latex] 0, i++ returns the old value of i:
- j = 0: i++ gives 0 (false), i = 1
- j = 1: gives 1 (true), count = 1, i = 2
- j = 2: count = 3, i = 3
- j = 3: count = 6, i = 4

count = 6 + i = 6 + 4 = 10

Answer: The program will compile successfully and output 10 when executed

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the following language:

[latex]L= \{ w \in \{0,1\}^* \mid w \text{ ends with the substring } 011 \}[/latex]

Which one of the following deterministic finite automata accepts [latex]L[/latex]?
questions.solution:
States should remember the longest suffix matching a prefix of 011: q0 (nothing), q1 ("0"), q2 ("01"), q3 ("011", final).

From the final state: on 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] q1 (suffix "0"), on 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] q0 (suffix "0111" has no useful part).
- (A) and (B) loop on 1 at the final state, accepting 0111 False
- (C) goes from the final state to q2 on 1, accepting 01111 False
- (D) has exactly the transitions above True

Answer: D

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
For a Turing machine M, < M > denotes an encoding of M. Consider the following two languages.

[latex]\begin{array}{ll} L1 = \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M \text{ takes more than } 2021 \text{ steps on all inputs} \} \\ L2 = \{ \langle M \rangle \mid M\text{ takes more than } 2021 \text{ steps on some input} \} \end{array}[/latex]

Which one of the following options is correct?
options: Both L1 and L2 are decidable.
L1 is decidable  and L2 is undecidable.
L1 is undecidable  and L2 is decidable.
Both L1 and L2 are undecidable.
questions.solution:
In 2021 steps, M can read at most the first 2021 input symbols. So "more than 2021 steps" depends only on inputs of length up to 2021, a finite set.

Simulate M for 2022 steps on each such input; this decides both "on all inputs" (L1) and "on some input" (L2).

Answer: Both L1 and L2 are decidable

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Define [latex]R_n[/latex] to be the maximum amount earned by cutting a rod of length n meters into one or more pieces of integer length and selling them. For [latex]i > 0[/latex], let [latex]p[i][/latex] denote the selling price of a rod whose length is [latex]i[/latex] meters. Consider the array of prices:

[latex]\text{p}[1]=1,\text{p}[2]=5,\text{p}[3]=8,\text{p}[4]=9,\text{p}[5]=10,\text{p}[6]=17,\text{p}[7]=18[/latex]

which of the following statements is/are correct about [latex]R_7[/latex]?
options: [latex]R_7[/latex] is achieved by three different solutions.
[latex]R_7[/latex] cannot be achieved by a solution consisting of three pieces.
questions.solution:
Best values: R1 = 1, R2 = 5, R3 = 8, R4 = 10 (2+2), R5 = 13 (2+3), R6 = 17, R7 = 18.

R7 = 18 is reached by:
- one piece of 7 (18)
- 6 + 1 (17 + 1)
- 2 + 2 + 3 (5 + 5 + 8)

Three different solutions, one of which has three pieces (so option 4 is false).

Answer: [latex]R_7=18[/latex] and it is achieved by three different solutions

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
An articulation point in a connected graph is a vertex such that removing the vertex and its incident edges disconnects the graph into two or more connected components.
Let T be a DFS tree obtained by doing DFS in a connected undirected graph G.
Which of the following options is/are correct?
options: Root of T can never be an articulation point in G.
Root of T is an articulation point in G if and only if it has 2 or more children.
A leaf of T can be an articulation point in G.
If u is an articulation point in G such that x is an ancestor of u in T and y is a descendent of u in T, then all paths from x to y in G must pass through u.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- The root is an articulation point exactly when it has two or more DFS children: there are no cross edges in an undirected DFS, so its subtrees connect only through the root [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE (option 1 is FALSE).
- A leaf of T: removing it leaves the rest of T connected [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] never an articulation point [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- Option 4: y's subtree may have a back edge to an ancestor above u (u is an articulation point because of another subtree), giving a path from x to y that avoids u [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Root of T is an articulation point iff it has 2 or more children

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
Consider the following Boolean expression.

[latex]F=(X+Y+Z)(\overline X +Y)(\overline Y +Z)[/latex]

Which of the following Boolean expressions is/are equivalent to [latex]\overline F[/latex] (complement of [latex]F[/latex])?
questions.solution:
Find where F = 1 (XYZ): X = 1 forces Y = 1 (second factor), Y = 1 forces Z = 1 (third), and 000 fails the first. So [latex]F=\Sigma(1,3,7)[/latex] and [latex]\overline F=\Sigma(0,2,4,5,6)[/latex].

- [latex]X\bar Y+\bar Z[/latex] = {4, 5} [latex]\cup[/latex] {0, 2, 4, 6} = {0, 2, 4, 5, 6} True
- [latex](X+\bar Z)(\bar Y+\bar Z)[/latex] = {0, 2, 4, 5, 6} True
- [latex]X\bar Y+Y\bar Z+\bar X\bar Y\bar Z[/latex] = {4, 5} [latex]\cup[/latex] {2, 6} [latex]\cup[/latex] {0} True
- Option 1 is the dual, not the complement (it contains 1, not 0) False

Answer: Options 2, 3 and 4

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
A relation [latex]R[/latex] is said to be circular if [latex]aRb[/latex] and [latex]bRc[/latex] together imply [latex]cRa[/latex].
Which of the following options is/are correct?
options: If a relation S is reflexive and symmetric, then S is an equivalence relation.
If a relation S is circular and symmetric, then S is an equivalence relation.
If a relation S is reflexive and circular, then S is an equivalence relation.
If a relation S is transitive and circular, then S is an equivalence relation.
questions.solution:
Reflexive + circular gives an equivalence relation:
- Symmetric: aRb and bRb (reflexive) [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] bRa (circular).
- Transitive: aRb and bRc [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] cRa (circular) [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] aRc (symmetric).

The others fail: reflexive + symmetric need not be transitive; circular + symmetric need not be reflexive (e.g. the empty relation); transitive + circular need not be reflexive either.

Answer: Reflexive and circular [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] equivalence relation

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
A TCP server application is programmed to listen on port number P on host S. A TCP client is connected to the TCP server over the network.
Consider that while the TCP connection was active, the server machine S crashed and rebooted. Assume that the client does not use the TCP keepalive timer. Which of the following behaviors is/are possible?
options: If the client was waiting to receive a packet, it may wait indefinitely.
The TCP server application on S can listen on P after reboot.
If the client sends a packet after the server reboot, it will receive a RST segment.
If the client sends a packet after the server reboot, it will receive a FIN segment.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- The client gets no notice of the crash; without keepalive, a client waiting to receive may wait forever [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.
- After reboot the application can bind and listen on port P again [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.
- The rebooted server has no record of the old connection, so a segment from the client gets a RST [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.
- FIN is sent only on a normal close of a known connection [latex]\text{---}[/latex] not possible.

Answer: Options 1, 2 and 3

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
Consider two hosts P and Q connected through a router R. The maximum transfer unit (MTU) value of the link between P and R is 1500 bytes, and between R and Q is 820 bytes.
A TCP segment of size 1400 bytes was transferred from P to Q through R, with IP identification value as 0x1234. Assume that the IP header size is 20 bytes. Further, the packet is allowed to be fragmented, i.e., Don't Fragment (DF) flag in the IP header is not set by P.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: Two fragments are created at R and the IP datagram size carrying the second fragment is 620 bytes.
If the second fragment is lost, R will resend the fragment with the IP identification value 0x1234.
If the second fragment is lost, P is required to resend the whole TCP segment.
TCP destination port can be determined by analysing only the second fragment.
questions.solution:
P [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] R: 1400 + 20 = 1420 [latex]\le[/latex] 1500, no fragmentation. R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q (MTU 820): max data 800 (a multiple of 8).
- Fragments: 800 and 600 bytes of data [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] datagrams of 820 and 620 bytes [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Routers do not keep or resend fragments [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- IP cannot rebuild the datagram without the lost piece; TCP at P must resend the whole segment [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- The TCP header (with ports) is only in the first fragment [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Options 1 and 3

questions.subject: Operating System
options: The value of countercounter is 5 after all the threads successfully complete the execution of parop.
The value of countercounter is 1 after all the threads successfully complete the execution of parop.
The value of countercounter is 0 after all the threads successfully complete the execution of parop.
There is a deadlock involving all the threads.
questions.solution:
Each thread needs 2 of the 5 permits, so up to 2 threads can be inside together, and counter++ is not atomic.
- 5: threads run one after another [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.
- 1: thread A reads 0 and is preempted; the others run one by one in the second slot (counter = 4); A writes 1 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.
- 0: at least the last write stores a value [latex]\ge1[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] impossible.
- Deadlock: all 5 threads do their first wait (S = 0) and then all block on the second [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.

Answer: Options 1, 2 and 4

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Consider a dynamic hashing approach for 4-bit integer keys:

1. There is a main hash table of size 4.
2. The 2 least significant bits of a key is used to index into the main hash table.
3. Initially, the main hash table entries are empty.
4. Thereafter, when more keys are hashed into it, to resolve collisions, the set of all keys corresponding to a main hash table. entry is organized as a binary tree that grows on demand.
5. First, the 3rd least significant bit is used to divide the keys into left and right subtrees.
6. To resolve more collisions, each node of the binary tree is further sub-divided into left and right subtrees based on the 4th least significant bit.
7. A split is done only if it is needed, i.e., only when there is a collision.

Consider the following state of the hash table.

Which of the following sequences of key insertions can cause the above state of the hash table (assume the keys are in decimal notation)?
questions.solution:
Read the state: index 00 empty; 01 has 3 keys (one with 3rd bit 0, two with 3rd bit 1, split by the 4th bit); 10 has 2 keys (3rd bit 0 and 1); 11 has 1 key.

Option C: 10, 9, 6, 7, 5, 13
- 10 = 1010 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10, bit3 = 0; 6 = 0110 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10, bit3 = 1 True
- 9 = 1001 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 01, bit3 = 0; 5 = 0101 and 13 = 1101 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 01, bit3 = 1, split by bit4 (0 and 1) True
- 7 = 0111 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 11 True

The others fail: (A) has 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] index 00; (B) has 1 and 9 colliding with bit3 = 0; (D) has 6 and 14 colliding and nothing in 11.

Answer: 10, 9, 6, 7, 5, 13

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
The function is Horner's rule: it evaluates [latex]Y[0]x^{n-1}+\cdots+Y[n-1][/latex].

With all Y[i] = 1, x = 2, n = 10: [latex]2^9+2^8+\cdots+1=2^{10}-1=1023[/latex]

Answer: 1023

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
Consider the sliding window flow-control protocol operating between a sender and a receiver over a full-duplex error-free link. Assume the following:

The time taken for processing the data frame by the receiver is negligible.
The time taken for processing the acknowledgement frame by the sender is negligible.
The sender has infinite number of frames available for transmission.
The size of the data frame is 2,000 bits and the size of the acknowledgement frame is 10 bits.
The link data rate in each direction is 1 Mbps ([latex]= 10^6[/latex] bits per second).
One way propagation delay of the link is 100 milliseconds.

The minimum value of the sender's window size in terms of the number of frames, (rounded to the nearest integer) needed to achieve a link utilization of 50% is _____________
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Frame transmission time = 2000 / [latex]10^6[/latex] = 2 ms
- ACK transmission time = 10 / [latex]10^6[/latex] = 0.01 ms
- Cycle = 2 + 100 + 0.01 + 100 = 202.01 ms

Utilization [latex]=\frac{W\times2}{202.01}=0.5\Rightarrow W=50.5[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] about 51 frames.

Answer: 51

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.solution:
Common sub-expressions share nodes:
- leaves: b, c, 1 (3 nodes)
- b + c (shared by a and d) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1 node
- (b + c) + 1 (shared by e and f) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1 node
- e + f [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1 node

Total = 6

Answer: 6

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
In a pushdown automaton [latex]P=(Q, \Sigma, \Gamma, \delta, q_0, F)[/latex], a transition of the form,

where [latex]p,q \in Q \; a \in \sigma \cup \{ \epsilon \} ,\;X,Y, \in \Gamma \cup \{ \epsilon \}[/latex], represents

[latex](q,Y) \in \delta(p,a,X)[/latex]

Consider the following pushdown automaton over the input alphabet [latex]\Sigma = \{a,b\}[/latex] and stack alphabet [latex]\Gamma = \{ \#, A\}[/latex].

The number of strings of length 100 accepted by the above pushdown automaton is ___________
questions.solution:
The PDA pushes # and then an A for every a; in q2 every b pops an A. It can reach the final state q3 only if an A is still on top.

So it accepts [latex]a^mb^n[/latex] with [latex]n \lt m[/latex]. For length 100: m + n = 100 with n [latex]\lt[/latex] m [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] n = 0, 1, [latex]\ldots[/latex], 49 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 50 strings.

Answer: 50

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider the following matrix.
[latex]\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\\ 1& 0& 1 & 1\\ 1& 1 & 0 & 1 \\1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}[/latex]
The largest eigenvalue of the above matrix is __________.
questions.solution:
The matrix is [latex]J-I[/latex], where J is the 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 all-ones matrix.
Eigenvalues of J: 4, 0, 0, 0. Subtracting 1: 3, [latex]-[/latex]1, [latex]-[/latex]1, [latex]-[/latex]1.

Largest = 3

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
A five-stage pipeline has stage delays of 150, 120, 150, 160 and 140 nanoseconds. The registers that are used between the pipeline stages have a delay of 5 nanoseconds each.
The total time to execute 100 independent instructions on this pipeline, assuming there are no pipeline stalls, is _______ nanoseconds.
questions.solution:
Clock cycle = slowest stage + register delay = 160 + 5 = 165 ns.
Cycles for 100 instructions on 5 stages = 5 + 100 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 104.

Time = 104 [latex]\times[/latex] 165 = 17160 ns

Answer: 17160

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
A sender (S) transmits a signal, which can be one of the two kinds: H and L with probabilities 0.1 and 0.9 respectively, to a receiver (R)
In the graph below, the weight of edge [latex](u,v)[/latex] is the probability of receiving [latex]v[/latex] when [latex]u[/latex] is transmitted, where [latex]u,v\in\{H,L\}[/latex]. For example, the probability that the received signal is [latex]L[/latex] given the transmitted signal was [latex]H[/latex], is 0.7.

If the received signal is [latex]H[/latex], the probability that the transmitted signal was [latex]H[/latex] (rounded to 2 decimal places) is __________.
questions.solution:
From the graph: P(recv H | sent H) = 0.3 and P(recv H | sent L) = 0.8.

P(recv H) = 0.1 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.3 + 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.8 = 0.03 + 0.72 = 0.75

Bayes: [latex]P(\text{sent H}\mid\text{recv H})=\frac{0.03}{0.75}=0.04[/latex]

Answer: 0.04

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
Consider the following instruction sequence where registers [latex]R_1,R_2 \text{ and }R_3[/latex] are general purpose and [latex]MEMORY[X][/latex] denotes the content at the memory location [latex]X[/latex].

[latex]\begin{array}{llc} \textbf{Instruction} & \textbf{Semantics} & \textbf{Instruction Size} \text{ (bytes)} \\ \hline \text{MOV } R1, (5000) & R1 \leftarrow \text{MEMORY}[5000] & 4 \\ \hline \text{MOV } R2, (R3) & R2 \leftarrow \text{MEMORY}[R3] & 4 \\ \hline \text{ADD} R2, R1 & R2 \leftarrow R1 + R2 & 2 \\ \hline \text{MOV } (R3), R2 & \text{MEMORY}[R3] \leftarrow R2 & 4 \\ \hline \text{INC } R3 & R3 \leftarrow R3+1 & 2 \\ \hline \text{DEC } R1 & R1 \leftarrow R1-1 & 2 \\ \hline \text{BNZ } 1004 & \text{Branch if not zero to the} & 2 \\ & \text{given absolute address} \\ \hline \text{HALT} & \text{Stop} & 1 \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]

Assume that the content of the memory location 5000 is 10, and the content of the register [latex]R_3[/latex] is 3000. The content of each of the memory locations from 3000 to 3020 is 50. The instruction sequence starts from the memory location 1000. All the numbers are in decimal format. Assume that the memory is byte addressable.
After the execution of the program, the content of memory location 3010 is ____________
questions.solution:
R1 = MEMORY[5000] = 10, so the loop (BNZ back to 1004) runs 10 times. Each pass adds R1 to MEMORY[R3] and moves R3 one byte ahead.

R3 goes 3000, 3001, [latex]\ldots[/latex], 3009. Location 3010 is never written, so it keeps its value 50.

Answer: 50

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 7 to 3.

Among the options below, an acceptable value for the total number of students in the class is:
questions.solution:
Boys : girls = 7 : 3, so the total must be a multiple of 7 + 3 = 10. Only 50 is (35 boys, 15 girls).

Answer: 50

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
A polygon is convex if, for every pair of points, P and Q belonging to the polygon, the line segment PQ lies completely inside or on the polygon.
Which one of the following is NOT a convex polygon?
questions.solution:
Shape (A) has a notch (an inward corner). A segment between two points on either side of the notch passes outside the shape, so it is not convex. The triangle, square and trapezium are convex.

Answer: A

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Consider the following sentences:

i. Everybody in the class is prepared for the exam.
ii. Babu invited Danish to his home because he enjoys playing chess.

Which of the following is the CORRECT observation about the above two sentences?
options: (i) is grammatically correct and (ii) is unambiguous
(i) is grammatically incorrect and (ii) is unambiguous
(i) is grammatically correct and (ii) is ambiguous
(i) is grammatically incorrect and (ii) is ambiguous
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- (i) "Everybody ... is prepared" is grammatically correct ("everybody" takes a singular verb).
- (ii) "he" could mean Babu or Danish [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] ambiguous.

Answer: (i) is grammatically correct and (ii) is ambiguous

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: A circular sheet of paper is folded along the lines in the direction shown. The paper, after being punched in the final folded state as shown and unfolded in the reverse order of folding, will look like _______.
questions.solution:
Unfold in reverse order:
- The punch on the vertical fold line opens into a long horizontal slot at the top; unfolding the horizontal fold copies it to the bottom.
- The small punch on the horizontal fold line opens into a small vertical slot; unfolding the vertical fold copies it to the other side.
- The quarter-circle at the corner becomes a full circle in the centre.

This is pattern (A): long horizontal slots top and bottom, small vertical slots left and right.

Answer: A

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
_________ is to surgery as writer is to ___________

Which one of the following options maintains a similar logical relation in the above sentence?
questions.solution:
A doctor performs surgery; a writer produces a book (person : their work).

Answer: Doctor, book

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: We have 2 rectangular sheets of paper, M and N, of dimensions 6 cm x 1 cm each. Sheet M is rolled to form an open cylinder by bringing the short edges of the sheet together. Sheet N is cut into equal square patches and assembled to form the largest possible closed cube. Assuming the ends of the cylinder are closed, the ratio of the volume of the cylinder to that of the cube is _________
questions.solution:
Cylinder: short edges (1 cm) joined [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] circumference 6, height 1. [latex]r=\frac{3}{\pi}[/latex], [latex]V=\pi r^2h=\frac{9}{\pi}[/latex].

Cube: area 6 cm[latex]^2[/latex] cut into 6 squares of 1 cm[latex]^2[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] side 1, V = 1.

Ratio [latex]=\frac{9}{\pi}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac{9}{\pi}[/latex]

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline \textbf{Items} & \textbf{Cost} & \textbf{Profit \%} & \textbf{Marked Price} \\ & (Rs.) & & (Rs.) \\ \hline P &5,400 &---&5,860\\ \hline Q&---&25&10,000\\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]

Details of prices of two items P and Q are presented in the above table. The ratio of cost of item P to cost of item Q is 3:4. Discount is calculated as the difference between the marked price and the selling price. The profit percentage is calculated as the ratio of the difference between selling price and cost, to the cost
[latex](\text{Profit} \%=\dfrac{\text{Selling price - Cost}}{\text{Cost}} \times 100)[/latex]
The discount on item Q, as a percentage of its marked price, is _______
questions.solution:
Cost of Q = [latex]5400\times\frac43=7200[/latex].
Selling price of Q = 7200 [latex]\times[/latex] 1.25 = 9000.
Discount = 10000 [latex]-[/latex] 9000 = 1000 = 10% of the marked price.

Answer: 10

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
There are five bags each containing identical sets of ten distinct chocolates. One chocolate is picked from each bag.
The probability that at least two chocolates are identical is _________
questions.solution:
P(all 5 different) = [latex]\frac{10\times9\times8\times7\times6}{10^5}=\frac{30240}{100000}=0.3024[/latex]

P(at least two identical) = 1 [latex]-[/latex] 0.3024 = 0.6976

Answer: 0.6976

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Given below are two statements 1 and 2, and two conclusions I and II

Statement 1: All bacteria are microorganisms.
Statement 2: All pathogens are microorganisms.

Conclusion I: Some pathogens are bacteria.
Conclusion II: All pathogens are not bacteria.

Based on the above statements and conclusions, which one of the following options is logically CORRECT?
options: Either conclusion I or II is correct
Neither conclusion I nor II is correct
questions.solution:
Both bacteria and pathogens are inside "microorganisms", but nothing says how bacteria and pathogens relate to each other. They may overlap or not, so neither "some pathogens are bacteria" nor "all pathogens are not bacteria" follows. They are also not complementary (both could fail), so "either" is wrong too.

Answer: Neither conclusion I nor II is correct

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Some people suggest anti-obesity measures (AOM) such as displaying calorie information in restaurant menus. Such measures sidestep addressing the core problems that cause obesity: poverty and income inequality.

Which one of the following statements summarizes the passage?
options: The proposed AOM addresses the core problems that cause obesity
If obesity reduces, poverty will naturally reduce, since obesity causes poverty
AOM are addressing the core problems and are likely to succeed
AOM are addressing the problem superficially
questions.solution:
The passage says these measures "sidestep" the core problems (poverty and inequality). So they deal with obesity only on the surface.

Answer: AOM are addressing the problem superficially

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Let G be a connected undirected weighted graph. Consider the following two statements.

S1: There exists a minimum weight edge in G which is present in every minimum spanning tree of G.
S2: If every edge in G has distinct weight, then G has a unique minimum spanning tree.

Which one of the following options is correct?
options: Both S1 and S2 are true
S1 is true and S2 is false
S1 is false and S2 is true
Both S1 and S2 are false
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: if several edges share the minimum weight (e.g. a triangle with all weights 1), each MST leaves out one of them, so no single minimum edge is in every MST [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- S2: distinct weights [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] unique MST [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: S1 is false and S2 is true

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: Let H be a binary min-heap consisting of n elements implemented as an array. What is the worst case time complexity of an optimal algorithm to find the maximum element in H?
questions.solution:
In a min-heap the maximum is in one of the [latex]\lceil n/2\rceil[/latex] leaves, and the leaves are not ordered among themselves, so all of them must be checked: [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex]

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.solution:
"Integer x;" is lexically fine (Integer is an identifier) and syntactically looks like a declaration "type-name identifier". But Integer is not a declared type, and that is found only by the semantic analyzer (symbol table / type checking).

Answer: Semantic analyzer

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
The format of the single-precision floating point representation of a real number as per the IEEE 754 standard is as follows:

[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline \text{sign} & \text{exponent} & \text{mantissa} \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]

Which one of the following choices is correct with respect to the smallest normalized positive number represented using the standard?
questions.solution:
Normalized numbers need exponent field from 1 to 254 (0 is for zero/denormals). The smallest normalized positive number has exponent 00000001 and mantissa all 0: [latex]1.0\times2^{1-127}=2^{-126}[/latex].

Answer: exponent = 00000001 and mantissa = 0[latex]\ldots[/latex]0

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
Which one of the following circuits implements the Boolean function given below?

[latex]f(x,y,z) = m_0+m_1+m_3+m_4+m_5+m_6[/latex]

where [latex]m_i[/latex] is the [latex]i^{th}[/latex] minterm.
questions.solution:
Select lines are y (s1) and z (s0), so input [latex]I_{2y+z}[/latex] must equal f with x free:
- yz = 00: m0 (x = 0), m4 (x = 1) both 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]I_0=1[/latex]
- yz = 01: m1, m5 both 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]I_1=1[/latex]
- yz = 10: m2 = 0, m6 = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]I_2=x[/latex]
- yz = 11: m3 = 1, m7 = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]I_3=\bar x[/latex]

Inputs (1, 1, x, x') = circuit A.

Answer: A

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Consider the following statements S1 and S2 about the relational data model:

S1: A relation scheme can have at most one foreign key.
S2: A foreign key in a relation scheme R cannot be used to refer to tuples of R.

Which one of the following choices is correct?
options: Both S1 and S2 are true
S1 is true and S2 is false
S1 is false and S2 is true
Both S1 and S2 are false
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: a relation can have several foreign keys (e.g. Enrolment(studentId, courseId) refers to two tables) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- S2: a foreign key can refer to the same relation (e.g. Employee.managerId [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Employee.empId) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Both S1 and S2 are false

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Consider the three-way handshake mechanism followed during TCP connection establishment between hosts P and Q. Let X and Y be two random 32-bit starting sequence numbers chosen by P and Q respectively. Suppose P sends a TCP connection request message to Q with a TCP segment having SYN bit =1, SEQ number =X, and ACK bit =0. Suppose Q accepts the connection request. Which one of the following choices represents the information present in the TCP segment header that is sent by Q to P?
options: SYN  bit =1, SEQ number =X+1, ACK bit =0, ACK number =Y, FIN bit =0
SYN  bit =0, SEQ number =X+1, ACK bit =0, ACK number =Y, FIN bit =1
SYN  bit =1, SEQ number =Y, ACK bit =1, ACK number =X+1, FIN bit =0
SYN  bit =1, SEQ number =Y, ACK bit =1, ACK number =X, FIN bit =0
questions.solution:
Q's reply is the SYN-ACK:
- SYN = 1 with Q's own initial sequence number SEQ = Y
- ACK = 1, acknowledging P's SYN (which uses one number) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] ACK number = X + 1
- FIN = 0

Answer: SYN = 1, SEQ = Y, ACK = 1, ACK number = X+1, FIN = 0

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text: What is the worst-case number of arithmetic operations performed by recursive binary search on a sorted array of size n?
questions.solution:
Each recursive call does a constant number of arithmetic operations (computing mid) and halves the range. The depth is [latex]\log_2 n[/latex], so the total is [latex]\Theta(\log_2 n)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(\log_2(n))[/latex]

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text: Let [latex]L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*[/latex] be an arbitrary regular language accepted by a minimal DFA with k states. Which one of the following languages must necessarily be accepted by a minimal DFA with k states?
questions.solution:
For the complement, use the same DFA and swap final and non-final states. It has k states and is still minimal (any two states distinguishable for L are also distinguishable for its complement).

Adding or removing the single string 01, or computing L[latex]\cdot[/latex]L, can change the number of states.

Answer: [latex]\{0,1\}^*-L[/latex]

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
arr[1] points to arr[1][0]; +9 moves 9 ints ahead in the row-major layout: position 5 + 9 = 14 = row 2, column 4.

arr[2][4] = 10 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 + 4 = 24

Answer: 24

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider the following sets, where [latex]n\geq 2[/latex]:

S1: Set of all nxn matrices with entries from the set [latex]\{a, b, c\}[/latex]
S2: Set of all functions from the set[latex]\{0,1,2,...,n^2-1\}[/latex] to the set [latex]\{0, 1, 2 \}[/latex]

Which of the following choice(s) is/are correct?
options: There does not exist a bijection from S1 to S2
There exists a surjection from S1 to S2
There exists a bijection from S1 to S2
There does not exist an injection from S1 to S2
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]|S_1|=3^{n^2}[/latex] (each of the [latex]n^2[/latex] entries has 3 choices).
- [latex]|S_2|=3^{n^2}[/latex] (each of the [latex]n^2[/latex] inputs has 3 choices).

Equal finite sizes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a bijection exists (read the matrix entries in order as the function values). A bijection is also a surjection and an injection.

Answer: A surjection exists; a bijection exists

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text: Let [latex]L_1[/latex] be a regular language and [latex]L_2[/latex] be a context-free language. Which of the following languages is/are context-free?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1\cap\overline{L_2}[/latex]: [latex]\overline{L_2}[/latex] need not be CFL [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not always CFL.
- [latex]\overline{\overline{L_1}\cup\overline{L_2}}=L_1\cap L_2[/latex] (De Morgan) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL True
- [latex]L_2\cup\overline{L_2}=\Sigma^*[/latex], so the whole thing is [latex]\Sigma^*[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL True
- [latex](L_1\cap L_2)\cup(\overline{L_1}\cap L_2)=L_2[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL True

Answer: Options 2, 3 and 4

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text: In the context of compilers, which of the following is/are NOT an intermediate representation of the source program?
questions.solution:
Three address code, AST and CFG are all forms of the program used between front end and back end. The symbol table only stores information about names; it is not a representation of the program.

Answer: Symbol table

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct in the context of CPU scheduling?
options: The goal is to only maximize CPU utilization and minimize throughput
Round-robin policy can be used even when the CPU time required by each of the processes is not known apriori
Implementing preemptive scheduling needs hardware support
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Turnaround = completion [latex]-[/latex] arrival, which includes waiting time [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- The goal is to maximize throughput (and utilization), not minimize it [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- Round-robin only needs a time quantum, not burst lengths [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Preemption needs a hardware timer interrupt [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Options 1, 3 and 4

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Choose the correct choice(s) regarding the following proportional logic assertion S:

[latex]S: (( P \wedge Q) \rightarrow R) \rightarrow (( P \wedge Q) \rightarrow (Q \rightarrow R))[/latex]
options: S  is neither a tautology nor a contradiction
The antecedent of S is logically equivalent to the consequent of S
questions.solution:
Simplify the consequent: [latex](P\wedge Q)\rightarrow(Q\rightarrow R)\equiv(P\wedge Q\wedge Q)\rightarrow R\equiv(P\wedge Q)\rightarrow R[/latex], which is exactly the antecedent.

So S has the form [latex]A\rightarrow A[/latex], which is always true.

Answer: S is a tautology; its antecedent is equivalent to its consequent

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.text:
Consider a complete binary tree with 7 nodes. Let A denote the set of first 3 elements obtained by performing Breadth-First Search (BFS) starting from the root. Let B denote the set of first 3 elements obtained by performing Depth-First Search (DFS) starting from the root.

The value of |A-B| is _____________
questions.solution:
Complete binary tree with 7 nodes: root, its two children L and R, and four grandchildren.
- BFS first 3: root, L, R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] A = {root, L, R}
- DFS first 3: root, L, L's left child [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] B = {root, L, LL}

A [latex]-[/latex] B = {R} [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] |A [latex]-[/latex] B| = 1

Answer: 1

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the following deterministic finite automaton (DFA)

The number of strings of length 8 accepted by the above automaton is _________
questions.solution:
Every path from the start reaches the final state after exactly 3 symbols (start [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] level 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] level 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] final, on either symbol at every step), and the final state loops on 0 and 1.

So every string of length [latex]\ge3[/latex] is accepted. Strings of length 8: [latex]2^8=256[/latex].

Answer: 256

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: If [latex]x[/latex] and [latex]y[/latex] are two decimal digits and [latex](0.1101)_2 = (0.8xy5)_{10}[/latex], the decimal value of [latex]x+y[/latex] is ___________
questions.solution:
[latex](0.1101)_2=\frac12+\frac14+\frac1{16}=0.8125[/latex]

0.8xy5 = 0.8125 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = 1, y = 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x + y = 3

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: Consider a set-associative cache of size 2KB ([latex]1KB=2^{10}[/latex] bytes) with cache block size of 64 bytes. Assume that the cache is byte-addressable and a 32 -bit address is used for accessing the cache. If the width of the tag field is 22 bits, the associativity of the cache is ______
questions.solution:
Offset = [latex]\log_2 64=6[/latex] bits. Tag = 22 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] set index = 32 [latex]-[/latex] 22 [latex]-[/latex] 6 = 4 bits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 16 sets.

Lines = 2 KB / 64 B = 32. Associativity = 32 / 16 = 2.

Answer: 2

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text: Consider a computer system with DMA support. The DMA module is transferring one 8-bit character in one CPU cycle from a device to memory through cycle stealing at regular intervals. Consider a 2 MHz processor. If 0.5% processor cycles are used for DMA, the data transfer rate of the device is __________ bits per second.
questions.solution:
Cycles used for DMA per second = 0.5% of [latex]2\times10^6[/latex] = [latex]10^4[/latex].
Each cycle moves 8 bits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]10^4\times8=80000[/latex] bits/s.

Answer: 80000

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text: A data file consisting of 1,50,000 student-records is stored on a hard disk with block size of 4096 bytes. The data file is sorted on the primary key RollNo. The size of a record pointer for this disk is 7 bytes. Each student-record has a candidate key attribute called ANum of size 12 bytes. Suppose an index file with records consisting of two fields, ANum value and the record pointer the corresponding student record, is built and stored on the same disk. Assume that the records of data file and index file are not split across disk blocks. The number of blocks in the index file is ______
questions.solution:
ANum is not the sorting key, so the index must be dense: one entry per record.

Entry size = 12 + 7 = 19 bytes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] entries per block = [latex]\lfloor4096/19\rfloor=215[/latex].
Blocks = [latex]\lceil150000/215\rceil=698[/latex]

Answer: 698

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: For a given biased coin, the probability that the outcome of a toss is a head is 0.4. This coin is tossed 1,000 times. Let X denote the random variable whose value is the number of times that head appeared in these 1,000 tosses. The standard deviation of X (rounded to 2 decimal place) is ________
questions.solution:
X is binomial with n = 1000, p = 0.4.
[latex]\sigma=\sqrt{np(1-p)}=\sqrt{1000\times0.4\times0.6}=\sqrt{240}\approx15.49[/latex]

Answer: 15.49

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
The function computes the GCD by repeated subtraction (and stops at 1 if either value hits 1).
SomeFunction(15, 255): 255 [latex]-[/latex] 15 repeatedly [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (15, 240) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\ldots[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (15, 15) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] returns 15.

gcd(15, 255) = 15

Answer: 15

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Suppose that P is a 4x5 matrix such that every solution of the equation Px=0 is a scalar multiple of [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & 4 &3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}^T[/latex]. The rank of P is _______
questions.solution:
All solutions of Px = 0 are multiples of one vector [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] nullity = 1.
P has 5 columns, so by rank-nullity: rank = 5 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 4.

Answer: 4

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Suppose that [latex]f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}[/latex] is a continuous function on the interval [-3,3] and a differentiable function in the interval (-3,3) such that for every [latex]x[/latex] in the interval, [latex]f'(x) \leq 2[/latex]. If [latex]f(-3) =7[/latex], then [latex]f(3) [/latex] is at most __________
questions.solution:
By the mean value theorem, [latex]f(3)-f(-3)=f'(c)\cdot6\le2\times6=12[/latex].

[latex]f(3)\le7+12=19[/latex]

Answer: 19

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
Consider the string abbccddeee. Each letter in the string must be assigned a binary code satisfying the following properties:

For any two letters, the code assigned to one letter must not be a prefix of the code assigned to the other letter.
For any two letters of the same frequency, the letter which occurs earlier in the dictionary order is assigned a code whose length is at most the length of the code assigned to the other letter.

Among the set of all binary code assignments which satisfy the above two properties, what is the minimum length of the encoded string?
questions.solution:
Frequencies: a 1, b 2, c 2, d 2, e 3 (total 10).

Huffman: merge a(1) with a frequency-2 letter. To respect the tie rule (b, c, d in dictionary order), merge a with d [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3; then b + c [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4; then ad + e [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6; then 4 + 6.
Code lengths: a 3, d 3, b 2, c 2, e 2 (b [latex]\le[/latex] c [latex]\le[/latex] d True).

Length = 1[latex]\times[/latex]3 + 2[latex]\times[/latex]2 + 2[latex]\times[/latex]2 + 2[latex]\times[/latex]3 + 3[latex]\times[/latex]2 = 3 + 4 + 4 + 6 + 6 = 23

Answer: 23

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
Assume a two-level inclusive cache hierarchy, L1 and L2, where L2 is the larger of the two. Consider the following statements.

S1: Read misses in a write through L1 cache do not result in writebacks of dirty lines to the L2
S2: Write allocate policy must be used in conjunction with write through caches and no-write allocate policy is used with writeback caches.

Which of the following statements is correct?
options: S1  is true and S2 is false
S1  is false and S2 is true
S1  is true and S2 is true
S1  is false and S2 is false
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: a write-through L1 never has dirty lines (every write already goes to L2), so a read miss never writes back a dirty line [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- S2: the usual pairing is the opposite (write-allocate with write-back, no-write-allocate with write-through), and neither is mandatory [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: S1 is true and S2 is false

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Suppose we want to design a synchronous circuit that processes a string of 0's and 1's. Given a string, it produces another string by replacing the first 1 in any subsequence of consecutive 1's by a 0. Consider the following example.

[latex]\begin{array}{ll} \text{Input sequence:} & 00100011000011100 \\ \text{Output sequence:} & 00000001000001100 \end{array}[/latex]

A Mealy Machine is a state machine where both the next state and the output are functions of the present state and the current input.
The above mentioned circuit can be designed as a two-state Mealy machine. The states in the Mealy machine can be represented using Boolean values 0 and 1. We denote the current state, the next state, the next incoming bit, and the output bit of the Mealy machine by the variables s, t, b and y respectively.
Assume the initial state of the Mealy machine is 0.

What are the Boolean expressions corresponding to t and y in terms of s and b?
questions.solution:
The state remembers the previous bit: t = b.

Output 1 only for a 1 that is not the first of a run, i.e. the current bit is 1 and the previous bit was 1: y = sb.

Check with 0011: outputs 0, 0, 0, 1 True

Answer: t = b, y = sb

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
In an examination, a student can choose the order in which two questions (QuesA and QuesB) must be attempted.

If the first question is answered wrong, the student gets zero marks.
If the first question is answered correctly and the second question is not answered correctly, the student gets the marks only for the first question.
If both the questions are answered correctly, the student gets the sum of the marks of the two questions.

The following table shows the probability of correctly answering a question and the marks of the question respectively.

[latex]\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{question} & \text{probabiloty of answering correctly} & \text{marks} \\ \hline \textsf{QuesA} & 0.8 & 10 \\ \textsf{QuesB} & 0.5 & 20 \end{array}[/latex]

Assuming that the student always wants to maximize her expected marks in the examination, in which order should she attempt the questions and what is the expected marks for that order (assume that the questions are independent)?
options: First QuesA and then QuesB. Expected marks 14.
First QuesB and then QuesA. Expected marks 14.
First QuesB and then QuesA. Expected marks 22.
First QuesA and then QuesB. Expected marks 16.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- A first: [latex]0.8\times(10+0.5\times20)=0.8\times20=16[/latex]
- B first: [latex]0.5\times(20+0.8\times10)=0.5\times28=14[/latex]

A first gives more.

Answer: First QuesA and then QuesB. Expected marks 16

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.solution:
CSE computes x + 3, y[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]f1 and y[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]f2 once before the loop and reuses them.

- Before the loop: t = x + 3, then z = t + f1 + f2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 additions, 2 dereferences.
- Loop: 100 iterations (i = 0, 2, [latex]\ldots[/latex], 198), each with i + 2, one addition to p and one to q [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 additions [latex]\times[/latex] 100 = 300.

Total: 303 additions, 2 dereferences.

Answer: 303 and 2

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
The relation scheme given below is used to store information about the employees of a company, where empId is the key and deptId indicates the department to which the employee is assigned. Each employee is assigned to exactly one department.

[latex]\textsf{emp($\underline{\textsf{empId}}$, name, gender, salary, deptId)}[/latex]

Consider the following SQL query:
 select deptId, count(*)
from emp
where gender = "female" and salary > (select avg(salary)from emp)
group by deptId;
The above query gives, for each department in the company, the number of female employees whose salary is greater than the average salary of
questions.solution:
The subquery (select avg(salary) from emp) has no condition and is not correlated, so it is the average salary of all employees in the company.

Answer: employees in the company

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Let S be the following schedule of operations of three transactions [latex]T_1, T_2 \text{ and }T_3[/latex] in a relational database system:

[latex]R_2(Y), R_1(X), R_3(Z), R_1(Y)W_1(X), R_2(Z), W_2(Y), R_3(X), W_3(Z)[/latex]

Consider the statements P and Q below:

P: S is conflict-serializable.
Q: If [latex]T_3[/latex] commits before [latex]T_1[/latex] finishes, then S is recoverable.

Which one of the following choices is correct?
options: Both P and Q are true
P is true and Q is false
P is false and Q is true
Both P and Q are false
questions.solution:
Conflicts:
- [latex]R_1(Y)[/latex] before [latex]W_2(Y)[/latex]: T1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T2
- [latex]W_1(X)[/latex] before [latex]R_3(X)[/latex]: T1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
- [latex]R_2(Z)[/latex] before [latex]W_3(Z)[/latex]: T2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
No cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] conflict serializable (T1, T2, T3). P is true.

T3 reads X written by T1. If T3 commits before T1, and T1 later aborts, T3 cannot be undone [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not recoverable. Q is false.

Answer: P is true and Q is false

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: A bag has [latex]r[/latex] red balls and [latex]b[/latex] black balls. All balls are identical except for their colours. In a trial, a ball is randomly drawn from the bag, its colour is noted and the ball is placed back into the bag along with another ball of the same colour. Note that the number of balls in the bag will increase by one, after the trial. A sequence of four such trials is conducted. Which one of the following choices gives the probability of drawing a red ball in the fourth trial?
questions.solution:
This is Polya's urn. By symmetry, every draw has the same chance of being red as the first draw.

Check for the 2nd draw: [latex]\frac{r}{r+b}\cdot\frac{r+1}{r+b+1}+\frac{b}{r+b}\cdot\frac{r}{r+b+1}=\frac{r(r+b+1)}{(r+b)(r+b+1)}=\frac{r}{r+b}[/latex]. The same holds for the 4th.

Answer: [latex]\frac{r}{r+b}[/latex]

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Consider the cyclic redundancy check (CRC) based error detecting scheme having the generator polynomial [latex]X^3+X+1[/latex]. Suppose the message [latex]m_4m_3m_2m_1m_0=11000[/latex] is to be transmitted. Check bits [latex]c_2c_1c_0[/latex] are appended at the end of the message by the transmitter using the above CRC scheme. The transmitted bit string is denoted by [latex]m_4m_3m_2m_1m_0c_2c_1c_0[/latex]. The value of the checkbit sequence [latex]c_2c_1c_0[/latex] is
questions.solution:
Generator [latex]x^3+x+1[/latex] = 1011. Append 3 zeros: 11000000, then divide (XOR):
- 1100 [latex]\oplus[/latex] 1011 = 0111 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bring 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1110
- 1110 [latex]\oplus[/latex] 1011 = 0101 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bring 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1010
- 1010 [latex]\oplus[/latex] 1011 = 0001 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bring 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0010 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bring 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0100

Remainder = 100

Answer: 100

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
options: Upon execution, the program creates a linked-list of five nodes
Upon execution, the program goes into an infinite loop
It has a missing returnreturn which will be reported as an error by the compiler
It dereferences an uninitialized pointer that may result in a run-time error
questions.solution:
The list has 4 nodes (values 0, 1, 2, 3). The last node's next is never set; malloc does not initialize it.

In the last loop pass (index = 3), head moves to the 4th node and then to its next (garbage), and the second printf dereferences that pointer [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undefined behaviour / possible crash.

(A missing return in main is allowed in C.)

Answer: It dereferences an uninitialized pointer that may result in a run-time error

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
Consider the following two statements about regular languages:

S1: Every infinite regular language contains an undecidable language as a subset.
S2: Every finite language is regular.

Which one of the following choices is correct?
options: Both S1 and S2 are true
Neither S1 nor S2 is true
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: an infinite language has uncountably many subsets, but only countably many are decidable. So some subset is undecidable [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- S2: a finite language is a finite union of single strings [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] regular [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Both S1 and S2 are true

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
For two n-dimensional real vectors [latex]P[/latex] and [latex]Q[/latex], the operation [latex]s(P,Q)[/latex] is defined as follows:

[latex]s(P,Q) = \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^n (P[i] \cdot Q[i])[/latex]

Let [latex]\mathcal{L}[/latex] be a set of 10-dimensional non-zero real vectors such that for every pair of distinct vectors [latex]P,Q \in \mathcal{L}, s(P,Q)=0[/latex]. What is the maximum cardinality possible for the set [latex]\mathcal{L}[/latex]?
questions.solution:
s(P, Q) is the dot product, so the set contains mutually orthogonal non-zero vectors. Such vectors are linearly independent, and [latex]\mathbb{R}^{10}[/latex] has at most 10 independent vectors (e.g. the 10 unit vectors).

Answer: 10

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text:
For a statement S in a program, in the context of liveness analysis, the following sets are defined:

USE(S) : the set of variables used in S
IN(S) : the set of variables that are live at the entry of S
OUT(S) : the set of variables that are live at the exit of S

Consider a basic block that consists of two statements, S1 followed by S2. Which one of the following statements is correct?
questions.solution:
In a basic block, control always goes from S1 straight to S2, so whatever is live just after S1 is exactly what is live just before S2: OUT(S1) = IN(S2).

Answer: OUT(S1) = IN(S2)

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.text:
For constants [latex]a\geq 1[/latex] and [latex]b \gt 1[/latex], consider the following recurrence defined on the non-negative integers:

[latex]T(n) = a \cdot T \left(\dfrac{n}{b} \right) + f(n)[/latex]

Which one of the following options is correct about the recurrence [latex]T(n)[/latex]?
options: if [latex]f(n)[/latex] is [latex]O(n^{\log_b(a)-\epsilon})[/latex] for some [latex]\epsilon \gt 0[/latex], then [latex]T(n)[/latex] is [latex]\Theta(n ^{\log_b(a)})[/latex].
questions.solution:
This is exactly case 1 of the Master theorem: if [latex]f(n)=O(n^{\log_b a-\epsilon})[/latex], then [latex]T(n)=\Theta(n^{\log_b a})[/latex].

The others are wrong in general: e.g. option 1 fails for a = 4, b = 2 (gives [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex]), and case 2 has an extra log factor ([latex]\Theta(n^{\log_b a}\log n)[/latex]).

Answer: Option 3

questions.subject: Databases
questions.text:
Suppose the following functional dependencies hold on a relation U with attributes [latex]P, Q, R, S, \text{ and } T[/latex]:

[latex]P \rightarrow QR \\ RS \rightarrow T[/latex]

Which of the following functional dependencies can be inferred from the above functional dependencies?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]P\rightarrow QR[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]P\rightarrow R[/latex] (decomposition) True
- [latex]PS\rightarrow RS[/latex] (augmentation) and [latex]RS\rightarrow T[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]PS\rightarrow T[/latex] True
- [latex]P\rightarrow Q[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]PS\rightarrow Q[/latex] True
- [latex]R\rightarrow T[/latex]: [latex]R^+=\{R\}[/latex], so not implied False

Answer: [latex]PS\rightarrow T,\ P\rightarrow R,\ PS\rightarrow Q[/latex]

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text:
For a string [latex]w[/latex], we define [latex]w^R[/latex] to be the reverse of [latex]w[/latex]. For example, if [latex]w=01101[/latex] then [latex]w^R=10110[/latex].
Which of the following languages is/are context-free?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]wxw^Rx^R[/latex]: the w-pair and x-pair cross each other [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not CFL.
- [latex]ww^Rxx^R[/latex]: two even palindromes one after another [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL.
- [latex]wxw^R[/latex]: take w = [latex]\epsilon[/latex], so it is all of [latex]\{0,1\}^*[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] regular, hence CFL.
- [latex]wxx^Rw^R[/latex]: nested matching (an even palindrome) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL.

Answer: Options 2, 3 and 4

questions.subject: Operating System
options: Both P1 and P2 will print the value of x as 2.
At least of P1 and P2 will print the value of x as 4.
At least one of the threads will print the value of y as 2.
Both T1 and T2, in both the processes, will print the value of y as 1.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- P1 and P2 are separate processes with separate copies of x. In each, the two threads increment x under the lock [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] each prints x = 2.
- y is a local variable of foo, so each thread has its own y starting at 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] every thread prints y = 1.

Answer: Options 1 and 4

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
Consider a computer system with multiple shared resource types, with one instance per resource type. Each instance can be owned by only one process at a time. Owning and freeing of resources are done by holding a global lock (L). The following scheme is used to own a resource instance:
 function OWNRESOURCE(Resource R) 
    Acquire lock L // a global lock 
    if R is available then 
        Acquire R        
        Release lock L 
    else
        if R is owned by another process P then        
        Terminate P, after releasing all resources owned by P        
        Acquire R        
        Restart P        
        Release lock L        
        end if
    end if    
end function
Which of the following choice(s) about the above scheme is/are correct?
options: The scheme ensures that deadlocks will not occur
The scheme may lead to live-lock
The scheme may lead to starvation
The scheme violates the mutual exclusion property
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- A process never waits while holding resources (the owner is terminated instead), so there is no circular wait [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] no deadlock.
- Two processes can keep terminating and restarting each other without progress [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] livelock possible.
- A process may be terminated again and again and never finish [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] starvation possible.
- Each resource still has only one owner at a time [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] mutual exclusion is kept.

Answer: Options 1, 2 and 3

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text: If the numerical value of a 2-byte unsigned integer on a little endian computer is 255 more than that on a big endian computer, which of the following choices represent(s) the unsigned integer on a little endian computer?
questions.solution:
Write the little-endian value as [latex]256h+l[/latex] (high byte h, low byte l). The same bytes read big-endian give [latex]256l+h[/latex].

Difference [latex]=255(h-l)=255\Rightarrow h=l+1[/latex].
- 0x6665: h = 0x66, l = 0x65 True
- 0x0100: h = 1, l = 0 True
- 0x0001 and 0x4243 have h = l [latex]-[/latex] 1 False

Answer: 0x6665 and 0x0100

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text:
Consider a computer network using the distance vector routing algorithm in its network layer. The partial topology of the network is shown below.

The objective is to find the shortest-cost path from the router R to routers P and Q. Assume that R does not initially know the shortest routes to P and Q. Assume that R has three neighboring routers denoted as X, Y and Z. During one iteration, R measures its distance to its neighbors X, Y, and Z as 3, 2 and 5, respectively. Router R gets routing vectors from its neighbors that indicate that the distance to router P from routers X, Y and Z are 7, 6 and 5, respectively. The routing vector also indicates that the distance to router Q from routers X, Y and Z are 4, 6 and 8 respectively. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct with respect to the new routing table o R, after updation during this iteration?
options: The distance from R to P will be stored as 10
The distance from R to Q will be stored as 7
The next hop router for a packet from R to P is Y
The next hop router for a packet from R to Q is Z
questions.solution:
Cost via each neighbour = (R to neighbour) + (neighbour's distance):
- To P: X 3 + 7 = 10, Y 2 + 6 = 8, Z 5 + 5 = 10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 via Y
- To Q: X 3 + 4 = 7, Y 2 + 6 = 8, Z 5 + 8 = 13 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 7 via X

So R-P is 8 via Y (not 10), and R-Q is 7 via X (not via Z).

Answer: Distance to Q is 7; next hop to P is Y

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
Consider the following directed graph:

Which of the following is/are correct about the graph?
options: The graph does not have a topological order
A depth-first traversal starting at vertex S classifies three directed edges as back edges
The graph does not have a strongly connected component
For each pair of vertices u and v, there is a directed path from u to v
questions.solution:
Following the arrows, the graph has three directed cycles:
- around the top-middle square (between the top two rows),
- around the bottom-left square through S,
- around the bottom-right square.

- A cycle means there is no topological order [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- A DFS from S reaches every vertex, and each of these three cycles produces exactly one back edge [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 back edges [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Every graph has strongly connected components (at least single vertices) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- Not every pair is mutually reachable (e.g. nothing returns from the top-right corner) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Options 1 and 2

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.text: Which of the following regular expressions represent(s) the set of all binary numbers that are divisible by three? Assume that the string [latex]\epsilon[/latex] is divisible by three.
questions.solution:
The DFA for "value mod 3" has states 0, 1, 2 (start and final 0); reading bit b moves r to [latex](2r+b)\bmod3[/latex].
- Option 1: from state 0, "0" stays; "1" goes to 1, [latex](01^*0)^*[/latex] loops 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1, and the final "1" returns to 0 True
- Option 2: same paths written differently (11, or 10 to state 2, loop, 01 back) True
- Option 3: [latex](0^*X^*)^*=(0+X)^*[/latex] where X is the loop in option 1 True
- Option 4: cannot produce 1001 (= 9, divisible by 3) False

Answer: Options 1, 2 and 3

questions.subject: Operating System
questions.text:
Consider a three-level page table to translate a 39-bit virtual address to a physical address as shown below:

The page size is 4 KB = (1KB =[latex]2^{10}[/latex] bytes) and page table entry size at every level is 8 bytes. A process P is currently using 2 GB (1 GB =[latex]2^{30}[/latex] bytes) virtual memory which os mapped to 2 GB of physical memory. The minimum amount of memory required for the page table of P across all levels is _________ KB
questions.solution:
2 GB / 4 KB = [latex]2^{19}[/latex] pages. Each page-table page holds 4096 / 8 = 512 = [latex]2^9[/latex] entries.

For the minimum, the pages are contiguous:
- Level 3: [latex]2^{19}/2^9=1024[/latex] pages
- Level 2: 1024 entries [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 pages
- Level 1: 1 page

Total = 1027 pages [latex]\times[/latex] 4 KB = 4108 KB

Answer: 4108

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.solution:
Let F(x, y) = foo(x, y, 10). Both values go 15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]-[/latex]5.
- F([latex]-[/latex]5, [latex]-[/latex]5) = 10
- F(5, [latex]-[/latex]5) = F([latex]-[/latex]5, [latex]-[/latex]5) = 10, and similarly F([latex]-[/latex]5, 5) = 10
- F(5, 5) = F(5, [latex]-[/latex]5) + F([latex]-[/latex]5, 5) = 20
- F(15, [latex]-[/latex]5) = F(5, [latex]-[/latex]5) = 10, so F(15, 5) = F(15, [latex]-[/latex]5) + F(5, 5) = 30
- By symmetry F(5, 15) = 30

F(15, 15) = F(15, 5) + F(5, 15) = 60

Answer: 60

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text: Let S be a set of consisting of 10 elements. The number of tuples of the form (A,B) such that A and B are subsets of S, and [latex]A\subseteq B[/latex] is _______
questions.solution:
For [latex]A\subseteq B\subseteq S[/latex], each element of S is in one of 3 states: not in B, in B but not A, or in A.

[latex]3^{10}=59049[/latex]

Answer: 59049

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.text:
Consider the following augmented grammar with [latex]\{ \#, @, <, >, a, b, c \}[/latex] as the set of terminals.

[latex]\begin{array}{l} S' \rightarrow S \\ S \rightarrow S \# cS \\ S \rightarrow SS \\ S \rightarrow S @ \\ S \rightarrow < S > \\ S \rightarrow a \\ S \rightarrow b \\ S \rightarrow c \end{array}[/latex]

Let [latex]I_0 = \text{CLOSURE}(\{S' \rightarrow \bullet S\})[/latex]. The number of items in the set [latex]\text{GOTO(GOTO}(I_0 \lt ), \lt )[/latex] is ___________
questions.solution:
In [latex]I_0[/latex], [latex]S\rightarrow\bullet\lt S\gt[/latex] moves on [latex]\lt[/latex] to [latex]S\rightarrow\lt\bullet S\gt[/latex], and its closure adds all 7 S-items with the dot at the start: 1 + 7 = 8 items.

Doing GOTO on [latex]\lt[/latex] again (from [latex]S\rightarrow\bullet\lt S\gt[/latex] inside that set) gives the same set again: 8 items.

Answer: 8

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.text:
Consider a Boolean function [latex]f(w,x,y,z) [/latex] such that

[latex]\begin{array}{lll} f(w,0,0,z) & = & 1 \\ f(1,x,1,z) & =& x+z \\ f(w,1,y,z) & = & wz +y \end{array}[/latex]

The number of literals in the minimal sum-of-products expression of [latex]f [/latex] is ________
questions.solution:
From the conditions:
- x = 0, y = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f = 1 (term [latex]\bar x\bar y[/latex])
- x = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f = wz + y
- x = 0, y = 1, w = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f = z

[latex]f=\bar x\bar y+xy+wz[/latex] satisfies all three (the case x = 0, y = 1, w = 0 is not fixed). It has 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 literals, and no shorter expression fits.

Answer: 6

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.text:
Consider a pipelined processor with 5 stages, Instruction Fetch(IF), Instruction Decode(ID), Execute (EX), Memory Access (MEM), and Write Back (WB). Each stage of the pipeline, except the EX stage, takes one cycle. Assume that the ID stage merely decodes the instruction and the register read is performed in the EX stage. The EX stage takes one cycle for ADD instruction and the register read is performed in the EX stage, The EX stage takes one cycle for ADD instruction and two cycles for MUL instruction. Ignore pipeline register latencies.
Consider the following sequence of 8 instructions:

ADD, MUL, ADD, MUL, ADD, MUL, ADD, MUL

Assume that every MUL instruction is data-dependent on the ADD instruction just before it and every ADD instruction (except the first ADD) is data-dependent on the MUL instruction just before it. The speedup defined as follows.

[latex]\textit{Speedup} = \dfrac{\text{Execution time without operand forwarding}}{\text{Execution time with operand forearding}}[/latex]

The Speedup achieved in executing the given instruction sequence on the pipelined processor (rounded to 2 decimal places) is _____________
questions.solution:
Each instruction depends on the one before it. ADD uses EX for 1 cycle, MUL for 2.

With forwarding: the EX stages run back to back: 4 [latex]\times[/latex] (1 + 2) = 12 EX cycles from cycle 3 to 14, then MEM and WB [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 16 cycles.

Without forwarding: each instruction's EX (register read) waits until the previous one's WB. Each ADD/MUL pair then takes 1 + 2 EX cycles plus 2 waiting cycles (MEM, WB) each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] the last WB is at cycle 30.

Speedup = 30 / 16 = 1.875 [latex]\approx[/latex] 1.87

Answer: 1.87

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Consider a network using the pure ALOHA medium access control protocol, where each frame is of length 1,000 bits. The channel transmission rate is 1 Mbps (=[latex]10^6[/latex] bits per second). The aggregate number of transmissions across all the nodes (including new frame transmissions and retransmitted frames due to collisions) is modelled as a Poisson process with a rate of 1,000 frames per second. Throughput is defined as the average number of frames successfully transmitted per second. The throughput of the network (rounded to the nearest integer) is ______________
questions.solution:
Frame time T = 1000 / [latex]10^6[/latex] = 1 ms. Load G = 1000 frames/s [latex]\times[/latex] 1 ms = 1.

Pure ALOHA success probability = [latex]e^{-2G}=e^{-2}\approx0.135[/latex].
Throughput = 1000 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.135 [latex]\approx[/latex] 135 frames/s

Answer: 135

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.text:
In a directed acyclic graph with a source vertex s, the quality-score of a directed path is defined to be the product of the weights of the edges on the path. Further, for a vertex v other than s, the quality-score of v is defined to be the maximum among the quality-scores of all the paths from s to v. The quality-score of s is assumed to be 1.

The sum of the quality-scores of all vertices on the graph shown above is ______
questions.solution:
Go in topological order, taking the best product into each vertex:
- s = 1, c = 1, a = 9
- f = c [latex]\times[/latex] 9 = 9, b = a [latex]\times[/latex] 1 = 9
- d = max(c [latex]\times[/latex] 1, a [latex]\times[/latex] 1) = 9
- g = max(f [latex]\times[/latex] 1, d [latex]\times[/latex] 9) = 81
- e = max(d [latex]\times[/latex] 9, b [latex]\times[/latex] 1) = 81
- t = max(g [latex]\times[/latex] 1, e [latex]\times[/latex] 9) = 729

Sum = 1 + 1 + 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 + 81 + 81 + 729 = 929

Answer: 929

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: Gauri said that she can play the keyboard __________ her sister.
questions.solution:
The correct comparison phrase is "as well as" (as + adverb + as). "As better as", "as nicest as" and "as worse as" are ungrammatical.

Answer: as well as

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: A transparent square sheet shown above is folded along the dotted line. The folded sheet will look like ___________
questions.solution:
The sheet is transparent, so folding the left half over the dotted line puts the mirror image of the left drawing on top of the right half.

The rising curve on the left reflects into a falling curve that meets the existing curve at the fold, making a closed lens. The two small vertical ticks on the left reflect and join the two horizontal dashes, giving the step-shaped marks inside the lens. Only option B shows this.

Answer: B

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: If [latex]\theta[/latex] is the angle, in degrees, between the longest diagonal of the cube and any one of the edges of the cube, then, [latex]\cos \theta =[/latex]
questions.solution:
For a cube of side a, the long diagonal is (a, a, a) with length [latex]a\sqrt3[/latex]. An edge along the x-axis is (a, 0, 0).

[latex]\cos\theta=\frac{a\cdot a}{a\cdot a\sqrt3}=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\frac{1}{\sqrt3}[/latex]

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: If [latex]\left( x - \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^2 - \left( x- \dfrac{3}{2} \right) ^2 = x+2[/latex], then the value of [latex]x[/latex] is:
questions.solution:
Difference of squares: [latex](x-\tfrac12)^2-(x-\tfrac32)^2=\left[(x-\tfrac12)-(x-\tfrac32)\right]\left[(x-\tfrac12)+(x-\tfrac32)\right]=1\cdot(2x-2)[/latex]

[latex]2x-2=x+2\Rightarrow x=4[/latex]

Answer: 4

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Pen : Write :: Knife : _______

Which one of the following options maintains a similar logical relation in the above?
questions.solution:
A pen is used to write; a knife is used to cut (tool : its function).

Answer: Cut

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
Listening to music during exercise improves performance and reduces discomfort. Scientists researched whether listening to music while studying can help students learn better and the results were inconclusive. Students who needed external stimulation for studying fared worse while students who did not need any external stimulation benefited from music.

Which one of the following statements is the CORRECT inference of the above passage?
options: Listening to music has no effect on learning and a positive effect on physical exercise
Listening to music has a clear positive effect both in physical exercise and on learning
Listening to music has a clear positive effect on physical exercise. Music has a positive effect on learning only in some students
Listening to music has a clear positive effect on learning in all students. Music has a positive effect only in some students who exercise
questions.solution:
The passage says music clearly helps physical exercise, but for studying the results were mixed: it helped some students and hurt others.

Answer: Clear positive effect on exercise; positive effect on learning only in some students

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text: A jigsaw puzzle has 2 pieces. One of the pieces is shown above. Which one of the given options for the missing piece when assembled will form a rectangle? The piece can be moved, rotated or flipped to assemble with the above piece.
questions.solution:
The given piece has a straight right edge and a jagged left edge with teeth of different lengths. The missing piece, rotated to sit next to it, must have teeth that exactly fill those gaps.

Only option A has the matching pattern of widths and depths, so together they form a rectangle.

Answer: A

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.text:
